body:
The `verify` Actions job failed during server TypeScript compilation due to an undefined identifier in `getChatHistory` (`TS2552: Cannot find name 'session'`).  
This PR fixes the MongoDB execution path by resolving the missing session lookup before message mapping.

- **Root cause**
  - `server/src/db.ts` referenced `session.messages` in the MongoDB branch without defining `session`.

- **Code change**
  - Added a `chatSessions` lookup by `sessionId` in `getChatHistory`.
  - Replaced the invalid branch with a typed null-safe return.

- **Behavioral impact**
  - In-memory fallback path remains unchanged.
  - MongoDB path now correctly returns mapped chat history or an empty array when no session exists.

```ts
const session = await mongoDb.collection('chatSessions').findOne({ sessionId }) as ChatSession | null;
return session ? session.messages.map(m => ({ role: m.role, text: m.text })) : [];
```

author: codyjohnsontx
body:
Pushes a notification when CodeRabbit submits a review, so the review doesn't sit unnoticed.

Fires on `pull_request_review` (submitted), filtered to `coderabbitai[bot]`.

Two things this deliberately gets right:

- **Does not filter on review state.** CodeRabbit submits reviews as `COMMENTED`, never `CHANGES_REQUESTED` — the obvious-looking state filter would never fire once.
- **Does not key off comments.** CodeRabbit posts its summary comment ~20s after a PR opens, while the real review is still minutes out. `pull_request_review` is the only signal that tracks the actual review.

Sends to ntfy. The Slack step self-skips until `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is set, so it's a no-op until that secret exists.

PR-controlled text (the PR title) is passed via `env:` rather than inline `${{ }}` in the `run:` block, to avoid shell injection from a crafted title.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Phạm vi

- Thay luồng lưu nhiều giai đoạn bằng một Firestore transaction chứa order, order_items, order_sequences và activity_logs.
- Khi một dòng sản phẩm bị Rules từ chối hoặc ghi thất bại, toàn bộ order, sequence, items và log đều rollback.
- Tạo đơn không còn ghi parent trước rồi mới ghi item theo các batch rời.
- Sửa đơn thực hiện đồng thời: cập nhật parent, cập nhật item hiện có, thêm item mới và xóa mềm item bị bỏ.
- Chặn trước đơn vượt giới hạn 500 writes thay vì tự chia batch làm dữ liệu dở dang.
- Thêm `revision` và `last_operation_id` cho order; client phát hiện form cũ khi một phiên khác đã lưu trước.
- Mỗi item hoạt động ghi `order_revision` và `last_operation_id` để truy vết cùng operation.
- Thông báo lỗi nói rõ toàn bộ thay đổi đã được hoàn tác.

## Firestore Rules

- Dùng `existsAfter/getAfter` để order_items có thể được tạo cùng parent order trong một transaction.
- Người có `orders.edit` được thêm và bỏ dòng sản phẩm khi sửa đơn, không bắt buộc có thêm `orders.create` hoặc `orders.delete`.
- Cho phép backfill ownership fields của order_items legacy khi các giá trị khớp parent order.
- Không nới quyền xem hoặc quyền sở hữu đơn hàng.

## Test client nghiệp vụ

- Lập kế hoạch item upsert/xóa mềm.
- Chặn item thiếu ID hoặc trùng ID.
- Tính và chặn giới hạn Firestore writes.
- Kiểm tra revision và conflict giữa hai phiên.
- Kiểm tra trang Đơn hàng thực sự gọi `saveOrderAtomic` và không còn `commitWriteChunks`/parent batch cũ.

## Test Firestore Rules và rollback

- Tạo order + sequence + hai items + activity trong một transaction.
- Một item sai ownership làm rollback toàn bộ transaction tạo đơn.
- Người chỉ có `orders.edit` vẫn thêm, sửa và bỏ item trong transaction sửa đơn.
- Một item mới sai ownership làm rollback parent update, item update, item delete và activity.

## Không nằm trong PR này

- Chưa thay đổi quy tắc xóa đơn theo tiến độ in, thanh toán, hóa đơn hoặc vận chuyển; phần đó thuộc bước tiếp theo.
- PR được giữ ở trạng thái Draft và không tự động merge.

body:
First beta of the 1.30.0 line. Custom PHP extensions and packages stop belonging to a single PHP version and become one declared set applied to every image lerd builds, so a site that changes its version keeps what the developer asked for, and lerd records what each version's image actually loaded rather than promising the whole set on a tier that cannot carry it. The fixed list covers only bugs that shipped in 1.29.0 or earlier. Regressions introduced and fixed inside this cycle never reached a user, so they are folded into the feature that carried them rather than listed as fixes of their own.

The demo fixtures are deliberately untouched; they track the stable line and get refreshed when 1.30.0 ships.

author: matthewyjiang
body:
## Summary

Root-cause fix for #399. The reported reviewer died because retryable provider failures were terminal even though the SDK already classified them as retryable. Rather than adding a verification-state taxonomy around the resulting failure, this prevents transient provider failures from ending the delegated run in the first place.

- Retry retryable provider-turn failures in the SDK run loop with cancellation-aware exponential backoff. A model turn makes at most four logical provider requests total, and malformed responses share that bound.
- Reclassify `StreamFailedAfterOutput` as retryable. The broken stream cannot resume, but the unchanged turn can be sent as a fresh request.
- Emit a typed `ProviderStreamReset` before retry deltas. The TUI, attachment path, and headless reporter discard stale partial output while preserving usage. The legacy malformed-response activity remains for existing 1.0 hosts.
- Preserve failed-attempt usage as separate physical request records and avoid double-counting earlier completed steps in cumulative TUI usage.
- Mark both errored and stopped delegated tasks as incomplete and unverified when retries cannot recover them.
- Document retry bounds, billing implications, cancellation, compatibility, and host reset responsibilities.

Completed tools and committed history from earlier model turns are preserved. Permanent failures still return immediately, and cancellation interrupts active requests and backoff sleeps.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt -- --check`
- `python3 scripts/check_architecture.py`
- `cargo clippy -p rho-sdk -p rho-providers -p rho-coding-agent --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

- `cargo test -p rho-sdk --test reliability_boundedness` - 6 passed

author: balrog57
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The web admin routes lacked Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) protection. Malicious websites could forge POST requests (e.g., config updates or toggling users) by having authenticated admin users visit an attacker-controlled page.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could manipulate configuration parameters, toggle administrative access for other users, or delete alerts.
🔧 Fix: Added stateless CSRF middleware (`withCSRF`) that verifies the `Origin` or `Referer` header against the expected `r.Host` on POST requests. It allows programmatic requests with missing origin headers but strictly blocks 'null' origins to prevent bypasses. Wrapped `s.routes()` inside `s.withAuth` with the new middleware.

author: tanyudii
body:
## Summary

- Fixes Option+drag (Mac) text selection not being able to auto-scroll when the desired selection is longer than one screen.
- `XtermJs.kt` no longer forces a local xterm.js selection on Option-drag (`macOptionClickForcesSelection` removed). Instead, Option-drag now falls through to tmux's own native mouse-reporting/copy-mode, same as a plain drag -- which already auto-scrolls correctly at the pane edges (a real, pre-existing tmux feature).
- A new authenticated route `GET /api/projects/:id/sessions/:name/paste-buffer` (`src/tmux.ts`'s `readPasteBuffer`, `src/project-sessions.ts`'s `getProjectSessionPasteBuffer`) relays tmux's resulting copy-mode paste buffer back to the browser.
- `attachOptionDragCaptureListener` (new, wasmJs) detects when an Option-held drag ends (with a small movement threshold to ignore a stray Option-click) and fetches that buffer, caching it for Cmd+C to write to the real OS clipboard as a fallback whenever xterm itself has no local selection.
- A cross-session race found live during verification (an unscoped `save-buffer` read could grab a different, concurrently-active session's copy on a shared tmux server) is narrowed with a settle delay before the read.

### Design note
An earlier approach (reusing xterm.js's own local selection plus a custom edge-auto-scroll requester) was implemented, then reverted (see the `Revert "..."` commits) after a live spike proved xterm's local selection is anchored to buffer coordinates that tmux silently overwrites on repaint -- a multi-screen selection's full text is never simultaneously present in one buffer to reconstruct. The shipped approach above avoids that problem entirely by letting tmux's own already-correct mechanism do the scrolling and selecting.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test` -- 692/692 passing
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` -- clean
- [x] `./gradlew :composeApp:wasmJsTest` / `:composeApp:compileKotlinJvm` / `detekt` -- all passing
- [x] Live verification against a real headless Chromium + real tmux server + real Compose UI: Option-drag now produces a real tmux copy-mode selection (confirmed via `tmux save-buffer -`), and Cmd+C writes the correct text to the real OS clipboard (confirmed via `navigator.clipboard.readText()`); plain-drag regression confirmed (no `paste-buffer` request fires without Option held)
- [ ] Auto-scroll's exact visual behavior could not be demonstrated via synthetic Playwright pointer events (a tooling limitation, not an app-code gap -- CDP does not keep delivering motion once the simulated pointer leaves the element bounds, so tmux's own edge-timer logic never re-triggers). Recommend a quick manual check on a real Mac browser for full confidence.

Full evidence report: `docs/testing/option-drag-scroll-select.tdd.md`

author: zk-xyz
body:
Closes #45 — both robustness findings from the 0.14 ingestion fuzzing.

## extractLogos superlinear cost
Profiling localized the cost: a single `body.find('img[src*="logo"]')` inside `isInLogoCloud` costs **2.65s alone** on a 50k-element body (cheerio's context-scoped find; the same selector from the root takes 9ms). Fixes:
- Bounded manual DOM walk (2,000-node cap) replaces the subtree find — real logo clouds are small containers, so semantics are preserved
- Candidate caps: 10 per selector, 15 total, header-SVG scan capped at 20
- Per-parent verdict cache (candidates sharing a header scan it once)

Measured: **7.3s → ~180ms at 50k elements; ~360ms at 100k (linear)**. The 50k robustness test that used to time out the slowest CI runner now runs in the standard 5s timeout, per the test's own re-raise note.

Bonus fix the bounded walk exposed (pre-existing, also in the old find()): the 4-level parent walk reaches `<body>`, so a client-logo cloud **anywhere** on the page flagged the whole document as a cloud and rejected the real header logo. body/html are now excluded from the count heuristic; regression test added.

## Tool-boundary error fencing
Handler throws surfaced as raw SDK `isError` text that can quote hostile input (yaml alias-bomb messages). The registration choke point in server.ts now wraps every handler: errors return the structured envelope (`tool_execution_failed`, templated `what_happened`, recovery next_steps) with the original message only fenced + truncated via `fenceUntrusted`. Covers every tool at once — including BrandDir YAML reads reached by brand_status and the extract-web parse sites named in the issue.

Tests: 996 → 1,000 (alias-bomb e2e through a real client/server pair; 50k perf bound; candidate-cap assertion; cloud/header-logo regression).

author: dibbayajyotiroy
body:
Closes #1457

### Please check if the PR fulfills these requirements

- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] CHANGELOG.md has been updated (for bug fixes / features / docs)

### What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Bug fix — internal `$system` events were silently not replicated even when `$system` was a configured replication source.

### What was changed?

Internal `$system` writes bypassed replication because only the API handlers call
`replication_repo.notify(...)`, while the system-event writer goes straight to
`StorageEngine::begin_write`. This PR connects the internal write path to replication:

- New `ReplicationNotifier` callback type in `syslog/sink.rs`, late-bound because the
  writer is constructed before the replication repo exists (same dependency shape as the
  log-sink registration from #1467).
- `LocalSystemLogger` builds a `TransactionNotification` (same struct and fields as the
  API handlers) after each successful write and invokes the registered notifier.
  Notification errors are logged and swallowed — a replication problem never fails a
  system-event write.
- The `replications/` and `logs/` families are **excluded** (matched on `SystemEventKind`,
  not entry strings) to prevent feedback loops: replication telemetry about the `$system`
  replication would feed it new transactions indefinitely, and captured replication
  error logs would do the same exactly during failures. Usage, audit, and lifecycle
  events all notify.
- Wiring in `cfg.rs` registers the notifier once the repo is built;
  `Components::replication_repo` becomes `Arc<AsyncRwLock<...>>` to share it with the
  callback (call sites unchanged via `Deref`).

API handler notify sites, the writer's persist/console paths, and replica-role
forwarding (which already notifies via the primary's HTTP API) are untouched.

Tests: `$system`-source replication gets exactly one pending transaction per usage
event; `replications/` and `logs/` events produce none; a failing notifier does not
fail the write; writer works with no notifier registered.

### Related issues

- Closes #1457
- Builds on the unified system-event writer from #1496 (single internal write site)
- Loop-guard rationale follows the reentrancy analysis from #1467

### Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

No. Users with a `$system`-source replication configured will start receiving usage,
audit, and lifecycle records on the destination (previously nothing was replicated);
`replications/` and `logs/` entries are intentionally not replicated.

### Other information:

Mechanism is "Plan B" approved in the issue discussion: notify from the single internal
writer rather than adding a storage-level hook, which would invert the storage→replication
layering and require refactoring all seven API notify sites.

author: tallen5431
body:
Pre-existing issues surfaced by a codebase review pass. **Unrelated to the OCR feature** (that's in #12).

> **Note on branching:** `main` is currently 2 commits behind the OCR branch, so `5c5f217` and `6f63fa9` (which #12 also carries) ride along in this PR's diff too. Whichever of the two PRs merges first, the other's diff collapses to just its own changes. This branch is based on `6f63fa9` — the exact code the review examined — with **no** OCR-feature commit.

## Data-loss & robustness (verified with an isolated test harness)

**1. Corrupt `inventory.json` → cleanup wipes every asset** (`data.py`)
`_safe_read` masks a JSON parse error as `[]`, so the routine prune (runs on **Cancel** and after any delete) saw *nothing referenced* and deleted every photo, thumbnail, and attachment — while the item records still sat in the file. Added `_load_or_none()` so prune tells **corrupt** from **genuinely empty** and bails on the former. A valid empty inventory still reclaims true orphans.

**2. One bad record makes the *whole* inventory unreadable** (`data.py`)
A single hand-edited value — a string `qty` like `"2.5"`, a numeric `estimated_value`/`price_paid`, or a non-dict entry — raised inside `inventory()` and broke the entire dashboard/search/edit. Now: defensive coercion (`_safe_str`/`_safe_qty`), non-dict entries skipped, and each record wrapped so one bad row degrades to a minimal safe record instead of taking down the read.

**3. "Apply & Save" erased fields it didn't refill** (`callbacks.py`)
Applying a partial lookup (e.g. a vision match that only knows the name) to an existing item overwrote `specifications`/`estimated_value`/`dimensions`/`tags`/`product_url` with blanks. Now merges with the item's stored values — the lookup only wins for fields it actually supplies.

## Config cleanup

- **`OLLAMA_HOST` default → `http://localhost:11434`** (`vision_lookup.py`) — was a hardcoded private Tailscale IP that broke Identify out of the box and could POST item photos to another tailnet host.
- **README vision-model default → `llava:13b`** to match code + `Start.sh` (README had said `llama3.2-vision`, causing a model-not-found 404 for anyone following the docs).
- **`Start.bat` PORT default `8050` → `8001`** to match `Start.sh`/`app.py`/README.
- **Untrack `launcher.log`** (already gitignored; leaked an absolute path).

## Not included

The security findings from the same review (inline-served attachment XSS, OCR-Lab arbitrary file read, SSRF redirect bypass, exposed tracebacks) are intentionally left for a separate pass.

## Testing

`data.py` fixes verified in isolation against a temp sandbox: corrupt JSON prunes 0 files / keeps all assets; valid empty inventory still reclaims orphans; referenced files kept; `inventory()` survives a mix of bad records (string/word qty, numeric fields, non-dict entry) with every good row intact. `apply_and_save`'s merge relies on `_specs_to_text`/`_tags_to_text`, both of which map an empty list to `""` so the fallback is safe.

author: docasheesh-png
body:
## What

Auto-runs the two **existing** dependency checks — the OSV/CVE supply-chain scan (`scan_vulnerabilities`) and the strong-copyleft license classification (`check_licenses`) — at **build-end**, appending one honest advisory block to a successful build's summary. Closes the P-PIPE gap where these ran **on-demand only** (the `check_licenses` handler's own comment noted "the automatic build-end wiring is a separate slice").

## Safety / policy

- **Advisory-only — never blocks a build.** A transitive CVE or a GPL dependency in a *generated* app must not fail an otherwise-working app (the one absolute rule). The gate only surfaces findings so the agent/admin can act; it never sets `ok=false`.
- **Default-OFF behind `AGENTV3_DEPHEALTH_GATE=on`** — the same conservative canary rollout `AGENTV3_LINT_GATE` used. When unset, builds are byte-for-byte unchanged (no extra network cost).

## How (mirrors the LintGate precedent)

- **`DependencyHealthGate.ts`** — the **pure, unit-tested** verdict composition (`dependencyHealthVerdict`): clean ⇒ empty summary (nothing appended); surfaces CVE-only, copyleft-only, or both (header first); ignores a positive count paired with blank summary text (defensive).
- **`ToolDispatcher.assessDependencyHealthGate()`** — thin, best-effort, **45s-timeout-bounded** glue that reads the workspace, runs the OSV scan + license analysis, and composes the verdict. On no `package.json`, an unreachable OSV API, an invalid lockfile, or a slow scan it returns `''` (clean) — it can never fail a real build on its own trouble.
- **`AgentRunner`** — appends the advisory at **both** build-end exits (normal completion + step-cap exit), guarded by `expectsArtifacts` + a real build.

## Tests

`DependencyHealthGate.test.ts` (6 cases): clean, unavailable-scan-reads-clean, CVE-only, copyleft-only, both-with-ordering, and the defensive blank-summary case.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` → **7502 passed** (only the pre-existing `src/server/sonic/*` optional-dep load failures remain — unrelated; identical on clean `main`).
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` → **no new errors**.

## Summary

A shrink-wrapped controller registered callbacks on the document root and scroll controller, but disposed its notifiers without unregistering those callbacks. If the editor presentation unmounted while the EditorState remained alive, the next document mutation invoked the stale callback and wrote to a disposed ValueNotifier.

author: kingiust2002
body:
## What / why

Two corrections to the favicon work from #79, per direct feedback with a reference image:

**1. "Half/half" meant ONE fused shape, not two side by side**

The previous combined favicon placed the two full marks next to each other. That's not what was asked — the reference showed a single ribbon-cross where the left half carries Health's colors and the right half carries Beauty's, as one continuous shape.

Confirmed both marks share the *exact same* underlying geometry (a 50%-opacity overlay of the two, cropped to their glyphs, lines up almost perfectly) — so clipping each mark to its half and drawing both at identical scale/position seams them into one shape instead of two icons side by side.

**2. Beauty's favicon was nearly invisible at real tab size**

`/brand/beauty-mark.png` carries ~40% transparent padding around the glyph, so at an actual 16px tab icon the visible mark shrank to a faint sliver. New `beauty-mark-icon.webp` is tight-cropped to the opaque glyph (same bounding-box technique used earlier for the wordmark sizing fix). The original asset is untouched — still used as-is in the header/footer/hero lockup, where it's rendered at an explicit controlled size and isn't affected by this.

**3. Format: WebP, smaller files**

Both new icons are exported as WebP straight from the compositing canvas (Chromium's native `toDataURL('image/webp')` — no new dependency). The combined icon dropped from ~99 KB (PNG) to ~28 KB.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` ✔ · `npm test` ✔ 12/12 · `npm run build` ✔.
- Built server, curled rendered `<head>`:
  - `/` and `/login` → `gateway-mark-combined.webp` (fused shape)
  - `/beauty/tg` and `/beauty/operator/*` → `beauty-mark-icon.webp` (tight-cropped)
  - `/health/tg` → unchanged (`/logo-mark.png`, already tightly cropped, not touched)
- Visually reviewed the fused icon and the cropped Beauty icon before wiring them in.

## Scope

3 layout files (icon path/type only) + 2 new WebP assets + 1 old PNG removed. No component or page-content changes.

author: davinoishi
body:
## Problem

Two feed-quality issues reported after #96:

1. Auto-generated game pages still appear, e.g. *"Florida Panthers vs. San Jose Sharks Live Updates, Score, and Play-by-play - October 1, 2026"* — the marker list didn't cover "Live Updates"/"Play-by-play", and items ingested before a marker exists stay in the feed for 30 days.
2. Same-story articles stay on separate cards, e.g. the Jeff Kealty hire (*"Assistant GM Jeff Kealty departs Predators…"* / *"Sharks Hire Jeff Kealty as Assistant General Manager"* / *"Sharks Hire New Assistant GM - Yahoo Sports"*).

## Root causes found

- The event keyword classifier matched substrings: `'assist'` hit "**Assist**ant" (→ game) and `'lines'` hit "Pred**lines**" (→ lineup), producing event types that fail the clustering compatibility gate.
- "GM" was dropped by the short-token filter and never equated with "General Manager".
- "Jeff Kealty" isn't in the entity table (staff aren't roster-synced), disabling the entity path entirely, and the title gates (6 shared tokens, 0.90 containment) are unreachable for short headlines.
- Titles were only compared against a cluster's **first** headline, so merge success depended on arrival order.

## Changes

**Ingest filter**
- Add `live updates`, `play-by-play`, `play by play` markers.
- New daily `cleanup_scoreboard_stubs` task retroactively deletes already-ingested stubs and their emptied clusters, so the feed self-heals whenever the marker list grows.

**Clustering / dedup**
- Word-boundary keyword matching in the event classifier (with explicit inflected forms); `hire` added to signing keywords; `signing↔other` marked event-compatible.
- Canonicalize "general manager" → "gm"; keep `gm` through the short-token filter.
- New shared-person-name path: capitalized name bigrams (excluding team/city/headline vocabulary) merge personnel stories whose subject isn't a known entity, gated on ≥4 shared title tokens, ≥0.40 title Jaccard, and event compatibility (new settings `title_name_min_shared_tokens`, `title_name_jaccard_threshold`).
- Step 2.5 compares against **every** title in a candidate cluster, not just the first variant's headline.
- Step 3 adds a suffix-stripped headline-to-headline token comparison so short rewrites ("Sharks Hire New Assistant GM - Yahoo Sports") aren't diluted by the cluster's full token pool.

**Latent purge bug (found while testing)**
- `purge_old_items` crashed with `IntegrityError` for any enriched raw_item: ORM-level delete NULLs the not-null `story_variants.raw_item_id` FK instead of using the DB cascade. Both purge and the new cleanup now bulk-delete; regression test included.

## Verification

- Full suite passes in both CI modes: 215 passed (Postgres), 182 passed / 33 skipped (SQLite).
- End-to-end check with the reported titles: both live-update pages are now rejected at ingest; the three Kealty articles were simulated in all six arrival orders — the two name-bearing articles merge in **6/6** orders and all three merge in 3/6 (previously 0/6 merged anything). The remaining split (nameless Yahoo headline vs an `other`-classified cluster) is score-gated; real articles carry descriptions and LLM summaries that add signal beyond bare titles.

author: pratiks360
body:
## Summary
- Scanning and waking/updating now run in a foreground service (`ScanService`) with a persistent notification, instead of a plain background thread tied to the Activity. Android can kill a backgrounded process at any time (more aggressively on some OEMs), which was silently aborting scans whenever the app was minimised.
- The tracked list is now saved to disk after every single app processed, not just once at the end of a scan - a mid-scan process kill now loses at most one app's progress instead of the whole scan (root cause of the list appearing empty after switching away mid-scan).
- Play Store no longer exposes a labeled "version" field on its public listing page. The only version-shaped tokens left are per-review "app version" tags in the reviews carousel, mixed with unrelated short numeric tags from the same nested review data (rating breakdowns, vote-weight tags). Verified live against several real listing pages that picking the wrong one was the source of every reported mismatch, e.g. a 2-segment noise tag like "7.1" or "8.0" numerically outranking the real, longer version, or colliding by coincidence with an app whose own version is also short.
- Candidates must now match both the **segment count** and the **leading (major) segment** of the installed version before being considered - a real update essentially never changes how many version parts there are or jumps the major version to something unrelated. If nothing satisfies both, the fetch now returns "unknown" instead of guessing from the single highest token on the page.
- Every current-vs-latest comparison (outdated flag, list coloring, per-row Update button, Update All filtering) now requires the scraped version be numerically *newer*, not just *different* - a wrong or stale scraped value can no longer be flagged as an available update.
- The tracked list now only displays outdated (or still-being-checked) apps; apps that are asleep but already current aren't actionable, so they're hidden. The status line still reports the true total tracked count.

## Reviewer notes
- Can't run a full Gradle build in this sandbox (AGP requires Gradle 9.4.1, and the CDN redirect used to download it is blocked at the TLS layer here) - reviewed the new/changed Java by hand against the real Android APIs and validated the version-picking logic against live-fetched Play Store pages, but please build and test on-device.
- New permissions: `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` (requested at runtime on API 33+); new `androidx.core:core` dependency for `NotificationCompat`/`ContextCompat`.
- The version heuristic favors correctness over completeness: apps that made a genuine major-version jump while asleep for a long time may now show "unknown" instead of a guessed number. This trade-off was made deliberately after live testing showed guessed numbers were frequently wrong/misleading.

## Test plan
- [ ] Build and install on-device; confirm a scan started and then minimised keeps running (notification stays visible) instead of stopping.
- [ ] Confirm the app list is no longer empty after switching away mid-scan and back.
- [ ] Confirm "Latest" versions look plausible and current==latest apps drop out of the list once resolved.
- [ ] Confirm Update / Update All still wake apps and open Play Store's updates screen as before.

body:
## Summary
Fix heap-use-after-free in `handleClientsBlockedOnKey()` when serving blocked clients.

Root cause: a plain `listIter` caches the successor `listNode*`, while the serve path can synchronously `freeClient()` another client still blocked on the same key (module reply + `CLIENT KILL`, and also `unblockClientOnKey` → `processCommand` → `evictClients()` with `maxmemory-clients`).

Fix: snapshot stable client IDs before serving, then re-resolve each id from the live `blocking_keys` waiter list (`getClientFromBlockingKeysList`) and skip clients that were freed/unlinked mid-loop. One path covers both linked clients and `RM_Call` fake/temp clients (absent from `clients_index`).

Reported by @gff-cw in #4198.

## Affected versions / backport
The original report mentioned 9.1.0, but the vulnerable pattern appears older than 9.1. Happy to help with backports to active release branches if desired.

- [x] ASan repro: module reply callback that `CLIENT KILL`s a successor blocked client

- [x] `./runtest --single unit/moduleapi/async_rm_call`
- [x] `./runtest --single unit/client-eviction --only '/BLPOP \+ maxmemory-clients'`

Fixes #4198

author: marcusbellamyshaw-cell
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a save race reported as a follow-up comment on closed issue #1158. `EmDashRuntime.handleContentUpdate`'s draft-revision path does read-existing → merge → create-revision → flip-pointer with no wrapping transaction (D1 has no multi-statement transactions) and an unconditional pointer-flip `UPDATE`. Two concurrent saves (autosave racing an explicit save, or two explicit saves) that both read `draft_revision_id: null` before either writes both create a new revision and race to flip the pointer — whichever `UPDATE` lands last wins regardless of which read the fresher data, so the other save's edit is silently discarded even though the API reports success. This matches the DCathal repro in the #1158 thread (two revisions created in the same second, the stale one becomes `draft_revision_id`).

Note: the *original* #1158 report (TipTap `editor.view.dispatch` bypassing `onUpdate`) was already fixed by #1119 and is unaffected here — this addresses the separate, still-reproducing save race described in the newest comment on that thread (0.28.1/0.29.0).

Fix: the pointer-flip `UPDATE` is now a compare-and-set keyed on the `draft_revision_id` read at the start of the attempt (`COALESCE(draft_revision_id, '') = <value read>`, NULL-safe across SQLite/D1 and Postgres). If the CAS fails, the losing save retries — re-reading the now-current draft, re-merging its own edit on top, and retrying the create+CAS — instead of silently overwriting. Bounded to 3 attempts. The orphaned revision row from a lost race is harmless; `pruneOldRevisions` sweeps it up on a later successful save since it's keyed by `entry_id`, not by pointer.

Known residual, out of scope for this PR: the autosave-only "update existing draft revision in place" path (`skipRevision` when a draft already exists) still isn't CAS-guarded — two concurrent autosaves (no explicit save involved) can still last-write-wins on that single row's `data` column. Closing that fully would need a version column on `revisions`, which felt like more surface than this fix needs; flagging in case a maintainer disagrees.

Closes (comment thread on) #1158

author: vietanhdev
body:
Likely the most common reason fan control doesn't work — and the app currently sends users somewhere that can't possibly fix it.

## The problem

`thinkpad_acpi`'s `fan_set_level()` opens with:

```c
if (!fan_control_allowed) return -EPERM;
```

and the parameter is `module_param_named(fan_control, fan_control_allowed, bool, 0444)`. **Mode `0444` means it isn't writable at runtime** — it needs a `modprobe.d` entry plus a module reload or reboot.

Nothing in this repo ever set it. So on a stock ThinkPad every write fails with EPERM, and `set_fan_speed` reported *"Permission denied. Click 'Grant Permissions'"* — advice that can never work, because the obstacle is the kernel module, not polkit. Users would grant permissions, see no change, and reasonably conclude the app is broken.

## Detection

Read-only, no privileges needed. The driver zeroes `fan_control_commands` when the parameter is off, and `fan_read()` only emits the `commands:` lines when it's set — so their absence means writes will fail.

Verified against a machine with `fan_control=1` set: three `commands:` lines present.

## Added

- **`get_fan_capability()`** → `Ready` / `NeedsModuleParam` / `NoThinkpadFan`, with a message naming the real obstacle. Three-state on purpose: *"couldn't check"* must never render as *"not supported"*.
- **`enable_fan_control()`** → writes the `modprobe.d` entry and attempts a reload, then **re-probes rather than assuming it worked**. A busy module can't be reloaded, so that case reports "reboot to activate" instead of claiming success.
- `set_fan_speed` checks this first and returns the accurate message.

Uses the existing `create_secure_temp_script()` rather than adding another predictable-`/tmp` pkexec site.

## Tests

`detects_fan_control_disabled_by_absent_commands_lines`, `detects_fan_control_enabled_by_commands_lines`, and a tolerance test ensuring a value that merely *mentions* "commands:" doesn't count.

Suite: 37 → 40.

author: e16tae
body:
## Summary

ADR-0044+0045 macro `macro-plan-20260718T111223Z-ccc3c7`, subtask **S5-att-stop-pin** (engineer workflow `compose-20260719T082151Z-c6b11b`). The attention plugin's Claude `Stop` sensor becomes the ADR-0044 §2 capture firing point:

- **Three-stage Stop handler** (a deeper refactor than "spawn first" — the old single body's early returns would have skipped capture): shared evidence collection → **capture spawn** in its own failure boundary → notification in its own boundary. Notification short-circuits (missing `session_id`/`prompt_id`, no terminal event, notify errors) never skip capture; capture failure (or a hung publisher killed at its slot) never skips notification; exit 0 always.
- **Fixed argv**: `--repo-root` (payload-cwd resolution; capture additionally *requires* a payload-carried cwd), `--host claude`, clamped optional `--session-id`, `--workflow-evidence fresh` only when the same projection read that powers enrichment observed a fresh terminal projection.
- **Separate publisher capability floor** `PUBLISH_SESSION_MIN_RUNTIME_VERSION = '0.82.0'` (the S4a-recorded first released runtime shipping `publish-session`; the two gates never share a constant with notify's `0.71.0`), declared in **`data/runtime-floors.json`** byte-for-byte with the spawn gate (§13 producer rule, test-pinned). Below-floor ⇒ silent capture skip with notifications intact; **capability drift** (floor passes, `scripts/context.mjs` absent) ⇒ equally silent no-op.
- **Stop hot-path budget as contract values**: `EMIT_SLOT_MS=12s`, `TERMINAL_BATCH_DEADLINE_MS=24s` (two full slots), `PUBLISH_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS=12s`, `STOP_HOT_PATH_BUDGET_MS=36s` — test-pinned, README-documented.
- **README + both plugin manifests + root Claude catalog** updated from "stdout-silent notification-only sensors" to the ADR-0044 §2 amendment (host-lifecycle sensors feeding allowlisted runtime-owned executors).

## Codex Review ensemble (verdict=modify) — all 4 MAJOR adopted

1. **GIT_\* env scrub on BOTH spawn seams** — inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` would misdirect the publisher's `git -C` probes to another repo (notify seam scrubbed too so the seams never diverge).
2. **Payload-cwd capture gate** — malformed/empty stdin degrades to `{}` and the process-cwd fallback exists only for the pre-ADR-0044 notification path; an automatic write keyed off it could replace a valid session generation with an anonymous slot.
3. **Projection/marker reads regular-file-gated** — a repo-controlled FIFO at a projection path blocked the whole sensor outside every timeout (budget was arithmetic, not a ceiling); now routed through the shared `readRegularFileSync` (isFile + 1 MiB cap).
4. **Leading-hyphen session ids omitted** — the released 0.82.0 argv parser (`requireValue`) rejects option-shaped values, silently losing the whole capture; omitting preserves the structural capture.

MINOR adopted: catalog wording; **real-0.82.0-publisher integration tests** (gate-on slot/entry round-trip via repo-config opt-in, short-circuit republish), real-timeout E2E, FIFO E2E. MINOR accepted-as-documented: the 12s capture slot's thin headroom over 4 sequential ~3s git probes — a killed publisher may hold `.lock` until the 60s stale-age (captures suppressed at most that window; notifications unaffected).

## Test plan

- attention suite 87/87 (gate 5 added: floor-declaration parity, budget pins, spawn unit suite, 0.82.0-stub E2E, real-publisher integration)
- full `npm test` 5000 tests: 4998 pass / 0 fail / 2 pre-existing skips; `lint:plugin-shape`, `validate:marketplace`, `validate:artifacts` green
- **11 mutations all caught** (order swap, capture removal, floor collapse, drift-guard removal, declaration drift, evidence-relay removal, timeout removal + GIT-scrub disable, hyphen-guard removal, cwd-gate removal, regular-file-gate bypass); restorations byte-verified against cp backups

author: nattapatkatun-cmd
body:
## Summary
- Remove `"orientation": "portrait"` from `manifest.json` — when launched as a standalone PWA on a foldable's outer/cover display (wide, non-standard aspect ratio, e.g. Oppo Find N6), Android was pinning a phone-shaped portrait window to a corner of the screen and leaving the rest blank ("เอียงซ้าย" — content stuck to the left).
- Lock viewport zoom in `index.html` (`maximum-scale=1.0, minimum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no`) so a leftover pinch-zoom level can't carry over into a fresh standalone launch and make the app appear zoomed in/cropped.
- Bump the service worker cache (`kindee-v9` → `kindee-v10`) so the updated manifest/HTML aren't served stale.

Regular phones and the unfolded inner screen were unaffected since their aspect ratio already matches a locked portrait window; only the foldable's wide cover display exposed the issue.

## Test plan
- [ ] Remove the existing "Add to Home Screen" icon and reinstall it so the updated manifest is picked up
- [ ] Open the reinstalled icon while the device is folded (outer/cover screen) and confirm the app fills the screen with no blank margin and no zoom/cropping
- [ ] Open the app on the unfolded inner screen and on a regular phone to confirm no regression

author: mdsaifulislammsi
body:
## Incident

Production desktop sign-in returned TRAFFIC_ROUTE_TIMEOUT from POST /api/auth/mfa/passkey/login/verify after the generic 7-second AUTH_LOGIN budget. Instance CPU and capacity were healthy, so this was a request-deadline race rather than route overload.

## Fix

- classify exact passkey/WebAuthn endpoints under the intended AUTH_WEBAUTHN policy
- add a precise post-admission commit boundary before CSRF, one-time proofs, session rotation, desktop assurance redemption, MFA, OTP, and password-reset mutations
- refuse controller mutations after a request timeout or disconnect wins
- expose the global timeout marker and stop protected middleware before downstream handlers after timeout
- avoid a second response from error middleware after headers are committed
- preserve all abuse limiters before the commit boundary

## Verification

- 36 focused timeout/policy/MFA/OTP regression tests
- 86 browser-session, socket, desktop handoff, CSRF, rate-limit, and AuthShield tests
- 45 full auth-route integration tests
- 39 full OTP route integration tests
- 73 frontend AuthContext, SocketContext, and auth API refresh tests
- production frontend build
- repository secret scan across 2,439 files
- independent diff review: no P0/P1 findings

The local staging-credential preflight was not applicable in this shell because staging release environment variables were intentionally absent. Deployment must remain workflow-gated after merge.

author: thomhurst
body:
Closes #2309.

## What

Introduces first-class asynchronous serde support for serializers/deserializers that must perform per-message I/O — the issue's driving use case is a Confluent.Kafka migration whose custom encryption/compression serde stack fetches short-lived keys:

- **New interfaces** (`Dekaf.Serialization`): `IAsyncSerializer<T>` (writes into an `IBufferWriter<byte>`), `IAsyncDeserializer<T>`, and combined `IAsyncSerde<T>`. Both carry a `CancellationToken` and document the pooled-memory validity contract (inputs/outputs only valid until the returned task completes).
- **Builder API**: overloads of the existing methods — `WithKeySerializer(IAsyncSerializer<TKey>)`, `WithValueSerializer(IAsyncSerializer<TValue>)`, `WithKeyDeserializer(IAsyncDeserializer<TKey>)`, `WithValueDeserializer(IAsyncDeserializer<TValue>)` — mirroring Confluent's same-name sync/async overload pattern for easy migration. Configuring both sync and async for the same component fails at `Build()`.
- **Producer**: when an async serializer is configured, every produce entry point (`ProduceAsync` ×3 incl. transactions/retry, `ProduceAllAsync` ×2, `FireAsync` ×3) diverts to a dedicated async path *before* any synchronous serialize: serialize into a pooled heap-safe buffer writer (`AsyncSerializationBufferWriter`, thread-cached, backed by `ProducerDataPool.BytePool`), then enqueue via the existing `EnqueueAppend` pooled-memory worker path (same machinery as the metadata-miss slow path). Fire-and-forget observes delivery in the background: errors reach the delivery handler or the FnF log, and the pooled completion source is always harvested. Mixed configurations (sync key + async value) use the existing thread-local sync pooled path for the sync component.
- **Consumer**: when an async deserializer is configured, `ConsumeAsync` and `ConsumeOneAsync` await deserialization per record before constructing the `ConsumeResult` (new internal pre-deserialized ctor; record fields are hoisted before the await because they reference pooled batch storage). `ConsumeBatchAsync` throws `NotSupportedException` (batch records are deserialized during synchronous iteration) with guidance to use `ConsumeAsync`/`ConsumeOneAsync`. Null semantics mirror the eager path exactly (null key skips the deserializer; null value invokes it with empty data + `IsNull = true`).
- Defense in depth: with an async serde configured, the sync serializer/deserializer slot holds a throwing placeholder, so any path that bypassed the async routing fails loudly instead of producing garbage.
- Docs: new "Async Serializers (IAsyncSerde)" section in `docs/serialization/custom.md`.

## Hot-path impact (Rule 1 / Rule 8)

The synchronous fast path is untouched except for **one readonly-bool branch per produce/consume entry point** (`_hasAsyncSerializers` / `_hasAsyncDeserializers`), the same shape and placement as the existing `_keyPreparer is not null` check. In `ConsumeAsync` the flag is hoisted once per stream like `hasInterceptors`. No allocations, no virtual dispatch, no async machinery added to the sync path.

Before/after `[MemoryDiagnoser]` numbers (broker-free, `--inProcess`, same machine):

`ProducerFireHotPathBenchmarks.FireBatch` (broker-free sync fire fast path — covers the exact entry point that gained the routing branch; sync serializers configured, so the branch is the only delta). Both runs `--inProcess` on the same machine (out-of-process BDN boilerplate build fails locally — pre-existing toolchain issue):

| Config | main (baseline) | this PR | Allocated |
|---|---|---|---|
| MessageSize=1000, DeliveryLatencyTargetMs=0 | 377.2 ns (median 370.1) | 334.2 ns (median 332.5) | 0 B → 0 B |
| MessageSize=1000, DeliveryLatencyTargetMs=10 | 888.3 ns (median 934.4) | 900.3 ns (median 930.7) | 0 B → 0 B |

Medians agree within ~1% (target-10) and the target-0 delta favors the candidate — parity within run-to-run noise, and the Allocated column stays `0 B`. The consumer-side `ConsumeOneBufferedFastPathBenchmarks` could not produce usable numbers locally (the in-process toolchain forces InvocationCount=1, yielding μs-scale noise); the consumer sync-path delta is one readonly-bool added to the existing `ConsumeOneAsync` fast-path condition plus a hoisted local in the `ConsumeAsync` loop — the same shape as the existing `hasInterceptors` hoist.

## Semantics notes

- With async serializers, `FireAsync`'s returned `ValueTask` still completes at append/enqueue (not delivery). BufferMemory backpressure surfaces via the background delivery observer (handler/log) rather than synchronously — same model the `ProduceAsync` metadata-miss slow path already uses.
- `IAsyncSerializerPreparer<T>` is unchanged and remains the right tool for one-time async setup (Schema Registry); the new interfaces are for genuinely per-message async work.

## Not in scope (follow-ups)

- `ConsumeBatchAsync` async-deserialization support (would need per-batch eager async materialization).
- ShareConsumer async serdes (builder intentionally has no async overloads yet).
- A Confluent-style `AsSyncOverAsync()` bridge wrapper.
- SchemaRegistry serializers implementing `IAsyncSerializer` natively.

## /simplify pass (applied)

Four parallel review agents (reuse / simplification / efficiency / altitude) ran on the diff; applied: the async path now reuses `ProduceInternalAsync` directly (per-component async branch at its serialize lines — the parallel ~90-line method was deleted), a shared `AwaitProduceCompletionAsync` tail replaces three copies of the instrumented-await ladder (adopted by `ProduceAsyncSlow` too), fire-and-forget appends via the accumulator's existing span/callback machinery instead of a per-message observer task + completion source, `ProduceInternalAsync` now checks the thread-local topic cache first (matters when every async-serde message routes through it), the new `ConsumeResult` ctor chains to the master ctor instead of hand-assigning 14 fields, the buffer writer got the `Array.MaxLength` growth clamp (drift from `DetachableBufferWriter`) and warm-buffer retention on reset, and the placeholder invariant is now enforced in the client constructors (not just the builder). Skipped deliberately: the `ConsumeOne` async sibling stays a documented mirror of the sync method (no zero-hot-path-cost sharing found), the `ProducerMessage` wrapper allocation in the arg-based async diverts (removing it would re-duplicate the produce path to save ~72 B on an already-allocating opt-in path), and a builder slot-union redesign (behavior-changing; the Build-time conflict throw covers it).

## Testing

- Unit (12 tests, all green): builder conflict validation ×4, async-serde build, `ConsumeBatchAsync` guard, placeholder throws ×2, `AsyncSerializationBufferWriter` round-trip/empty/growth/advance-past-end.
- Integration (6 tests, all green vs real Kafka via Testcontainers): XOR "encryption" serde with a forced async hop — `ProduceAsync`+`ConsumeAsync` round-trip (key+value, call-count-verified), `ConsumeOneAsync` (mixed sync/async), `ProduceAllAsync` ×50, `FireAsync`, `FireAsync` with delivery handler, null-value tombstone round-trip.
- Full solution builds clean (net10.0 + netstandard2.0), 0 warnings.
- Full unit suite run 6× total post-change: one run had a single failure whose identity was lost before the report was captured (overwritten by the subsequent run); 5 consecutive full-suite runs after it were 5873/5873 green, including 4 back-to-back capture runs that produced no failure to attribute. Flagging per the flaky-test rule rather than hiding it — if CI reproduces it, the name will pin it down.

To provide a convenient way to view and manage booking submissions and receive automated email alerts directly, the online booking page (`public/book.html`) was integrated with Netlify Forms.

author: joshtol
body:
This repository is **public**, and confidential/internal planning docs reached `main` more than once this month. This adds a guard that turns a mistaken commit into a hard failure instead of a silent leak. It is **build-step 1 of the External Docs Standard** (the rest of that skill is handed off separately).

## What it does
A file is blocked if it carries a **classification banner** (`CLASSIFICATION: CONFIDENTIAL` / `INTERNAL`, optionally in an HTML comment) **or** a **filename token** (`.confidential.` / `.internal.`). Loose words in prose do not trip it.

- **`scripts/check-classification.mjs`** — no-deps scanner. Scans tracked files (CI) or staged files (`--staged`, hook). Self-exempts its own docs.
- **`.githooks/pre-commit`** + `package.json` `prepare` (auto-points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`) + a `check:classification` script — local fast-fail before a commit is even created.
- **`.github/workflows/classification-guard.yml`** — the un-bypassable CI backstop (its own workflow, so it is not serialized behind `ci.yml`'s shared-test-db concurrency).
- **`.gitignore`** token patterns so `git add .` will not sweep marked files in.
- **`.gitattributes`** pins the hook to LF; **`docs/classification-guard.md`** documents the convention.

## Verified
Clean on the current tree (1435 files, no false positives), and it catches a planted banner doc plus a token-named file. This PR's own `classification-guard` check exercises it live.

## One-time admin step (you)
Add **`classification-guard`** as a **required status check** on the `main` branch protection rules. Until then the CI job is visible but advisory; the required-check setting is what turns a red X into an actual merge block.

author: kumar-gaurav-1
body:
🎯 **What:** The previous code used an insecure, hardcoded `NSAppleScript` execution as a fallback to lock the macOS screen.
⚠️ **Risk:** Executing automated AppleScripts that interface with System Events is an insecure pattern. It requires broad accessibility permissions and exposes a surface for potentially executing arbitrary automated interactions if the input or script string were ever maliciously modified or intercepted. It is generally a security anti-pattern for a simple task like locking a screen.
🛡️ **Solution:** Removed the `NSAppleScript` execution entirely. The lock function has been updated to dynamically load and call the `SACLockScreenImmediate` function from the private macOS `login.framework` via `dlopen`/`dlsym`. This is a standard, robust, and native method used in macOS utilities for locking screens safely without triggering AppleScript prompts. If this fails, it retains the safe `/usr/bin/pmset displaysleepnow` fallback mechanism. Re-structured logging dynamically interpolated error strings to include `privacy: .public` as per best practices.

author: kylenaluan
body:
## Intent Native Phase 6b/6c of the color-grade AE plugin: add Curves and Wheels to the in-effect editor. 6b Curves is UI-only (the C++ engine already evaluated the tone/RGB curves) - an interactive ImGui curve widget writing recipe-backed curve state. 6c Wheels adds a NEW DaVinci Lift/Gamma/Gain engine stage (per-channel printer-lights out=clamp01((gain*x+lift*(1-x))^(1/gamma)), neutral=exact identity), written TS-oracle-first then ported bit-exact to the C++ Engine.h and gated by native:core-parity; plus an Adobe-style 3-way secondary mode that adds no new engine math (additive user band tints + LGG-master luminance). Deliberate decisions: (1) editor look-state lives in DEDICATED user recipe fields (userToneCurve/userChannelR-G-B, userShadowTint/Mid/High, lift/gamma/gain, wheelsMode) separate from the theme-seeded overrides, composed onto the popup theme by one shared core helper cg::core::applyEditorOverrides used by BOTH the effect's BakeAutoLut render path AND the pure themeFromRecipe - this was the fix for an AE round-1 blocker where BakeAutoLut built the theme from the Theme popup and never read the recipe's curve/wheel edits, so they never reached the baked LUT; the dedicated-fields design is old-project-safe (empty user fields bake the exact theme) and theme-switch-safe (no stale override). (2) RECIPE_VERSION bumped 3->4 with an append-only layout and a v3->v4 migration arm (alongside v2->v4) so old grades survive; v4 was restructured while still unshipped. (3) Curve point-manipulation is pure in EditorBridge.h with curveClampPoint enforcing x-ascending + y-non-decreasing (the engine's forceMonotoneY invariant) so the drawn/baked PCHIP always passes through the control dots - fix for a round-1 far-drag detach bug. (4) Wheels draw a color ring (LggRingColor primary-aligned HSV; TintRingColor via core LAB->Rec.709) - the 3-way ring is intentionally more muted because it shows real gamut-limited LAB tints vs the LGG abstract hue wheel. No new keyframeable PF params (curves/wheels are recipe-only by design); the whole-blob RecipeHash already busts the preview cache. Headless gates (native:core-parity incl new recipeeditor render-path guard and gradelgg/recipelgg; native:editor-test incl far-drag monotone; preview/analysis/scopes; TS unit tests) all pass and all 4 native configs (Debug/Release x CPU/GPU) build clean. NOTE: the native C++ build, the editor ImGui UI, and AEGP runtime are captain-verified in After Effects (two AE rounds passed) and are deliberately NOT wired into CI - the C++/parity harnesses need a local g++/clang and are gated locally, not in CI. ## What Changed - Added an interactive ImGui **Curves** tab (master + per-channel R/G/B) to the native editor, with pure point-manipulation helpers in `EditorBridge.h` (`curveClampPoint` enforces x-ascending + y-non-decreasing so the drawn/baked PCHIP always passes through the control dots); the engine already evaluated these curves, so 6b is UI-only. - Added a **Wheels** tab with a new DaVinci Lift/Gamma/Gain engine stage (`out=clamp01((gain*x+lift*(1-x))^(1/gamma))`, neutral = exact identity) written TS-oracle-first in `engine.ts` then ported bit-exact into `Engine.h`, plus an Adobe-style 3-way secondary mode (additive user band tints + LGG-master luminance, no new engine math); the composed per-channel gamma is clamped to a positive floor before inversion. - Routed all editor look-state through dedicated user recipe fields (`userToneCurve`/`userChannelR-G-B`, `userShadowTint/Mid/High`, `lift/gamma/gain`, `wheelsMode`) composed onto the popup theme by one shared `cg::core::applyEditorOverrides` used by both the effect's `BakeAutoLut` render path and pure `themeFromRecipe`; bumped `RECIPE_VERSION` 3→4 with an append-only layout and v2/v3→v4 migration so old grades still bake. Gated by `native:core-parity` (grade 3.3e-7, recipe 6e-8) and `native:editor-test`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The engine port is bit-exact and parity-gated, the round-1 gamma fix is correctly applied in both engines, and migration is append-only and self-tested; the one issue is a bounded, edit-then-theme-switch curve-leak that deviates from a stated design goal but is not a crash or corruption risk. ## Testing `Baseline TS suite and all five native headless gates (core-parity, editor, preview, analysis, scopes) pass with g++ locally. On top of pass/fail I produced product-level evidence: a transcript applying the built transform to real gray-ramp pixels that shows the new DaVinci LGG stage doing exactly what the intent describes - neutral=byte-exact identity, lift raises shadows with white pinned, gain pulls the white point with black pinned, gamma bends midtones with endpoints anchored, per-channel gain tints highlights, and the final review commit's 1e-3 gamma floor keeping output bounded/finite for gamma<=0. The ImGui editor widgets and AEGP round-trip are native-Windows/AE-only and captain-verified (out of this Linux harness), so no editor screenshot is possible; the color math those widgets drive is demonstrated directly on pixels.`
Evidence: DaVinci LGG engine stage - real-pixel apply transcript 1) NEUTRAL LGG = exact identity mid in(0.5,0.5,0.5) -> out(0.5000,0.5000,0.5000) IDENTITY 2) LIFT +0.15: shadow 0.1->0.2350, high 0.9->0.9150 (white pinned) 3) GAIN 0.8: high 0.9->0.7200 (black pinned) 4) GAMMA 1.6: mid 0.5->0.6484 (endpoints anchored) 5) warm gain [1.1,1.0,0.9]: high -> 0.99,0.90,0.81 (R>B) 6) gamma-floor clamp: gamma=0 & -0.5 mid 0.5 -> 0.0000 bounded&finite=YES ```text DaVinci Lift/Gamma/Gain engine stage - real-pixel apply through the baked transform formula: out = clamp01((gain*x + lift*(1-x))^(1/gamma)) [None/Manual theme] 1) NEUTRAL LGG = exact identity (byte-for-byte passthrough) shadow in(0.1, 0.1, 0.1) -> out(0.1000, 0.1000, 0.1000) IDENTITY mid in(0.5, 0.5, 0.5) -> out(0.5000, 0.5000, 0.5000) IDENTITY high in(0.9, 0.9, 0.9) -> out(0.9000, 0.9000, 0.9000) IDENTITY 2) LIFT +0.15 (raises shadows, white pinned) shadow -> 0.2350, 0.2350, 0.2350 mid -> 0.5750, 0.5750, 0.5750 high -> 0.9150, 0.9150, 0.9150 3) GAIN 0.8 (pulls highlights/white-point down, black pinned) shadow -> 0.0800, 0.0800, 0.0800 mid -> 0.4000, 0.4000, 0.4000 high -> 0.7200, 0.7200, 0.7200 4) GAMMA 1.6 (brightens midtones, both endpoints anchored) shadow -> 0.2371, 0.2371, 0.2371 mid -> 0.6484, 0.6484, 0.6484 high -> 0.9363, 0.9363, 0.9363 5) Per-channel warm-highlight gain [R1.1, G1.0, B0.9] (R raised above B) shadow -> 0.1100, 0.1000, 0.0900 mid -> 0.5500, 0.5000, 0.4500 high -> 0.9900, 0.9000, 0.8100 6) GAMMA-FLOOR clamp fix (final review commit caabed3): a wheel can compose gamma<=0; without the 1e-3 floor, 1/gamma flips sign and blows the channel to white/NaN. gamma=0: mid 0.5 -> 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000 bounded&finite=YES gamma=-0.5: mid 0.5 -> 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000 bounded&finite=YES ```

✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `native/ColorGradeFX/editor/EditorWindow.cpp:1044` - The Gamma wheel can produce a non-positive per-channel gamma: the master slider bottoms out at 0.2 (EditorWindow.cpp:1044) and the color disc adds a zero-sum per-channel offset up to ±0.60 (colorK), so a channel gamma can reach ~-0.4. The engine then computes 1/gamma (Engine.h:532) with no positivity guard, violating LiftGammaGain's documented 'gamma Must be > 0' invariant. author: zigiella
body:
## Qué

Añade la **regla operativa** que faltaba en §III y un antipatrón en §V: la coordinadora **solo spawnea a sus subagentes**; a un **cliente separado** lo despierta la dirección (latido) o su reloj, y para paralelizar su trabajo se **encola** en `next.md`, no se spawnea.

## Por qué (el hueco)

El Charter ya define las dos topologías, pero solo en génesis (§III): *subagente* comparte tecnología con la coordinadora, *cliente separado* es multi-tecnología. La distinción es un atributo de arranque; **no había guardarraíl en tiempo de ejecución** que impidiera a la coordinadora colapsar un cliente separado en subagente. La coordinadora puede saber la topología y aun así errar, porque la consecuencia no estaba nombrada como fallo.

Spawnear un cliente separado como subagente lo colapsa sobre el modelo de la coordinadora y **anula la diversidad multi-modelo que es su razón de ser** — la misma diversidad que el Art. 5 exige al auditor cross-tec. Es un fallo de tipo, no de resultado: el trabajo puede salir correcto y el diseño quedar roto.

## Caso real (motivación)

**Savia, 2026-07-19.** La dirección pidió «prioriza todo». La coordinadora, al paralelizar bajo presión, spawneó a **Xilema (cliente separado, configurada por la dirección, posiblemente en otro modelo)** como subagente propia para adelantar la Fase 3. El PR salió limpio y con tests verdes, pero se ejecutó sobre el modelo de la coordinadora, no el de Xilema, silenciando la config de la dirección. La dirección lo detectó y pidió reforzar el Charter. Origen del PR.

## El cambio (2 líneas, principios intactos, añade procedimiento)

- **§III topología:** cláusula operativa (spawnear vs latido; encolar para paralelizar; la tecnología configurada es la razón de ser).
- **§V antipatrones:** item nuevo — «invocar a un cliente separado como subagente propio».

## Notas para la mantenedora

- **VERSION/CHANGELOG sin tocar a propósito** (§IX: sellar la versión es acto de la mantenedora). Candidato a la próxima versión (añade procedimiento, conserva los seis invariantes y los cinco artículos).
- Respetadas las reglas de escritura (`plantillas/reglas-escritura.md`): sin guiones largos, sin contrastes retóricos.
- Candidato a una entrada en `EJEMPLOS.md` con el caso de Savia, a tu criterio.

author: jxzzlfh
body:
## 问题
第 2 步「创作文章」点击「生成 3 个标题」后等待很久标题不出现。

## 根因
`WriterService.getArticle` 把 `article.final.md` 与 `titles.json` 放在**同一个 try/catch** 里读取。而 `titlesRunner` 只写 `titles.json`，正文 `article.final.md` 要等 `articleRunner`（下一步「生成正文」）才落盘。

因此生成标题后 reload 项目时：读 `article.final.md` 抛 ENOENT → 触发 catch → 把已生成的 `titles.json` 也一并返回成 `null` → 前端 `project.article.titles` 为 null → 标题区不渲染。

任务、SSE、反代均正常（任务 succeeded、事件已入库、SSE 能即时重放），纯属后端读取逻辑把两个独立产物绑在了一起。

## 修复
将两次读取拆为独立 try/catch：
- 正文缺失 → `markdown: ""`
- 标题缺失 → `titles: null`

互不影响。

## 验证
- `tsc --noEmit` ✅、`eslint` ✅
- 容器内跑 `app.test.ts`：新增回归测试「exposes generated titles even before the article body exists」✅，原有 4 个测试全过 ✅
- 重新构建部署后，对存量项目 `d0ecd75d` 调 `GET /api/projects/:id`：`article.titles` 从 `null` 变为 3 个标题 ✅

author: cyberlife-coder
body:
## Description

Fixes #1442 — nodes created implicitly via `addEdge`/`INSERT EDGE` were invisible to `graph-nodes`/MATCH on schemaless graph collections (the SDK default). Root cause: `Collection::add_edge`/`add_edges_batch` never validated that an edge's `source`/`target` had a stored payload unless the collection used a *strict* graph schema — silently accepting edges to node IDs that were never created. `GET /graph/nodes`, `all_node_ids()`, and `MATCH` all resolve their node set from the payload store, not the edge store, so those "phantom" edges were permanently invisible outside direct edge queries.

The investigation showed the in-process memory wedge (`velesdb-memory`'s `relate()`) already required both endpoints to exist via its own client-side check — core just didn't enforce the same invariant. The fix makes `add_edge`/`add_edges_batch` reject (not silently accept, not auto-create) an edge to a missing endpoint with `Error::NodeNotFound` (`VELES-022`, REST `404`), matching what strict-schema collections and the wedge already did.

An adversarial multi-angle review of the initial fix (6 independent finder passes: line-by-line diff scan, removed-behavior audit, cross-file caller trace, reuse/simplification, efficiency/hotspots, altitude/conventions) surfaced four additional real bugs beyond the original scope, all fixed in the second commit:

- **`POST /collections/{name}/relations`** (the exact REST endpoint the original bug report was about) mapped every non-`EdgeExists` `add_edge` error to a hardcoded `500`, so the new `NodeNotFound` surfaced as *Internal Server Error* instead of `404`/`VELES-022`. This endpoint had **zero** REST test coverage before this PR.
- **`velesdb-memory`'s `relate()`** downgraded the identical concurrent-delete race to a generic internal error instead of its own documented `NotFound`/`invalid_params` contract.
- **`velesdb-migrate`'s FK-relations phase** writes edges into a fresh, edge-only `GraphCollection` that never otherwise gets node payloads — under the naive fix, *every* migrated edge would now be rejected outright. It now stubs each endpoint before inserting (deduplicated across the whole relation), and a batch-level validation failure degrades to per-edge accounting instead of aborting the entire migration. This path also had zero test coverage before this PR.
- **`tauri-plugin-velesdb`**'s `add_edge`/`add_edges_batch` collapsed every core error into a generic `InvalidConfig` instead of using the crate's own `#[from]` conversion that preserves the VELES-XXX code. ⚠️ **Not compile-verified** — this crate needs GTK/webkit2gtk system libraries unavailable in the sandbox this PR was authored in; please confirm in CI.

Also from review: the new validation helper now reuses the existing `get_node_payload` instead of re-implementing the lock+retrieve; two BFS/DFS stress tests were switched from per-edge to bulk node seeding (a real fsync hotspot the naive fix introduced); added schemaless-mode test coverage for the mixed-endpoint case (only source or only target exists); documented the pre-existing check-then-write race shared by both the strict and schemaless validation paths (not newly introduced, not fixed — closing it fully would need a lock-scope change with real deadlock risk I didn't want to rush); de-duplicated a 3×-copy-pasted node-seeding block in `velesdb-cli`'s `e2e_complete.rs`.

`velesdb-migrate`, `velesdb-mobile`, `velesdb-wasm`, and (beyond the one contract fix above) `velesdb-memory` needed no other changes: migrate's non-relations paths never exercised dangling-edge paths, mobile/wasm ship their own self-contained graph stores not backed by `velesdb_core::Collection`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] 💥 Breaking change — schemaless graph collections (the default) now reject `add_edge`/`add_edges_batch` calls whose endpoints weren't created first, where they previously silently succeeded. See the CHANGELOG migration note.
- [x] 📚 Documentation update (`GRAPH_PATTERNS.md`, `VELESQL_SPEC.md`, OpenAPI spec, CHANGELOG)

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Unit tests — `velesdb-core` (5271 passed, 2 new), `velesdb-server` (152 lib + 87 `api_integration` incl. 2 new relations tests), `velesdb-cli` (all binaries green), `velesdb-migrate` (257 passed incl. 1 new e2e test proving the graph-relations phase survives the new invariant), `velesdb-memory` (267 passed)
- [x] Integration tests — full BDD suite (632 passed), all `velesdb-server` integration binaries
- [ ] Manual testing — not performed; relied on the above plus `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic` (clean on every crate compilable in this sandbox) and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (clean)

**Test Configuration:**
- OS: Linux (sandboxed container)
- Rust version: matches workspace toolchain

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project (clippy pedantic + rustfmt clean)
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code (adversarial multi-angle review, see above)
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published

## Additional Notes

`tauri-plugin-velesdb` could not be built or tested in the authoring sandbox (missing `atk`/`gtk`/`webkit2gtk` system libraries, and the package mirror needed to install them was unreachable). The one change there (`crates/tauri-plugin-velesdb/src/commands_graph.rs`) is a small, type-checked-by-inspection swap from a manual `.map_err` to `?` relying on an existing `#[from] velesdb_core::Error` impl — please have CI confirm it compiles.

author: dev634
body:
## Finding (database performance review, next-steps item #4)

Postgres does **not** auto-index foreign-key columns, and Prisma with the default `relationMode = "foreignKeys"` doesn't add them either. Auditing the migration history, the schema had **zero** FK indexes — only the three implicit `@unique` indexes and the one explicit `RateLimitAttempt` index. Consequences:

- **Reads:** every `findByProject` did a **sequential scan**. The project detail page fires seven of them in one `Promise.all` (tasks, groups, categories, materials, interventions, subcontractors, interims), plus the client detail page's `findByClient`, the file browser's `findChildren`/`findFilesByFolder`, etc.
- **Deletes:** every `onDelete: Cascade` / `SetNull` scanned the child table **across all projects** to find rows to delete or null out — e.g. deleting one `SubcontractorCompany` full-scanned `ProjectTask`, `ProjectTaskGroup` **and** `ProjectTaskCategory` for the `SetNull`, holding a lock for the duration.

The repository layer itself is already efficient — `Promise.all` + Prisma `include` (which batches to `WHERE … IN`), no unbounded N+1. The only lever was the missing indexes.

## Change

Add `@@index` on **every** FK column, backing both the read filters and the cascade/set-null delete scans:

- `Project.clientId`
- `ProjectTask`: `projectId`, `groupId`, `categoryId`, `assignedCompanyId`, `assignedInterimId`
- `ProjectTaskGroup`: `projectId`, `categoryId`, `assignedCompanyId`, `assignedInterimId`
- `ProjectTaskCategory`: `projectId`, `assignedCompanyId`, `assignedInterimId`
- `ProjectFolder`: `(projectId, parentId)` (backs `findChildren`) + `parentId` (self-referential cascade)
- `ProjectMaterial`: `projectId`, `taskId`, `taskGroupId`, `taskCategoryId`
- `Intervention.projectId`, `SubcontractorCompany.projectId`, `SubcontractorPerson.companyId`, `Interim.projectId`
- `ProjectFile`: `projectId`, `folderId`
- `PasswordResetToken.userId`

**Schema/index-only** — no query or application code changes, so behaviour is identical, just without the seq scans. Migration = 26 additive `CREATE INDEX` statements; at this app's scale index creation on deploy is near-instant.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint` clean, `npx vitest run` = 250/250
- Migration applied cleanly to the local DB (`migrate dev`); project detail page + dashboard re-render correctly with the regenerated Prisma client, no console/server errors
- Production applies it automatically via `prisma migrate deploy` on container start

author: kannonski
body:
Three shell-integration features built on the OSC 133 marks kedi already emits.

## Recall — the session timeline (⌘R / View ▸ Recall Commands…)
A structured lens over a shell's command history — **not** a re-render of the terminal. Deliberately does **not** compete with atuin's command-recall; instead it owns the thing atuin can't: **output**.

- **Output is persisted.** Each finished command's clean, xterm-rendered output (no ANSI, capped 128 KB) is captured at command-end and written to `<app_data>/history/<launch>-<session>.jsonl`. So it stays copyable after the buffer scrolls, a **pop-out/move**, or a **restart**.
- **Two scopes:** *this terminal* (live + restored via `history_load`) and *⏳ earlier* (every session on disk via `history_recent`). Toggle with **⌘E** / pills.
- **Actions:** **⌘C** copy output · **⌘D** diff the previous run of the same command · **↵** jump · **⌘↵** re-run · **⇥** cycles all/✗/⏱ filters.
- **Bounds:** last **50** commands per session; newest ~**30** session files retained.
- A **launch-epoch** key stops a fresh session (sid resets to 1 each launch) from inheriting a prior run's history; a **1.5 s replay-grace** stops the pop-out ring-replay from double-recording.
- New `OSC 133;E` (base64 command line) in the preexec hook so the timeline knows what each command was.

## Command-finished notifications
Slow commands (≥8 s) that finish while you're looking elsewhere (another tab / kedi unfocused) fire a native notification. `tauri-plugin-notification` + `notification:default` capability.

## Clickable paths
⌘-click a `path` or `path:line[:col]` → opens in your editor (`open_path` → `code -g` / `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` / OS default).

## Notes
- All parsing stays in the frontend (xterm); the backend just persists the already-clean entries.
- `history_recent` (⌘E) currently loads all persisted output into memory on open — fine for KB-sized output; can switch to metadata-only + lazy fetch if it ever gets heavy.

## Testing
Relaunch, fresh tab, run commands → ⌘R. Verified: copy/diff/jump/re-run, filters, pop-out preserves history+output, and restart→⌘E archive copies output from disk. Cross-platform CI bundles unaffected.

**Gap:** the client rejected `opts.class` on the local append path (`localUnsupported('message taxonomy routing')`), so taxonomy-directed routing couldn't be requested. Server#48 (PR#51) now does append-time class/prefix/to routing.

**Fix (minimal):** stop rejecting `opts.class`; forward `class` in the local append payload, matching server#48's append shape (`exactKeys(payload, ['message'], ['visibility','recipientDroneIds','class','to'])`, `class`=optionalString(64)).

author: weyhon
body:
## What changed

- Added a Codex runtime backed by the official `codex app-server` JSON-RPC protocol.
- Persistently maps each owned Slack thread to a Codex thread and resumes it after bridge restarts.
- Downloads private Slack images with bot-token authentication and forwards local image paths to Codex turns.
- Added an installable Claude Code marketplace package with corrected MCP/start entrypoints.
- Added production macOS service templates, per-bot state isolation, and migration guidance.
- Added persistent developer instructions and reapplies safety/runtime settings when a migrated Codex thread is resumed.
- Preserved user/channel allowlists, top-level mention gating, and mention-free follow-ups only in known bot threads.
- Added conversation-aware DM routing: top-level DMs stay in the main timeline and share one continuous agent session, while deliberately opened DM threads remain isolated.
- Isolated the Slack Codex runtime's `CODEX_HOME` so Codex Desktop cannot overwrite its model cache or session database.
- Added 30-second RPC and 15-minute turn timeouts; timeouts are reported to Slack before launchd restarts the bridge.
- Added dedicated Claude Channel settings plus Screen and launchd/expect supervisors so Slack can run without a visible terminal and without inheriting globally enabled Discord/Telegram channels.
- Bumped the independent project to version 0.3.3.

## Why

The bridge must support both Claude Code Channels and Codex while keeping credentials, sessions, and runtime protocols separate. Codex Mini was still running from the upstream `cc-connect` binary, so its operation and future improvements were not fully owned by this repository.

Slack top-level DMs were previously assigned a new thread/session for every message. That made private conversations visually fragmented and prevented reliable continuity. Routing now distinguishes channel roots, top-level DMs, and deliberate DM threads.

A shared `~/.codex/models_cache.json` was being written by Codex Desktop in a schema that the standalone Codex CLI 0.144.3 could not parse. Slack delivery succeeded and a Codex task started, but `turn/start` then hung silently. The bridge now keeps cache/session state isolated while optionally sharing authentication, configuration, skills, and plugins for local feature parity.

The previous Claude Slack Screen resumed a session that also loaded globally enabled Discord and Telegram plugins. The new Slack-specific Session loads only `channel-bridge`, preventing duplicate Discord consumers while leaving the user's foreground Discord terminal untouched.

macOS LaunchAgents do not automatically inherit Terminal Full Disk Access for privacy-protected cloud folders. The deployment therefore documents both a launchd/expect supervisor (after granting the relevant access) and a detached Screen fallback that preserves the authorized Terminal security context.

## Security

- Slack bot/app tokens remain outside the repository in mode-600 state directories.
- Slack user and channel allowlists remain mandatory.
- Top-level channel messages require a bot mention; only an owned thread accepts follow-ups without another mention.
- Only roots that explicitly mention this bot are migrated, preventing cross-bot thread ownership.
- Full-machine Codex/Claude permissions remain an explicit deployment choice.
- The development-channel confirmation wrapper is limited to locally reviewed plugins.
- Secret scan found no real Slack, Claude, or Anthropic token patterns.

## Validation

- `npm run check`: TypeScript build plus 9 passing tests.
- `claude plugin validate .`: passed (one non-blocking marketplace-description warning).
- Both macOS plist templates pass `plutil -lint`; the Screen script passes `bash -n`.
- Codex Mini LaunchAgent is running from the isolated Codex home.
- The isolated model cache has zero entries missing `supports_reasoning_summaries`.
- A new Slack-triggered Codex session was written below the isolated session directory.
- Live Slack dual-mention test produced both `Codex正常` and `Claude正常` in the same thread.
- Live isolated Claude Slack Session test returned `新Session正常`.
- Live final detached Screen test returned `后台Slack正常` in the top-level DM timeline.
- The Claude Slack process tree contains only `channel-bridge`; no Discord or Telegram child was spawned.
- The pre-existing foreground Discord parent/child processes remained running with unchanged PIDs throughout migration.
- Live channel mention/no-mention, image download, and Codex/Claude DM continuity tests passed.
- `git diff --check` and the real-token secret scan passed.
