author: jenner-analytics
body:
[Jenneranalytics.com](https://jenneranalytics.com) provides an API that runs SAS code, with support for more than 200 SAS procedures. You can also use it with AI assistants in a collaborative workspace. It's available for Mac on the Apple App Store, and by license for Windows and Linux.

We support the larger community by
(1) increasing access to SAS-compatible systems,
(2) by providing test coverage and a test coverage framework to public SAS repos in order to encourage the use of best practices in software engineering.

The SAS half of this workflow runs on Jenner unmodified — this PR adds a small compatibility bundle so you can see for yourself. It's the test we wrote for your workflow, shared in case it's useful, and was assembled with AI assistance as is most code in modern businesses today. The bundle rebuilds the `have` table from your state-list array and then does the `SELECT DISTINCT` per column in `PROC SQL` — the same `col1_unq` / `col2_unq` / `col3_unq` union your `sqldf` step produces, but staying inside SAS instead of the round-trip through PostgreSQL.

What made this one fun to lift out was `%let stateslnq=%sysfunc(compbl(%str(...)))`: packing all fifty state names into one compressed macro string and then dropping it straight into `array states[50] $64 (&stateslnq)` as the initializer is a tidy trick — the array literal and the data generator stay in lockstep with a single edit, and `int(50*uniform(54321))+1` keeps the whole thing reproducible. It's a compact way to stand up a million-row demographics table with no external input at all, which is exactly what makes the distinct-value question interesting.

The `jenner-check/` directory is self-contained and nothing in it runs on merge — no workflow files, no hooks, nothing outside the folder is touched. It holds one bundle, the runner, and a captured copy of the passing run:

```
jenner-check/
├── run_jenner.sh
├── README.md
└── t001_states_distinct/
    ├── script.sas        # your %let stateslnq + array DATA step, sd1 -> WORK, row count reduced
    ├── autoexec.sas      # options obs=100; validvarname=v7;
    ├── expected.json     # pinned status / exit code / log lines
    └── expected/         # captured log + listing from the passing run
```

To run it yourself, check out this PR's branch and, from the repo root:

```bash
gh pr checkout 1
curl -sS --data-binary @jenner-check/t001_states_distinct/script.sas https://api.jenneranalytics.com/v1/quick
```

Or `cd jenner-check && ./run_jenner.sh --all`, which re-runs the bundle and verifies each pinned field in `expected.json`. The hosted API is free to try with no signup; full API reference: [the docs](https://docs.jenneranalytics.com/api/).

On data: the runner uploads only the SAS source text of the script it runs (plus the two-line autoexec) to api.jenneranalytics.com, which runs it and returns the log and listing. It does not read or upload any data files, so anything sitting next to a script stays on your machine, and nothing is sent unless you run one of the commands yourself — the same as pasting a snippet into any hosted tool. The one thing worth a glance is that a script's own source is what's transmitted, so you can review it first if it ever embeds values inline.

Merge it, close it, or ignore it — all fine, and no response is expected. We won't open further PRs on this repo. To opt out of any future contact entirely, put `no-more-prs` in a comment or open an issue titled `jenner-check: opt out`.

---

CEO / Jenner Analytics Ltd

author: takeokunn
body:
## Summary

No diff existed against `main` to review (this repo's whole history
was created in the previous PR), so this is a full-codebase
correctness sweep across `src/` and `t/`. Every finding below was
confirmed by direct SBCL execution before being fixed, and each ships
with a regression test that reproduces the original defect.

- **Recorded-call history aliasing** (`core-utilities.lisp`): `%record-call`/
  `%snapshot-recorded-calls` only shallow-copied each call plist, so
  mutating a returned `:result`/`:arguments` value (e.g. `NREVERSE`,
  `SETF GETF`) silently corrupted a boundary's own recorded history —
  contradicting the documented "independent snapshot" guarantee. Fixed
  with `COPY-TREE` at both record and snapshot time, which covers every
  boundary built on this shared mechanism (filesystem, process, env,
  network).
- **`plist-remove-keys` transposition** (`core-utilities.lisp`): pushed
  value before key, so the retained plist came back with keys/values
  swapped. Its only caller builds the "unknown filesystem write
  options" error message, which showed a garbled, non-plist structure.
- **`assert-recorded-call-sequence` false negative** (`testing.lisp`):
  the parallel `LOOP for actual in calls` silently stopped as soon as
  the shorter `calls` list was exhausted, so `:exact-length nil`
  (documented for prefix-only checks) never caught a missing trailing
  expected call.
- **Fake clock stale closures** (`clock.lisp`): `make-fake-clock`'s
  `now-fn`/`monotonic-fn` closures captured the initial `start`/
  `monotonic-start` values instead of reading the mutable slots, so the
  inherited public `clock-now-fn`/`clock-monotonic-fn` readers stayed
  frozen at construction time even after `advance-fake-clock`.
- **Directory listing merge-pathnames bug** (`filesystem-directory.lisp`):
  a directory argument without a trailing separator (e.g.
  `#P"/tmp/mydir"`) parses its last component as a file name, so
  merging a wild name/type onto it listed the *parent* directory.
- **Fake `:overwrite` semantics** (`filesystem-fakes-helpers.lisp`):
  `make-test-filesystem` treated `:if-exists :overwrite` like
  `:supersede` (full replacement); real CL `:overwrite` preserves any
  existing tail beyond the new content's length, so tests written
  against the fake didn't match `make-filesystem` in production.
- **Subprocess timeout only sends SIGTERM** (`process-exec-helpers.lisp`):
  a child that traps or ignores SIGTERM hung `process-boundary-run`
  forever despite a `:timeout`. Now escalates to SIGKILL after a
  bounded grace period.
- **Subprocess output deadlock + fd leak** (`process-exec-helpers.lisp`):
  `%run-native-process/cps` waited for the whole process to exit
  before reading stdout/stderr, so a child writing more than one OS
  pipe buffer combined across both streams deadlocked on `write()`.
  Both streams are now drained concurrently in threads while waiting,
  and the process handle is closed afterward (it was never closed
  before, leaking two file descriptors per invocation).

## Test plan
- [x] `sbcl --script` load of `:cl-boundary-kit` plus every test file
  except `t/prolog-boundary-invariants.lisp` (needs `cl-prolog`, which
  isn't buildable for aarch64-darwin locally): **106/106 green**,
  including 8 new regression tests, one per fix above.
- [x] Manually reproduced each original defect against the
  pre-fix code and confirmed the fix resolves it (aliasing corruption,
  plist transposition, missing-call false negative, stale clock
  closures, wrong directory listed, `:overwrite` truncation, SIGTERM-
  ignoring child hanging, and a 300KB-output pipe deadlock).
- [ ] CI (`nix flake check` on x86_64-linux via GitHub Actions),
  including `t/prolog-boundary-invariants.lisp` and the doc-contract
  suite, which this environment can't run locally.

author: urtech87-ops
body:
Hardens the public AI/TTS proxies (nonce is scrapable, so it is not wallet protection) to cap the cost-abuse blast radius. Scope is limited to `functions.php` proxy security — no changes to tool JS, prompts, models, the dispatcher, the seeder, or page structure. Normal-user behavior is unchanged. `php -l` passes on every commit.

## Phase A — cap input size on the text proxy
- New constant `TG_AI_MAX_INPUT_CHARS` (8000, overridable in wp-config.php) next to `TG_AI_MODEL`.
- `tg_build_user_prompt()`: each payload value is capped at 8000 chars before substitution, and the final assembled prompt is hard-truncated to 8000 chars.
- `tg_ai_proxy_handler()`: requests whose total `payload` string size exceeds 20,000 chars are rejected early with HTTP 413 "Input too long." — before any rate-limit bookkeeping or API call. Generous enough for essays/long text, but bounded.

## Phase B — server-side max_tokens ceiling
- New constant `TG_AI_MAX_TOKENS` (2000). `tg_call_openrouter()` clamps the per-tool value: `min((int)($config['max_tokens'] ?? 1500), TG_AI_MAX_TOKENS)`. A misconfigured or oversized per-tool setting can no longer inflate output cost.

## Phase C — production-quiet logging, no raw API bodies to the browser
- The full-response `error_log()` calls now run only when `WP_DEBUG` is on.
- Error paths log a short string (tool key + HTTP status + provider error message) — never the full body, never user input.
- The empty-response error returned to the browser is now generic ("AI returned an empty response. Please try again.") instead of echoing the raw API body.

## Phase D — method and tool validation
- Both `tg_ai_proxy_handler()` and `tg_tts_proxy_handler()` reject non-POST requests with HTTP 405 before doing anything else.
- The AI handler rejects an empty or unknown `tool` key with HTTP 400 **before** the rate-limit/daily-cap counters run, so junk requests no longer burn a rate-limit slot.
- TTS input cap confirmed already bounded (12,000-char check plus 4,000-char chunking) — left as-is per spec.

## Phase E — backstop verification (report)
- ✅ `check_ajax_referer('tg_tool_nonce', 'nonce')` present on all three AJAX handlers: AI proxy, TTS proxy, and `tg_handle_removebg`.
- ✅ `tg_check_rate_limit` + `tg_check_daily_cap` called in both the AI handler (30/hr, `TG_AI_DAILY_CAP`) and the TTS handler (15/hr, `TG_TTS_DAILY_CAP`).
- ✅ Admin exemption (`current_user_can('manage_options')`) exists in both `tg_check_rate_limit` and `tg_check_daily_cap`, so admin testing is never blocked.
- ✅ `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` never reaches the client: the only `wp_localize_script` call (`tgAiConfig`) exposes ajaxUrl, nonce, toolKey, actionLabel, a boolean `removebgConfigured` flag, and the TTS model slug — no keys.
- ⚠️ Fixed: `tg_handle_removebg` had a nonce but **no rate limit** — added `tg_check_rate_limit('tg_removebg_rate_', 10)` (10/hour, admin-exempt), since remove.bg is a paid credit-metered API.
- 📝 Out-of-scope observation (not changed): `tg_handle_url_to_pdf` has no nonce check and no rate limit, and fetches arbitrary URLs server-side. It costs no API credits, but you may want a follow-up to add `check_ajax_referer` + rate limiting there.

## Testing checklist
- [ ] Normal AI tools still work (essay, grammar, faq, etc.) with typical input
- [ ] A pasted 100KB input is rejected with a clear message, not sent to the API
- [ ] TTS still works
- [ ] With WP_DEBUG off, no full API bodies are written to debug.log
- [ ] Admin (logged in) is still exempt from rate limits
- [ ] Rate limit + daily cap still trigger for logged-out users

## Mini-Fix-Bericht (vollständig, als PR-Beschreibung)

**Regel eingehalten:** nichts auf `main` gepusht — Branch `nachlese-3`, Commit `27532f3`.

### 1. Slot-Anlage lokalisiert und serverseitig gehärtet ✅
Zwei Anlage-Pfade gefunden, beide ohne Dublettenprüfung:
- `addPickupSlot` in `src/server/actions/farm.ts` (Einstellungen → Abholzeiten)
- `createOnboardingSlots` in `src/server/actions/onboarding.ts` (Onboarding, Batch via `createMany`)

Neue gemeinsame, pure Regel-Bibliothek **`src/lib/pickup-slot-rules.ts`**: `isDuplicateSlot` (Einzel-Anlage) und `hasDuplicateSlots` (Batch — prüft gegen den Bestand **und** innerhalb des Aufrufs, damit zweimal dieselbe Zeit im selben Onboarding-Schritt ebenfalls abgefangen wird). Gesperrt ist ausschließlich die **exakte** Kombination Wochentag + Von + Bis; zwei verschiedene Fenster am selben Tag (Sa 9–12 und Sa 15–17) bleiben ausdrücklich erlaubt. Meldung: **„Diese Abholzeit existiert bereits."** (`DUPLICATE_SLOT_MESSAGE`, eine Konstante für beide Pfade). Bei Ablehnung wird nichts geschrieben.

### 2. Dieselbe Prüfung in Settings UND Onboarding ✅
Beide Actions nutzen dieselben Helper und dieselbe Meldungs-Konstante. Die Clients brauchten keinen Umbau: Das Settings-Formular zeigt Action-Fehler bereits per `toast.error`, das Onboarding über sein bestehendes `result.error`-Muster — die neue Meldung fließt durch die vorhandenen `{ error }`-Rückgaben.

### 3. Tests ✅ (9 neu, gesamt 142 grün)
`tests/pickup-slot-rules.test.ts` — Helper: nur exakte Dubletten (anderer Tag / andere Von- / andere Bis-Zeit → kein Duplikat), Batch prüft auch untereinander. Actions (Prisma/Auth gemockt): exaktes Duplikat → abgelehnt mit exakt der deutschen Meldung, kein Schreibzugriff; gleicher Tag, andere Zeit → angelegt; **Ownership unverändert** (ohne Session „Nicht angemeldet", fremde Farm „Hof nicht gefunden." — jeweils ohne Schreibzugriff).

### 4. Mobil-Pflichtzeile ✅ — gemessen (375 × 812, Chromium gegen Produktions-Build)
Der Fehlertext erscheint als Sonner-Toast; Messung einer Toast-Replik mit der echten Meldung: Breite 343 px, **kein Text-Überlauf**, vollständig im Viewport, 0 px Seiten-Überlauf. This pull request introduces several improvements to the starter script generation and the UI, focusing on enhanced support for MCP (Modular Copilot Protocol) configuration, improved relation cardinality labeling, and UI polish. The most significant change is the automatic generation of `.vscode/mcp.json` for Python starter projects, enabling easier integration with Copilot Chat and external tools. The changes also include improved test coverage for MCP config generation, clearer relation labeling, and minor UI adjustments.

**Starter script and MCP integration:**
- Added generation of `.vscode/mcp.json` (with appropriate environment variables for BASIC, M2M, or OIDC authentication) when creating a starter script project, except for ATFX connections. This enables seamless Copilot Chat integration. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-441046ac42e7cf820fea0bbf74dc751978c112caef321f766f10d0d6b3211620R81-R149) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-441046ac42e7cf820fea0bbf74dc751978c112caef321f766f10d0d6b3211620R174-R180)
- Implemented helper functions (`_build_mcp_env_basic`, `_build_mcp_env_m2m`, `_build_mcp_env_oidc`, `_build_mcp_json`) to construct MCP environment and configuration objects based on the server authentication type.

**Testing and validation:**
- Added comprehensive unit tests for MCP environment and JSON generation, including validation of generated files and their content for all supported authentication types. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-65a62afd4066e773c317371ed1c0868ea9dde624e195f0042683d0483876fc5dR11-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-65a62afd4066e773c317371ed1c0868ea9dde624e195f0042683d0483876fc5dR310-R506)

author: jonbackhaus
body:
## meal-planner-fkg.7 (P2)

Reading Notes needs a TCC **Automation** grant; reading `NoteStore.sqlite` needs **Full Disk Access**. Under launchd there's no UI to answer the prompt, so a fresh machine, a new binary path, or a macOS upgrade resetting TCC turns every sync into a silent no-op — undocumented, and only a `console.warn` (invisible on the daemon).

## Code
- `SyncResult` gains `suspiciousEmptyRead`, set when q95.14's empty-read guard trips (0 notes read while the index is non-empty — the denied/failed-Notes-read fingerprint).
- `makeBuildPlanWithSync` fires a **loud, secret-free alert** (to `#agent-alerts` + local log) once when that signal is set, then **proceeds** against the existing index (proceed+alert). Guarded so a broken alerter can't sink generation.
- `syncNotes` stays alert-free (no notifier dep). A denied read that *throws* is already covered by the existing throw→alert path; a denied read that returns *empty* now alerts via this signal. No regression to q95.14/q95.13/q95.7.

## Docs (`RUNBOOK.md`)
- §0.1 grant Automation (→ Notes) + Full Disk Access to the daemon's node binary before first run (trigger the prompt via a foreground `pnpm sync`; TCC keys on binary identity).
- §0.2 post-OS-update / node-upgrade re-verify step (ties the new alert to "re-check TCC").
- §0.3 Apple-schema-change risk note. Cross-refs bd6.11 (osascript hang) + q95.13 (NoteStore read).

## Verification
- New tests: alerts once + proceeds on suspicious read; no alert on normal sync; doesn't reject when the alert throws; `suspiciousEmptyRead` true only on the guarded case.
- Independently re-verified (based on current main): typecheck/typecheck:test/lint/build clean; **546 tests pass**.

author: othmanemad
body:
## What

Adds an **opt-in `waitForSubflows` mode** to _Stream CSV to Subflows_. After dispatching all batches, the parent pauses on a **Join Waitpoint** and resumes once every dispatched child run reaches a terminal state, returning a `{ completed, failed }` summary.

Based on `feat/stream-csv-to-subflows` (fan-out) — this PR adds the fan-in half.

## How it works

- A **Join Waitpoint** is an ordinary `WEBHOOK` waitpoint carrying a non-null `expectedCount` — that field is the sole discriminator, so no new `PauseType`/entity/token protocol.
- When a child lands terminal, the `runsMetadataQueue` worker runs `COUNT(flow_run WHERE parentRunId=:p AND status terminal)` over the existing `idx_run_parent_run_id` index; on `>= expectedCount` it completes + resumes the parent.
- **COUNT is the whole mechanism** — idempotent under BullMQ retries and concurrent completions because it reads committed state. Exactly-once resume comes from `waitpointService.complete()` (pessimistic-locked, `WHERE status=PENDING`).
- The parent's own `PAUSED` upload re-runs the same `completeFanInIfDone` helper, sealing the finish-before-pause race.

Deliberately **no Redis fast-path and no counter column**: at ADR-0009's bounded fan-out, one indexed COUNT per completion is cheap. A `ponytail:` comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path if a large fan-out ever regresses.

## DB footprint per child completion

- 1 indexed `getPendingByFlowRunId(parent)` read to gate; COUNT only for actual joins.
- 1 `complete` write, once, by the single winner. Zero Redis, zero extra writes.

## Changes

- Migration: nullable `expectedCount` column on `waitpoint`.
- `flow-runs-queue.ts`: `completeFanInIfDone` (shared by child-terminal and parent-paused paths).
- Piece: `waitForSubflows` checkbox + `RESUME` handling returning the tally.
- Waitpoint entity/service/types/controller, framework + engine wiring to pass `expectedCount`.
- ADR-0010 (amends ADR-0009) + `.agents` domain docs.

## Notes

- `.env.dev` / `docker-compose.dev.yml` local changes are intentionally **not** included.
- Failed batches count toward completion (the CSV action keeps `FAIL_PARENT_ON_FAILURE=false`); fail-fast via `failParentOnFailure=true` is untouched.
- Orphan child (a dispatched run that never materializes) → indefinite pause until retention cleanup, same as `callFlow` + `waitForResponse` today. Orphan-timeout backstop is future work.

## Summary

author: imaustink
body:
## Summary

Following up on the CRD-duplication fix (#28): every Tool/Skill/Agent that
ships a manually-`kubectl apply`-able CR (`tools/*/tool.yaml`,
`apps/agent-orchestrator/config/samples/*.yaml`,
`apps/opencode-swe-agent/agent.yaml`) also has a Helm-templated twin in
`charts/community-components/templates/` — the version actually installed by
a real deployment. Their prose fields (`description`/`input`/`output`/
`markdown`/`orchestratorPrompt`/`agentPrompt`) are meant to be identical
across both, but nothing enforced that.

Running the new checker against `main` found real, pre-existing drift:
- `apps/agent-orchestrator/config/samples/recipe-refining-skill.yaml` was
  missing the `tool_instance_key` mechanism and several behavior updates
  present in the chart template.
- `apps/opencode-swe-agent/agent.yaml` was missing the ADR 0017 session
  continuity behavior described in the chart template.

Anyone applying either file directly (the documented manual-install path)
would get stale instructions.

## Changes
- `scripts/sync-manifest-docs.py`: extracts the shared prose fields from a
  plain-CR file and its chart-template twin and either reports a diff
  (`--check`) or overwrites the plain-CR side from the chart template
  (`--fix`, which is treated as the source of truth). Deliberately leaves
  everything else (header comments, hardcoded vs. `{{ .Values.* }}` image/
  serviceAccountName/secretRef, the `{{- if }}` enable guard) untouched —
  those are expected to differ.
- `.github/workflows/validate-crds.yml`: new `check-manifest-docs-sync` job
  runs `--check` on any PR touching either side, so this can't silently
  drift again.
- Ran `--fix` to bring the two already-drifted files up to date.
- `charts/community-components/README.md`: documents the pattern for anyone
  adding a new component with both a plain-CR and chart-template twin.

Note: this doesn't touch `swe-agent-description-tools` (open, unmerged) —
its 4 edited files were already textually consistent, so there was nothing
to fix there specifically; this is the general tooling that prevents the
next such branch from drifting silently.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `check-manifest-docs-sync` job runs and passes.

author: aia2025
body:
## Zusammenfassung

Baut die `apexcore-mvp`-Dossier-Vorlage auf die dreistufige Struktur um, jetzt erweitert um die Kanzlei-Rückmeldung vom 19.07.2026 (Olaf Bitter, Kieslich Rechtsanwälte) mit dem Ziel, den Anwalt bis unmittelbar vor die Freigabe der Abmahnung zu führen:

- **Ebene A — Technische Tatsachen**: jede Aussage verweist inline auf ihr Beweismittel (Anlage/Datei/Seite/Hash/Beweisqualität) statt nur gesammelt im Anhang.
- **Ebene B — Vorläufige rechtliche Einordnung**: Tabelle (Norm / Tatbestandsmerkmal / Feststellung / Ergebnis / Beweismittel-Referenz / Offene Punkte) mit dem vorgeschriebenen Disclaimer-Header.
- **Gutachterliche Prüfung im Detail** (neu): vollständige Subsumtion je Norm im klassischen Gutachtenstil (Tatbestandsmerkmal — Feststellung — Subsumtion — Ergebnis).
- **Anspruchsgrundlage und Rechtsfolgen** (neu): Standard-Anspruchsgrundlage und typische Ansprüche je Norm.
- **Erwartete Einwendungen der Gegenseite und mögliche Erwiderungen** (neu): automatisiert erstellte Vorbereitungshilfe.
- **Prozessuale Risikobewertung** (neu): vorläufige, hedged Einschätzung der Beweislage.
- **Ebene C — Anwaltliche Entscheidung**: jetzt inkl. **Mandats- und Abmahnungsparameter** (Aktivlegitimation, Passivlegitimation, Gegenstandswert, Vertragsstrafe, Frist, Kosten) — echte Leerfelder, die ausschließlich aus Mandatsdaten/Kanzlei-Eingabe kommen, niemals automatisiert befüllt.

Neue Abschnitte aus der ersten Runde bleiben: "Sachverhalt für den anwaltlichen Schriftsatz", "Vorläufige rechtliche Subsumtion", "KI-Übergabe" (kopierbarer Prompt-Block, jetzt inkl. Anspruchsgrundlagen, erwarteten Einwendungen, Risikobewertung und Mandatsparameter-Warnhinweis bei fehlenden Angaben).

Screenshot-Annotation via Pillow. Fable-Reviewer-Prompt liefert `legal_subsumption_chain` (jetzt inkl. subsumtion/ergebnis/anspruchsgrundlage/rechtsfolgen), `erwartete_einwendungen` und `prozessuale_risikobewertung` im strukturierten JSON.

**Wichtiges Sicherheits-/Integritäts-Gate (unverändert):** `apexcore-mvp/main.py`'s `detect()` liefert weiterhin `random.uniform()`-Mock-Scores. Nur menschlich als `verified=True` markierte `TechnicalFinding`-Objekte fließen in Ebene B/Gutachten/KI-Übergabe. `MandateParameters` wird von `review()` nie automatisch befüllt — fehlende Mandatsdaten führen zu einer sichtbaren Warnung im KI-Übergabe-Prompt statt zu stillschweigend übergangenen Lücken.

## Beispiele

`apexcore-mvp/examples/arag_demo.py` (ARAG SE, `AX-2026-0E8E4D2534`) und `apexcore-mvp/examples/flatex_demo.py` (flatexDEGIRO Bank AG, `AX-2026-576B23137D`) — beide vollständig durchgespielt, je 15 Seiten PDF + Markdown-Export. Aktivlegitimation ist bei beiden Fällen konsistent als "OFFEN" markiert (Wettbewerber-vs-Verband-Frage aus der Tageszusammenfassung, BGH März 2025). Werte ohne Quelle in diesem Chat (URL, Uhrzeit, echte Hashes, Gegenstandswert, Vertragsstrafe, Frist, Kosten) bleiben sichtbare Platzhalter.

Migrationshinweise für die Anbindung an die echte Pipeline unter `/data/apexcore` (KVM8, außerhalb des Zugriffs dieser Session) in `apexcore-mvp/MIGRATION.md`.

## Geänderte/neue Dateien

- `apexcore-mvp/evidence.py` — `quality`-Feld (Beweisqualität)
- `apexcore-mvp/fable_reviewer.py` — `MandateParameters`, `ExpectedDefense`, erweiterte `LegalSubsumptionRow`, erweitertes JSON-Schema
- `apexcore-mvp/dossier_template.py` — 4 neue Sektionen, erweiterte Ebene B/C, Markdown-Export im Gleichschritt
- `apexcore-mvp/main.py` — `assemble_pdf()` nutzt `render_dossier()`
- `apexcore-mvp/examples/arag_demo.py`, `flatex_demo.py` — beide Fälle vollständig durchgespielt
- `apexcore-mvp/requirements.txt`, `MIGRATION.md`, `.gitignore`

## Test-Plan

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile` über alle Module — ok
- [x] Beide Beispiele lokal ausgeführt, PDFs erzeugt (je 15 Seiten) und visuell geprüft

## Summary

Adds comprehensive CI/CD checks to prevent regressions, separated from the squad-managed workflow so squad upgrades won't overwrite project-specific checks.

Closes #11

Working as **Tank** (Integration & Test Engineer) — `squad:tank`

## Changes

### New: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
Project-owned CI workflow with a **two-job pipeline**:

**Job 1: `lint`** (fast feedback, ~30s)
- **Dockerfile linting** — hadolint scans all 7 service Dockerfiles (DL3008/DL3013 suppressed for ROS base images)

**Job 2: `build-and-test`** (full stack, ~5min)
- Builds all images, starts the stack, waits for healthy
- **Smoke tests** — runs `tests/smoke.sh` (service health + proxy routing for all 5 endpoints)
- **ROS graph check** — `ros2 node list` via the ROS container
- **Playwright acceptance tests** — S1 (stack health) and S2 (window manager) via Chromium
- **Artifact uploads** — Playwright report + traces uploaded on failure (14-day retention)

Triggers: PRs to dev/preview/main/insider + push to dev/main/insider.

### Reverted: `.github/workflows/squad-ci.yml`
Restored to its original squad-cli-managed state — this file may be updated by `squad upgrade` and should not contain project-specific checks.

## Why separate files?

`squad-ci.yml` is managed by the squad-cli and gets overwritten during `squad upgrade`. All project-specific CI checks (linting, smoke tests, acceptance tests) live in `ci.yml` so they survive upgrades.

## Feasibility assessment

| Test tier | CI feasibility | Status |
|-----------|---------------|--------|
| Dockerfile linting | ✅ Trivial | **Enabled** |
| Smoke tests (smoke.sh) | ✅ Fully feasible | **Enabled** |
| S1–S2 acceptance (Playwright) | ✅ Feasible | **Enabled** |
| S3–S9 acceptance | ⚠️ Feasible but heavyweight | Documented for future enablement |

S3–S9 involve terminal I/O, VNC pixel analysis, and service restarts. They work locally but are deferred from CI to keep pipeline time reasonable. A comment in the workflow documents how to enable them later.

author: georgi
body:
Closes #3532.

Adds `nodetool.model3d.RenderToImage` — 3D scene + camera → image. Renders GLB/glTF with three.js: orbit camera (azimuth/elevation/fov/zoom) auto-framed from the model's bounding sphere, lighting presets (studio / soft / flat) with an intensity multiplier, width/height, and background color or transparent PNG. No grid, axes, or gizmos — the scene is built fresh from the model plus the requested lights.

## How it renders

One shared render core (`render3d-core.ts`), two hosts:

- **Browser runner** — the node is tagged `node + browser`. In the in-browser workflow runner it renders directly on an `OffscreenCanvas` via WebGL (main thread or worker) — no headless Chrome involved. Registered as its own module group in `browserRunnerCore.ts`, imported via the `nodes/model3d/render` subpath so the rest of the model3d family (node:fs loaders, manifold/meshoptimizer ops) stays out of the browser bundle. The Node-only branch is behind a `/* @vite-ignore */` dynamic import, so Vite skips it while esbuild still follows it for the server bundle.
- **Node backend** — no WebGL on the server, so the node launches a headless Chromium (`CHROME_PATH` or chrome-launcher discovery, SwiftShader flags so WebGL works on GPU-less servers), injects a self-contained page bundle (three.js + the same core, built by esbuild during the package build), and drives it over CDP with base64 GLB in / base64 PNG out.

## Packaging

- `dist/render3d-page.js` is registered in `PACKAGE_RUNTIME_ASSETS` (`@nodetool-ai/config`), so the Electron backend packaging stages and verifies it, and it resolves through the package export `@nodetool-ai/video-nodes/render3d-page.js` in dev/npm layouts.
- New video-nodes deps: `three` (matching web's `^0.185.1`), `chrome-launcher`, `chrome-remote-interface` (the same launch approach the automation nodes use); dev deps `@types/three`, `esbuild`, `@types/chrome-remote-interface`.
- GLBs using `EXT_meshopt_compression` decode via the existing `meshoptimizer` dependency.

## Tests

`packages/video-nodes/tests/model3d-render.test.ts`: camera framing/orbit math, platform tags, input validation (empty model, non-glTF format), and a real end-to-end headless render asserting a valid PNG of the requested size (skipped when no Chromium binary is found).

Verified manually: rendered a cube GLB through the headless path — auto-framing, studio lighting, background color, and aspect ratio all correct. `npm run build:packages`, video-nodes/config/base-nodes lint + tests, web typecheck, web production build (the render chunk emits for both main and worker bundles), and the web browser-runner jest suites all pass. Pre-existing sandbox-only failures (better-sqlite3 bindings, mobile react-native types) are unrelated.

author: xdezex
body:
## Summary
- Adds a `PreToolUse` hook (matcher `Bash`) that **denies** compound commands which `cd` (or `git -C`) into the main repo checkout and invoke `git`, while the session's cwd is pinned inside a `.claude/worktrees/*` path.
- Adds a second `PreToolUse` hook (same matcher, warn-only) that flags destructive git operations (`git clean`, `git reset`, `git checkout --`, `git stash drop`) run from inside a worktree, since worktrees share one `.git` object store with the main tree and these can affect shared refs/objects even though they look worktree-scoped.

This targets a real, observed failure mode: an agent isolated in its own worktree (via `EnterWorktree`) chaining `cd <main-repo-root> && git add ... && git status`, which stages/commits against the shared main checkout instead of its own isolated worktree copy.

## Prior art / this is a known problem
This isn't a one-off — it's a documented, currently open upstream issue:

- **[anthropics/claude-code#30213](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/30213)** (open) — describes the exact `cd && git` vs `git -C` inconsistency this PR works around: `git -C <path> <command>` never triggers Claude Code's built-in "bare repository attack" approval gate, while `cd <path> && git <command>` always does, even for known worktree paths. The suggested upstream fix is to *allow* the pattern for worktree targets; this PR takes the stricter direction instead — it *blocks* references to the main checkout, rather than allowlisting the worktree case, since there's rarely a legitimate reason to reach back into the main checkout from an isolated worktree at all (everything needed is already present in the worktree's own full checkout, and `origin/<ref>` history is accessible via the shared object store without touching the main checkout's working directory).
- **[anthropics/claude-code#46808](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/46808)** (closed/stale) — hooks can silently fail to fire in worktree contexts due to settings-resolution/watcher gaps. We hit a version of this ourselves while testing (this worktree's `.claude/` didn't exist when the session started, so the live watcher didn't pick up the hook until a fresh session/`/hooks` reload).
- **[anthropics/claude-code#29667](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/29667)** (closed/duplicate/stale) — independent report of the exact behavior this PR blocks: "it suddenly jumped out of the worktree and started making changes there... very dangerous behavior to existing code on the main repo." Confirms this is a real (if non-deterministic) model behavior, not something reliably preventable by CLAUDE.md instructions alone — which is why this is enforced via a hook rather than documentation.
- **[anthropics/claude-code#44557](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/44557)** (closed/duplicate) — plausible root cause for how the bad command gets composed in the first place: subagents can resolve file paths against the main repo root instead of the worktree even while pinned there.
- The destructive-ops warning hook is adapted from a published community hook: https://gist.github.com/yurukusa/98bd43c5d0d8a6ebbf2cf21bfc1e2907

## How the first hook works
Reads `cwd` and `tool_input.command` from the PreToolUse JSON payload. If `cwd` is inside `<repo-root>/.claude/worktrees/<name>/...`, it computes `<repo-root>` and checks whether the command references that root path *outside* of a worktree path, combined with any `git` token. If so, returns `permissionDecision: deny` with a reason explaining the fix (run the git command directly against the current worktree instead).

Scoped narrowly to `cd`/`git -C` + `git` commands specifically, not all main-checkout references, since:
- A background/isolated session's cwd auto-resets to the worktree after each Bash call, so a bare `cd <main-root>` alone (no chained command) can't cause lasting drift — the only real risk is a single compound command mixing `cd`+`git`.
- Non-git commands referencing the main checkout (e.g. reading a file for comparison) aren't the risk this addresses.

## How the second hook works
Runs `git rev-parse --git-dir` in the command's actual working directory (more portable than string-matching `.claude/worktrees/`, since it works for worktrees created any way, not just via `EnterWorktree`). If the result contains `worktrees` and the command matches a destructive git pattern, it returns a `systemMessage` + `additionalContext` warning — non-blocking, since these operations are often intentional within the current worktree; the risk is specifically the shared-object-store side effect.

## Test plan
- [x] Pipe-tested both hook commands against multiple scenarios each (real-world bad example, worktree-local benign commands, main-root reference without git, non-worktree session, `git -C` form, reference to a *different* worktree, destructive ops in/out of worktree context) — all matched expected allow/deny/warn.
- [x] Validated `.claude/settings.json` JSON syntax via `jq -e` after each change.
- [x] Live-fire verified in a fresh session started with cwd directly inside this worktree (sidesteps the watcher-registration gap from #46808): all 4 first-hook scenarios (block cd+git, block git -C, allow plain git, allow cd+non-git) behaved exactly as expected.
- [x] Live-fire verified the second hook in the current session after the watcher caught up: `git reset` (harmless, no `--hard`) correctly triggered the hook path without blocking execution.

author: petyok
body:
## The recurring problem

macOS CI has flaked ~repeatedly on the `notify`/FSEvents-backed watcher tests, and every previous fix was a "bump the timeout" band-aid (`462801b test(watcher): harden debounce test for slow macOS FSEvents`, `0246caa`, ...). It never converged: this week both `spawn_config_watcher_emits_after_write` and `debounce_coalesces_rapid_writes` failed even with a 60s bound (`expected exactly one debounced event within 60s`).

## Root cause

These two tests assert on **real FSEvents delivery** for a temp file. On the macOS CI sandbox FSEvents delivery is non-deterministic (events arrive seconds late or not at all). That's a property of the OS + third-party `notify` crate we don't own, so no timeout tuning makes it reliable.

## Fix

Gate the two real-delivery tests behind `#[cfg_attr(target_os = "macos", ignore = "...")]`:

- they still **compile** on every platform (no bitrot),
- they still **run on Linux** (inotify — deterministic, actually catches regressions in our watcher wiring + debounce logic),
- macOS CI **skips** them, so the FSEvents timing lottery can't block PRs anymore.

Run locally on macOS with `cargo test -- --ignored`.

`spawn_config_watcher_missing_path_errors` (no FS events, pure error path) still runs everywhere.

Scope: this is the last real-FS/timing offender on macOS (the `$HOME` race was fixed structurally in #28), so the macOS job becomes deterministic after this.

Verified on Linux: `cargo test --lib watcher` -> 3 passed, 0 ignored; `cargo fmt --check` clean.

body:
## Problem

Both night measurement rolls (run_689c2bb32a14, run_57807c247bb4) reported overstated criteria coverage: `criteria_total` was derived from whichever check rows happened to carry criterion ids, so a run that died early reported 2/3 where the truth against the seeded contract (art_97864f4daa5f, 6 criteria) was 2/6. Coverage inflated exactly when the run failed early — the case where the honest number matters most.

## Fix

- `aggregate_verification()` gains `contract_criteria` (keyword, default empty): when supplied, `criteria_total = contract ∪ observed` — every declared criterion counts in the denominator whether or not its checks dispatched; rogue evidence ids are never dropped.
- `RunCompletion.finalize()` accepts the bind-mode contract; `_aggregate_verification` extracts `criterion_ids()`.
- The executor threads the contract it already loads for bind mode into the finalize call (pre-initialized so an early-failing run stays safe).
- Author mode (no contract) is byte-identical to before.

- Pure layer: full-denominator with partial evidence (2/6 not 2/3), author-mode unchanged, rogue-id union, zero-evidence 0/m (would each have caught the shipped bug).

author: physercoe
body:
Closes #334.

## Summary
Newer ACP daemons — `kimi-code-ts` (ADR-054 D6), added in #335 — report per-session model/mode state via a `configOptions` select array in the `session/new` reply instead of the legacy `modes`/`models` blocks. `ACPDriver` only parsed the legacy shape, so the mode/model picker never hydrated for these engines even though `session/set_model` works on the wire (the gap #334 documents).

## Change
New `translateConfigOptions(raw)` maps the `configOptions` array into the **same** mode/model list shape the legacy path already produces — mode entries keyed by `id`, model entries by `modelId` (both carrying `name`) — so the existing id-set caching + synthetic initial-state system event downstream in `Start` consumes either shape unchanged.

- **Shape-driven + engine-neutral** (per the issue's rationale): translates whichever shape arrives; any future ACP adopter (gemini-cli/codex) benefits with no further work.
- **No regression** (acceptance #3): filled *per category*, only when the legacy field is absent, so a legacy-shaped reply produces byte-identical output. The existing `TestACPDriver_EmitsInitialModeModelSystemEvent` / `SetModelDispatch` / `SetModelDispatch_KimiShape` tests stay green.
- **`thought_level`** (acceptance #4, out of scope): no mobile picker yet, so its current value rides the initial-state event under a distinct `thoughtLevel` key for forensics only — never folded into the mode/model reducer.
- **`config_option_update`** mid-session notifications fold into the same `system`-event path as `current_mode_update` / `current_model_update`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] configOptions → initial mode/model state event, picker renders with current model preselected (`currentModeId`/`currentModelId` set from `currentValue`).
- [x] `set_model` validates against the cached list populated from configOptions (integration test round-trips it).
- [x] No regression for gemini-cli / Python kimi-code — legacy tests byte-identical.
- [x] `session/load` empty/`{}` carryover unaffected (W7/W7c path untouched; #335's `TestSessions_ResumeThreadsACPCursor_KimiCodeTS` covers the kimi-code-ts resume case).

## Tests
- `TestTranslateConfigOptions` — unit; the live kimi-code 0.27.0 capture from #334 plus malformed JSON, no-configOptions, and empty-value drop.
- `TestACPDriver_ConfigOptionsHydratesModeModelState` — integration; asserts the synthesized system event's current ids + `thoughtLevel` forensics field + a `set_model` round-trip against the configOptions-advertised model.

author: nirradi
body:
Implements task 1.4b from `stream-1-plan.md`.

The product decision is **60 days ahead, no booking in the past**. The calendar will also disable out-of-range navigation, but the backend must be authoritative — the API has to reject an out-of-range booking that doesn't come from our UI.

## Changes

- `BOOKING_HORIZON_DAYS = 60` module constant; the denial message derives the number from it.
- `_check_not_in_the_past` and `_check_within_horizon`, following the existing `_check_*` pattern.
- `Context` gains an injectable `now`, defaulting to the current UTC instant, so the time-relative rules stay pure functions of `(request, context)` and tests pin the clock instead of racing it. No existing call site changes.

## Rule ordering

The date rules run **before** duration and availability. `evaluate` short-circuits on the first denial, so ordering decides which single message a user sees. Telling someone to shorten a 3-hour booking that sits 90 days out would send them to fix the one thing that isn't the problem — they'd shorten it, resubmit, and be refused again.

## Boundaries

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Starts exactly now | allowed |
| 1 minute in the past | denied |
| Exactly 60 days ahead | allowed |
| 60 days + 1 minute | denied |
| 3h booking 90 days out | denied citing the **date**, not the duration |

## Negative controls

Both boundary tests were verified non-vacuous:

- Flipping the horizon bound `>` to `>=` fails `test_booking_exactly_at_the_horizon_is_allowed`.
- Flipping the past bound `<` to `<=` fails `test_booking_starting_now_is_allowed`.

71 tests pass; `black --check` and `flake8` clean.

body:
Consumer half of the group-signal sender-forgery fix (Crit) + the silent auto-join fix (High), from the app security review.

## Repin
Bumps `@forgesworn/roost-kit` to **504cff8** (roost-kit#4), where `giftUnwrap` now verifies the seal signature + binds `rumor.pubkey===seal.pubkey`, so `e.pubkey` (the rumor author) is **authenticated**.

## Sender-auth (Critical)
Binds every content-embedded actor field to the authenticated sender in `onIncoming`: `buzz.from`, `lost.by`, `findping.from`, `disband.by` must equal `e.pubkey` (mirrors the existing `joined` guard). ## Auto-join (High)
`joinFromLink` now **always** routes through the join-confirmation screen (handle pre-filled), even for onboarded users — a tapped/scanned `#join=` link or QR can no longer silently enrol someone and publish their real pubkey into an attacker's circle.

author: 7nohe
body:
## Summary

Post-1.0 backlog item (security): the OAuth manager stored a caller-supplied `redirectTo` in the state payload and handed it back verbatim — an app following the natural pattern (`/auth/github?redirectTo=...` → redirect after login) was an open-redirect phishing vector. It was also awkward to do correctly: `user()` never returned the stored `redirectTo` at all.

- **Sanitize at both ends**: `createOAuthState` drops unsafe values before storing; `verifyOAuthState` re-sanitizes on the way out (covers custom stores and states persisted before an allowlist change).
- **Rules**: app-relative paths (`/settings`) always pass; absolute URLs only when the host is in the new `stateConfig.allowedRedirectHosts` allowlist (`*.example.com` wildcards supported); protocol-relative (`//evil.com`), backslash variants (`/\evil.com`), `javascript:`/`data:` and other non-http schemes are dropped to `undefined`.
- **New API**: `OAuthManager.handleCallback(provider, { code, state })` returns `{ profile, redirectTo }` with the sanitized target (`user()` now delegates to it); `sanitizeOAuthRedirect()` exported for custom flows.
- **Scaffold**: `guren add oauth` controller template now demonstrates the safe round-trip (`?redirectTo=` in `redirectToProvider`, `handleCallback` + fallback in `callback`).
- **Docs (en/ja)**: new "Post-login redirect" section; also fixes the stale `redirect` action name in the route-flow example (the scaffold has used `redirectToProvider` for a while).
- `@guren/server` + `@guren/cli` minor changesets included (stacks on pending 1.3.0 items).

## Verification

- 8 new tests: `sanitizeOAuthRedirect` matrix (relative, protocol-relative, backslash, schemes, allowlist + wildcard, suffix-spoof), intake/outlet sanitization through the state store, `handleCallback` end-to-end with mocked provider, `allowedRedirectHosts` via `stateConfig`.

body:
**The hymnal is complete: 920 entries, 1–920.** (683 does not exist in the printed hymnal.)

## Worship aids 696–920
`scripts/import-worship-aids.mjs` fills the section from the supplied `sdah_hymns_full.json`, leaving the verified 1–695 untouched. 225 entries in the hymnal's own groupings:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Scripture Songs & Readings | 149 |
| Call to Worship | 36 |
| Words of Assurance | 13 |
| Offertory Sentences | 13 |
| Benedictions | 14 |

The source needed real cleaning, all handled:

- **multi-book references** — "Ecclesiastes 12, Proverbs 20, Psalm 119, Proverbs 3, and Psalm 103, NIV"
- **semicolon references** — "Psalm 122:1; 118:24, RSV"
- **emphasis brackets split across lines** — `Let [` / `the redeemed` / `] thank the Lord` rejoined into one line
- **stray verse numbers** left loose in the body

Where a reading has no title, the scripture reference names it the way the printed hymnal does — and is then not repeated underneath.

## Accompaniment now follows the words
A hymn MIDI holds the tune **once**, because every verse is sung to the same music. Playing it once and stopping left singers stranded after verse 1 — which is what you were hearing.

The tune now **repeats once per verse**. Repeats are counted in `playHymn` rather than handed to the sequencer, so we control exactly when it stops. Refrains aren't counted: the tune already covers the refrain, since it's sung after each verse rather than on its own.

The play button also shows a live counter (`2/5`) so singers can see which verse the music is on.

This is why MP3s aren't needed — the tune is identical every verse, so repeating it gives the same result as a full-length recording, at ~8 KB instead of several MB per hymn.

author: braboj
body:
Closes #1443

## Problem

`deploy.yml` runs `npm run validate` unconditionally on every push to `main`. Its `test` step (`vitest run --coverage`) reads `docs/optical-specs/**` for the data-integrity invariants in `src/data/mtf-readings.test.ts` (`dirsWithLog`, directory-name, same-product).

The PR `build` job runs the same `validate` but is gated on the `code` path-filter, which **omits `docs/optical-specs/**`**. PR #1441 added only `tools/**` + a `digitization-log.md`, so `build` was skipped, the vitest suite never ran on the PR, it merged green, and the `main` deploy then failed on that exact test — a failure notification instead of a gate (incident hotfixed by #1442).

## Fix

Add a dedicated always-run `test` job (no path filter) that runs `npm run test`, and wire it into the `gate` aggregator. This mirrors the deploy's test step exactly as the `format` job (ADR-076) mirrors Prettier — enumeration-free, so no path list to keep in sync as tests read new tracked dirs.

`build`, `lighthouse`, `pytest`, and `staleness` keep their (correct) path filters. Follows `quality-gates.md` "PR gate MUST mirror the deploy gate" and "Mirror cross-cutting checks with an always-run job".

## Verification

Ran the always-run job's command locally:

- Baseline `npx vitest run src/data/mtf-readings.test.ts` → **18 passed**.

## Summary

No smoke check exercised full-text search at all. Requested after deploying #660 (extracted the Xapian binding into the standalone `go-xapian` module) to verify the module swap didn't break FTS at runtime — but the gap applies generally: the whole delivery→index→search pipeline had zero live coverage before this.

## What

`checkFTS(user, pass)`:
1. Delivers a message via LMTP with a unique marker in both body and subject.
2. Polls `SEARCH BODY <marker>` until the autoindex worker picks it up (bounded by `-timeout * 3`).
3. Verifies `SEARCH TEXT`, `SEARCH HEADER SUBJECT`, and `SEARCH FROM` all find it too.
4. Negative control: a token that was never delivered must return zero matches — catches a stuck/stale index that would otherwise silently return everything.

Gated behind `-fts-user`/`-fts-pass`, same enablement pattern as the existing `-quota-user`/`-acl-user` checks.

author: metaforismo
body:
Closes #111383

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators rescheduling an active one-shot cron job would lose the future invocation when the original run completed. A successful `deleteAfterRun` job was deleted, while a retained one-shot was disabled, even though its schedule had moved into the future.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron completion now compares the admitted job's normalized scheduling inputs with the current stored row. When an in-flight edit owns a different schedule, the completed run still records its run and delivery metadata but cannot delete, disable, retry, advance, or disarm the edited schedule. The same ownership rule covers scheduled and manual runs.

## User Impact

Operators and agents can reschedule a running one-shot job without the completed invocation silently removing or disabling the new future run. The future schedule remains durable across Gateway restart.

## Evidence

- Regression first reproduced on current `main`: `deleteAfterRun=true` removed the job; `deleteAfterRun=false` left it disabled with no `nextRunAtMs`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.read-ops-nonblocking.test.ts`: 6/6 passed, including both delete policies, restart persistence, and the manual-run sibling path.
- `pnpm test:changed -- src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/ops.ts src/cron/service.read-ops-nonblocking.test.ts`: 57/57 passed.
- Expanded cron proof (`schedule-identity`, `service.read-ops-nonblocking`, `ops.run-admission`, `ops.regression`, `timer.regression`, `service.trigger-eval`): 131/131 passed.
- Hosted CI exposed an `on-exit` schedule-identity gap in the first revision. The follow-up adds normalized identity for its command and working directory; the exact failing regression and the broader 131-test cron suite now pass locally.
- Isolated Gateway proof on Node 24.15.0: a real command payload wrote `started-2`, ran for 30 seconds, and was rescheduled by CLI to `+5m` while `status=running`. After it wrote `done-2`, `cron list` showed the same job with `enabled=true`, the future `at` timestamp, `lastStatus=ok`, and `lastDurationMs=30034`. The same state survived a clean Gateway restart.
- `pnpm check:changed -- ...`: formatting, repository guards, plugin boundaries, and core typecheck passed. The local core-test typecheck was interrupted after 846 seconds without diagnostics; hosted CI remains the authoritative full typecheck.
- Full `pnpm build` reached `tsdown-unified` but the host had only 114 MiB free and failed with `ENOSPC`; source CLI builds completed successfully and powered the live Gateway proof.

AI-assisted: yes. Codex helped implement and validate this change; I reviewed the diff and understand the code.

author: xertox1234
body:
## What

The mutating-git branch of `git-safety.sh` resolved a `git` command's effective repo (the `-C <path>` override) with a greedy, quote-blind extraction:

```bash
C_TARGET=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | tr -d '\042\047' \
  | sed -nE 's/.*git[[:space:]]+-C[[:space:]]+([^[:space:]]+).*/\1/p' | head -1)
```

`tr -d` deletes quote **chars** but keeps their **content**, and `.*git…-C` matches the **last** `git -C` anywhere in the string. So a commit **message** that merely mentions `git -C <path>` was read as a real `-C` override.

## Why it matters — the bug is bidirectional

| Scenario | cwd | Old | Want |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git commit -m "see git -C <MAIN> commit"` | worktree | **DENY** (false) | ALLOW |
| `git -C <MAIN> commit -m "see git -C <WT>"` | worktree | **ALLOW** (bypass) | DENY |
| `git -C <WT> commit -m "see git -C <MAIN>"` | main | **DENY** (false) | ALLOW |
| `git commit -m "ref git -C <WT>"` | main | **ALLOW** (bypass) | DENY |

- **main-path decoy → false-DENY:** a fabricated violation blocks legitimate work.
- **worktree-path decoy → BYPASS (false-negative):** the greedy last-match **substitutes** the registered-worktree path from the message for the real target, laundering a genuine main-checkout mutation past the contract. Row 4 is exactly the `git commit` in the main checkout that the contract exists to deny.

The bypass direction was **not** in the original CONFIRMED probe (which only caught the false-DENY) — the pre-write advisor pass flagged it, and building the 2×2 truth table made it a first-class RED test.

## The fix

Replace the greedy strip with a role-aware tokenizer `git_c_target` — the sibling of `emit_write_targets` shipped in #664. It emits **only the first command-position `git`'s `-C` argument**: the `-C` **flag** must be **unquoted** (so a `-C` buried in a quoted `-m` message — one atomic token — is never mined), but the `-C` **value** may still be quoted, so `git -C '<main>' commit` still DENYs. Env-assignment recognition is taint-tolerant; `git`/`-C` recognition is taint-strict.

## Tests

`test-git-safety.sh`: 4 new assertions forming a 2×2 (`{real -C present?}` × `{message decoys main | worktree}`) — main-decoy → must-ALLOW, worktree-decoy → must-DENY. **All 4 RED before, 57/57 green after.** Every pre-existing `-C` guard preserved. Full 29-suite hook sweep green.

## Review outcome (code-reviewer + security-auditor)

A post-implementation review confirmed the tokenizer is **correct and strictly-improving** — it closes the bidirectional message-decoy bug and introduces **no new bypass** (the extractor line is the only behavior change; the split + regex are byte-identical on `main`).

The review also **corrected a false claim** in the first draft of this PR: I had documented the unchanged `tr ';|&'` split residual as "false-positive only, never a false-negative." **That is wrong.** A split metachar *after* the verb (in a `-m` message) is FP-only, but one *before* the verb (inside a `-c name=value` global option) fractures the segment and lets a real main mutation through — confirmed against the live hook:

```
git -C <MAIN> -c core.pager='a;b' commit -m x   →  ALLOW  (should DENY)
```

This bypass — and its siblings (chained `-C`, quoted `-C` flag, glued `-C<path>`, env-value-with-space) — are **pre-existing** (they live in the quote-blind regex/split "front door" upstream of the extractor, unchanged by this PR). The second commit here corrects the documentation to stop asserting a false safety property; the actual fixes are tracked for their own clean, fully-tested landing in `todos/P2-2026-07-19-git-safety-frontdoor-quote-aware-segmentation.md` (never-delegate, `human_led`).

**Scope of this PR:** the `-C` *extraction* fix + honest documentation. It does not claim to close the front-door bypasses.

Closes the `-C` acceptance criterion of `todos/P2-2026-07-18-port-sibling-hooks-to-shared-cmd-detect.md`.

author: patrickrose
body:
Fixes #782.

## Problem

When a game reaches its turn limit it never transitions to a terminal state. The server correctly refuses to advance past the limit (`hasFinished()` is `false` there), so `phaseEnd` stays `0` and `GameWrapper` collapses its poll interval to **100ms (~10 req/s) per device for the rest of the event** — a self-inflicted DDoS on the API from every screen showing "GAME COMPLETE".

Two related symptoms from the same root cause:
- The 100ms collapse also happened **transiently at every phase boundary** (all countdowns hit `0` together → synchronised burst).
- Because `delay` was derived from `phaseEnd` and the local countdown decremented it every second, `useInterval`'s effect reset before it could fire in the final 5s → **no server sync in the last 5s, then a synchronised stampede at `0`**.

## Fix

The change is entirely client-side in `GameWrapper.tsx` — the server behaviour (not advancing past the limit) is correct; the bug was deriving the poll cadence from `phaseEnd`.

- **Derive a `finished` flag** from `atTurnLimit(turnNumber, phase, setupInformation)` so the client can tell a genuinely finished game apart from a momentary phase boundary. No server type or DB migration needed — the client already has both the API response and `setupInformation`.
- **Decouple the poll cadence from the live countdown:** poll at a steady 5s while active, back off to 30s once the game is finished or paused, and floor the interval at 1s.
- **Add a stable per-device jitter factor** so devices don't poll in lockstep and stampede the API at boundaries.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint` — clean
- `npx jest` — 545/545 pass

author: johnkirwan
body:
## Summary

Fixes the High-Priority TODO item **"Clear stale analysis state after every upload attempt."**

In the Shiny app's headings mode, a failed file upload used to leave the previous analysis (e.g. the example headings) alive. Because `go2`/`go3` inferred "example headings already loaded → jump to Results" from the fragile condition `raw_hd == NULL && hd != NULL`, a failed parse satisfied exactly that condition — so clicking **Next**/**Analyse** displayed the stale example's results as if they belonged to the file just selected.

## Changes (`inst/app/app.R`)

- **(A) Clear-then-commit upload observer** — the headings-mode file-upload handler now clears prior `hd`/`hd_map`/`method`/`ts`/`error` (and resets `step`) *before* reading, and commits `rv$raw_hd` only from the read's return value (`NULL` on failure). A failed upload can no longer leave stale state behind.
- **(B) Source-gated fast-path** — the "example headings → Results" shortcut in both `go2` and `go3` now fires only when `rv$source == "example"`, making the invariant structural rather than a NULL-coincidence.

## Tests

New `tests/testthat/test-app-stale-state.R` (3 `testServer` regressions):
1. A failed headings upload clears the prior example analysis and **Next** does not show stale Results.
2. The source guard leaves the legitimate example fast-path intact (still reaches Results).
3. A successful re-upload replaces prior example state and commits the new data.

`[ FAIL 0 | PASS 17 ]` locally (5 unrelated ggplot rendering warnings). Full suite left to CI.

## Reviews

Per-task reviews and a final whole-branch review (opus) all returned 0 Critical/Important findings. One non-blocking Minor: the `go2`/`go3` handlers are symmetric but each failure/positive path is asserted on only one of the two.

author: dbressler85
body:
Wires the data MFL doesn't publish — dynasty values, player age, and waiver trends — via two free, no-key providers.

## Providers
- **FantasyCalc** → dynasty values (normalized to 0–100) + age + overall rank. Its player objects carry **both `mflId` and `sleeperId`**, so values join to our MFL ids directly *and* give a Sleeper→MFL crosswalk for free.
- **Sleeper** → trending adds (waiver heat), keyed by `sleeperId`, mapped to MFL via that crosswalk.
- **News** skipped by choice (no solid free source).

## Design
- New `lib/enrichment.js` fetches both on a **6h in-memory TTL**, degrades to nulls if a provider is down (app behaves exactly as before), and never blocks an MFL call.
- `snapshot()` exposes `value/age/trend/ownership/rank` with synchronous lookups; in **demo it delegates to the fixtures**, so demo behavior is unchanged.
- Swapped in everywhere services used `demo.dynasty/ownership/trend`: player hub (search, rankings incl. **Value/Trending/Rookies**, profile), roster asset values, waiver board / best-available / bid suggestions.
- Bonus fix: `best-available` returned empty in live — now uses live free agents.

**Ownership %** stays null — no free site-wide source exists; trend is the honest heat signal.

## Verification
- `npm run smoke` passes (demo unchanged).
- Provider logic verified against stubbed responses: value normalization (9500→100, 4750→50, 950→10), age/rank mapping, and the Sleeper→MFL trend crosswalk.
- End-to-end through the player profile: value 100, age 24, trend 777, dynasty rank recomputed.

author: nghiacc
body: ## Summary Cancel then re-Offer was racing the server baton lock. **Why cancel exists (even though PoW is client-side):** hashing the nonce is on-device, but `/api/challenge` still **reserves** the mint baton tip + fee UTXO and binds the memorial note into the sighash. Only one open challenge is allowed globally so two phones don’t get the same UTXO. Cancel (or 15‑min TTL) frees that reservation for the next miner. **Bug:** Cancel fired `/api/cancel` without awaiting, and AbortError cleanup released `challengeIdRef.current` — which could be a *newer* offer — leaving the baton locked or cancelling the wrong challenge. ## Changes - Await cancel before treating the UI as idle; clear the local challenge id synchronously - Abort/error paths only release **this** offer’s challenge id - Offer generation guard so a stale `finally` cannot reset a newer mine - Serialize `/api/cancel` on the same chain lock as challenge/submit - Clearer error when another device holds the baton ## Deploy Merge → web CI. On Contabo: `git pull` + restart mint-api. ## Test plan - [ ] Start mine → Cancel → Offer again immediately (should get a new challenge) - [ ] Start mine → Cancel → wait → Offer (same) - [ ] Two devices: one mining → other Offer sees the “another device” message until cancel/TTL

author: wigy
body:
## Summary

Implements `le-pending-effects-parity.test.ts` (previously a lone `test.todo('behavioral tests')`) and fixes the card-data gap it exists to guard.

Four corruption **pending-effects** hazards are printed in both **The Wizards (TW)** and **The Lidless Eye (LE)**. Three of the four pairs had effects implemented on only *one* printing, while the sibling carried an empty `effects: []` — an **inert card that silently does nothing when played**:

| Card | Empty printing | Ported from (certified) |
|------|----------------|--------------------------|
| Despair of the Heart | `le-109` | `tw-27` |
| Greed | `tw-42` | `le-113` |
| Weariness of the Heart | `tw-111` | `le-149` |
| Lure of the Senses | — (already matched) | — |

## Why porting is safe
- Both printings of each card have **identical authoritative text** (verified against `data/cards.json`).
- **No engine code branches on these card ids** (grep: 0 refs) — behavior is driven entirely by the `effects` array, so an identical effects array yields identical behavior.
- The source printing of each is **certified and has passing card tests**, so the ported printing inherits already-verified behavior.

`le-109` and `tw-111` also gained the matching `keywords: ["corruption"]`; `le-109` gained `removalNumber: 4`, matching its sibling.

## The test
For each of the four pairs, asserts:
- effect arrays are identical (⇒ identical engine behavior),
- neither printing is inert (empty effects — the guarded regression),
- structural fields match (`cardType`, `eventType`, `unique`, `keywords`).

## Verification
- `npm run build` — clean
- Parity test + sibling card tests (`tw-27`, `le-113`, `le-149`) + `rule-10.19`/`rule-10.38` — **40 passing**
- Full `10-corruption-influence-endgame` rules suite — **114 passing**, no failures

author: gaspareu
body:
## Contexte

Le connecteur Cookidoo reposait sur un contrat d'API **non vérifié par l'écriture** : les formats
avaient été déduits de lectures et d'un projet open-source tiers. Cette branche confronte chaque
élément du contrat à l'API réelle, via des **sondes d'écriture** sur un compte Cookidoo (création,
PATCH, upload d'image, suppression, relecture), puis corrige ce que ces sondes ont démenti.

Trois affirmations du contrat précédent étaient fausses :

| Affirmation | Réalité mesurée |
|---|---|
| « Deux schémas : écriture ≠ lecture » | Une seule ressource, **deux vues** sélectionnées par l'en-tête `Accept`. Avec `application/json`, les annotations sont simplement **invisibles**. |
| « `cookTime` est ignoré par Cookidoo » | Il est **persisté et relu** — c'était un artefact de la vue aplatie. |
| « L'accessoire n'a pas d'équivalent dans le payload » | `accessory` existe (`MODE:steaming`). |

## Changements

**`fix` — puissance du rissolage paramétrable**
`power` était figé à `"Intense"`. Ce champ pilote l'intention machine envoyée au TM7
(`"Intense"` → `HighTemperature_FullPower`, `"Gentle"` → `HighTemperature_MediumPower`) : **tous les
rissolages partaient à pleine puissance**, y compris ceux rédigés comme doux. Nouveau type
`Tm7Power` dans le référentiel TM7 (+ miroir front), exposé à l'IA via le schéma d'outil, la
validation Zod et le prompt. Défaut inchangé pour ne pas modifier les recettes existantes.

**`feat` — détection des étapes dégradées**
Cookidoo accepte une annotation invalide (mode inconnu, `manual`) en `200 OK`, la stocke, puis la
dégrade en simple texte à la conversion vers l'appareil — **sans aucune erreur HTTP**. C'est le seul
mode d'échec réellement silencieux de cette API. `findUnguidedSteps` relit la vue appareil
(`/device/recipes/{id}`) après l'export et remonte un warning `steps_not_guided` pour toute étape
retombée en `CustomerText`. Contrôle best-effort : son échec n'invalide pas l'export.

Les `GET` du client demandent désormais la vue complète (`customer-recipe.full+json`) — sans elle,
toute relecture est trompeuse.

**`docs` — contrat réécrit**
`docs/COOKIDOO-CONTRAT.md` : chaque élément est adossé à une requête réelle, avec un journal des
sondes. Les hypothèses sur `custom_coordinates`, le renommage et le PATCH combiné sont levées.
La correspondance annotation → intention machine est documentée.

## Validation

```
deno test --allow-net --allow-env supabase/functions/_shared/   141 passed, 0 failed
npm run test:run                                                433 passed (54 fichiers)
npm run build                                                   OK (typecheck inclus)
```

8 tests ajoutés (3 mapper, 5 client), écrits avant le code.

> Note : sans `--allow-env`, 10 tests Deno préexistants échouent (`ai-config`, `decrypt-keys`) —
> sans rapport avec cette branche, vérifié par `git stash`. La commande de `CLAUDE.md` mériterait
> d'être complétée.

## Points d'attention

- [ ] **Déploiement** : `export-recipe-cookidoo` et `home-assistant` ne changent en prod qu'au merge (CI).
- [ ] **Migration** `cookidoo_recipe_id` non appliquée tant que la branche n'est pas mergée → anti-doublon inactif.
- [ ] **`isImageOwnedByUser`** : le code envoie `false`, la sonde a validé `true`. Les deux fonctionnent,
      seule la déclaration de propriété change. Décision produit, laissée en l'état et documentée.

## Reste ouvert

Quatre modes (`blend`, `turbo`, `warm_up`, `rice_cooker`) sont annoncés par un projet tiers et le
schéma de validation comporte bien 8 variantes de `MODE`, dont 4 confirmées. Testables via la vue
appareil, sans matériel.

body:
## Problem

Codex model sync calls `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models?client_version=1.0.0`. That endpoint filters the returned catalog by `minimal_client_version` against whatever `client_version` the caller sends, and codex CLI's own manifest (`openai/codex` `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json`) already requires `0.144.0` for its newest models. `1.0.0` predates that by a wide margin, so the request can come back a clean 200 with the gated entries just missing, no error to react to.

We hit this in our own implementation of the same call: a real ChatGPT Plus account got a 200 with an empty model list at `client_version=0.21.0`, and the list populated once we bumped to a current release.

There's also no fallback in the generic sync branch this entry runs through (`route.js` ~519-547): a 200 with zero models is returned to the client as-is, with no warning field, nothing to signal that something's off.

## Fix

- Bump `client_version` to `0.144.6` (current stable, comfortably above the `0.144.0` gate) via a named constant with a comment explaining the gating, so it doesn't quietly go stale again.
- Add the `originator: codex_cli_rs` header. Every other codex call site in this codebase already sends it (`open-sse/providers/registry/codex.js`, `open-sse/handlers/imageProviders/codex.js`, `open-sse/services/usage/codex.js`), just not this one.
- Move the codex entry onto the existing `buildOAuthResolver` helper, the same pattern `gemini-cli` and `grok-cli` already use. `refreshCodexToken` was already implemented and used elsewhere (the general provider refresh table in `open-sse/services/tokenRefresh.js`), just never wired into model sync, so codex model listing never retried on an expired token the way the other OAuth providers do. This also means a genuinely empty response now comes back with a `warning` field instead of a silent empty array.

## Scope

Kept this to the codex entry only. I looked at also wiring a static-catalog fallback for a fully-empty result (like `kimchi`/`grok-cli` do), but there's no static codex catalog in `open-sse/config/providerModels.js` to fall back to, and I didn't want to guess at a model list. Happy to follow up separately if that's wanted.

## Checks

- `bunx eslint "src/app/api/providers/[id]/models/route.js"` clean.
- Skipped the test suite: `vitest` isn't a declared dependency and there's no `test` script in `package.json`, even though `tests/unit/*.test.js` exists, so I couldn't run it against a fresh clone.

Reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/refs/heads/main/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json

author: lhgravendeel
body:
The advisory lock manager had four verified bugs:

1. The non-try forms (pg_advisory_lock, pg_advisory_lock_shared, and the xact variants) discarded the result of a try-acquire and returned success without holding the lock; pg_advisory_xact_lock even registered the key for transaction-end release despite the failed acquisition. They now block until the lock is grantable, waiting on a Database-level monitor that every release path notifies, honoring lock_timeout (55P03) with a 30s safety cap, and detecting deadlocks between waiters (40P01, deterministic highest-pid victim) via the wait-for graph shared with row-lock waits.

2. Acquisitions were not reference-counted (a Set of holder sessions), so re-acquire was a no-op and one unlock released everything. Holds are now counted per (session, key, mode, ownership); each successful lock needs a matching unlock and surplus unlocks return false.

3. Shared vs exclusive mode was tracked per-key, letting pg_advisory_unlock_shared release an exclusive lock. Modes now have proper conflict semantics (shared coexists with shared; exclusive excludes others; a session may stack both modes) and an unlock only releases a hold of its own mode.

4. The two-int form shared a keyspace with the single-bigint form. The forms now live in distinct keyspaces like PG (objsubid 1 vs 2), and pg_locks splits the key into classid/objid with the correct mode (ExclusiveLock/ShareLock) per hold.

Also: transaction-level holds are released at COMMIT, ROLLBACK, and PREPARE TRANSACTION but are not releasable via pg_advisory_unlock; session disconnect now releases all advisory holds; and the previously missing pg_try_advisory_xact_lock_shared function is supported.

author: thejhyefactor
body:
Hey, I had a look at #1736 and traced one current path that can still leave a pull stuck on its final part.

The existing inactivity monitor only started its timeout after `blobDownloadPart.Write` recorded some data. If a range request connected but never delivered its first body byte, `lastUpdated` stayed zero and the monitor skipped that attempt forever. The same monitor also polled for completion once per second, so a finished chunk waited for the next tick before returning.

Prior art: #15716 identified the same first-byte gap and was closed unmerged without review. This PR keeps that core behaviour, but uses a per-attempt start time instead of overwriting the shared progress timestamp, signals completed transfers immediately, and adds benchmark plus race-tested coverage for both paths.

### What changed

- Start the inactivity window when each range attempt begins, then move it forward whenever bytes arrive.
- Signal the monitor as soon as the transfer goroutine exits instead of polling for completion.
- Keep the existing 30-second production stall threshold and retry behaviour.
- Add regression coverage for a connection that sends headers but no body bytes, plus the completed-transfer path.

### Benchmark

Apple M4 (16 GB), macOS 26.5.2, Go 1.26.2, base `573386c3`, 10 samples:

| Completion path | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `BenchmarkDownloadChunkCompletion` | 1.001113 s/op | 689.5 µs/op | -99.93% (p=0.000, n=10) |
| Allocated bytes | 49.16 KiB/op | 52.06 KiB/op | no significant change (p=0.853) |
| Allocations | 211.5 allocs/op | 210.0 allocs/op | no significant change (p=0.853) |

Commands:

```sh
go test ./server -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkDownloadChunkCompletion$' -benchmem -benchtime=1x -count=10
benchstat before.txt after.txt
```

This benchmark measures the completion/finalization wait after a local 1 MiB transfer. It isn't a claim that internet bandwidth is 1,500× faster; it shows the fixed polling tail is gone. In a real multipart pull, that removes up to one monitor tick after the last or retried part finishes.

I also captured CPU and allocation profiles over a two-second run. CPU time is dominated by the expected socket/syscall path, and the monitor doesn't appear as a hotspot.

### Validation

- `go test ./server -count=1`
- `go test ./server -run '^TestDownloadChunk' -count=50`
- `go test -race ./server -run '^TestDownloadChunk' -count=20`
- `go mod tidy -diff`
- `git diff --check`

I ran `go test ./... -count=1` as well. The server and the rest of the buildable Go packages passed, but the command exits non-zero in this fresh clone because `app/ui/app.go` embeds `app/dist`, which isn't present without the separate UI build step.

Related to #1736.

author: jason-easyazz
body:
Phase 2 / enrollment UX for the panel identity plan — built to Jason's spec after the first enrollment attempt required following chat instructions while standing at the panel.

## What
`scripts/setup/zoe_enroll_flow.py`, run on the panel Pi:
- **Zoe speaks every step** from the panel (server TTS → aplay, espeak fallback), confirms each capture, retries with corrective guidance.
- **Face mode**: all instructions up front, then one **silent 12-second recording** segmented into front/left/right windows; best detector hit per window is embedded and enrolled (consent=true, frames discarded). Silent + single-session by necessity: the Jabra PanaCast shares the Pi's USB power budget with the Jabra speaker — TTS playback during video streaming repeatedly browned the camera off the bus (physical replug required). The module never forces 720p for the same reason.
- **Voice mode**: three spoken-prompted phrases recorded via arecord (the zoe-voice daemon is stopped for the window — the Jabra can't hold two input streams — and restarted in a finally).

## Live-proven
Ran on the real panel: 3 face angles enrolled in one pass, then live-recognized at 0.49 (threshold 0.45) at room distance with `FACE_MIN_PX=36` (the default 60 px gate rejects real standing-distance faces on this 640×360 camera).

## Notes
- Ops doc: per-turn face checks in the daemon should wait for a powered USB hub on the panel — wake-word turns play audio, which is exactly the camera-brownout condition.
- No CI-runnable surface (hardware flow); `py_compile` + live panel run are the verification.

author: ehotwagner
body:
adr: ADR-0051 — a coordination room derives from the items it references (.github#1204)

Accept the #1204 proposal: adopt the "room" shape for the deadlock/negotiation
tail the per-item worker channel (ADR-0027 §5) does not serve. A room is an
issue a contended cluster references with a soft `Rooms: #R` body line — the
`Paths:`/`Blocked by:` declaration family — so membership and lifecycle derive
from the item link, not a roster or a sub-issue parent. The only code delta is
`inbox`'s subject set widening from "items I claim" to "items I claim ∪ rooms
those items reference"; `say`/`messages` are already subject-general.

Amends ADR-0027 §5 at both ends (header banner + inline §5 note + README
amendment row), per the adr-coherence bidirectional rule. This is a
coordination-protocol concept, not a system-shape change: no new repo,
boundary, coherent-set axis, or contract.

Implementation (the inbox subject-set delta, the Rooms: grammar/precedence,
and `room open`) is filed as a separate follow-up per the house rule that an
ADR carries effects, not assignments.

architecture-map: unaffected

Closes #1204.

author: labartist
body:
## Why Jul 17 still shows 3,083 steps

The max-merge from PR #47 protects a day from being *overwritten* with a lower number — but it can't recover data the server **never received**. If the Shortcut's last push on the 17th ran mid-afternoon at 3,083 steps, everything walked after that was never sent anywhere; when the 18th began, the 17th's row was frozen at the last value it ever heard.

That's a client-timing gap, and no pure server change can fix it retroactively. What the server *can* do is accept corrections the next day — Health still knows the 17th's true total on the 18th.

## The change

`POST /api/update` now takes an optional **`days`** array of closed-out totals:

```json
{ "steps": 500, "distance": 0.3, "calories": 9,
  "days": [ { "date": "2026-07-17", "steps": 8412, "distance": 6.1, "calories": 210 } ] }
```

Each entry merges into `vitals_history` by the same per-metric `Math.max` as live pushes — so it can raise or create a day, never lower one. Guardrails: max 7 entries processed, `YYYY-MM-DD` validated, future dates rejected (a typo'd date can't evict real rows from the 14-day window). The today-upsert was refactored onto the same `mergeDay` helper. Fully backward compatible — pushes without `days` behave exactly as before.

**With the Shortcut sending yesterday's totals on every push, each day self-heals one day later** — the early-last-push gap and any late Watch sync both get folded in automatically.

## Verification

Ran the real handler against a stubbed `@vercel/kv` through 15 scenarios — the 9 existing regressions (max-merge, tz keying, fallback, sort/cap) plus 6 new: back-fill heals an undercounted yesterday, cannot lower a healed day, creates missing past rows, keeps history sorted, ignores garbage/future entries, caps at 7. All pass; `node --check` clean.

## Shortcut change (needed to activate)

Add to the Shortcut, after the existing Health queries:
1. **Find Health Samples** for Steps / Walking+Running Distance / Active Energy with date filter **Yesterday** (or "Get numeric value of Health sample" for yesterday's date range).
2. **Format yesterday's date** as `yyyy-MM-dd`.
3. Add to the JSON body: `"days": [{"date": "<that date>", "steps": <…>, "distance": <…>, "calories": <…>}]`.

Once merged + deployed, one push with `"days": [{"date": "2026-07-17", …true totals…}]` also fixes the 17th's row immediately.
