body:
## Summary
Implements #1252 — turns the context graph from write-mostly into a queryable decision system: MADR-style decision lifecycle + supersession, DACI person edges, typed provenance/confidence, pgvector entity resolution (dedup) at capture time, and a hybrid-retrieval decision-package + semantic-search read path. Builds on the unified write path from #1251.

Technical decisions were pre-approved in the issue (2026-07-18): direct-Bedrock embeddings (Titan V2 @512, decoupled from the repository pipeline), threshold-banded non-destructive ER, `superseded_at`-only temporal depth, real `status`/`superseded_at` columns.

## Changes
- **Migration 115** (registered in `migrations.json`): nullable `status` + `superseded_at` on `graph_nodes` with a partial `(node_type, status)` index and a MADR CHECK constraint; a 512-dim pgvector `embedding` column + HNSW cosine index; seeds `GRAPH_EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID` (`amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`) with a re-embed-on-dimension-change caveat; backfills existing decision nodes to `accepted`.
- **`lib/graph/graph-embeddings.ts`** — self-contained direct-Bedrock embedding helper (IAM role, no new secret), decoupled from `lib/ai-helpers.ts`; fails open with an 8s timeout.
- **`lib/graph/entity-resolution.ts`** — threshold-banded dedup (`≥0.90` auto-reuse with `metadata.dedup` + warning / `0.75–0.90` candidates-in-warnings / `<0.75` silent create) for person/evidence/policy nodes; non-destructive (`SAME_AS` only); degrades gracefully when embeddings error (a decision is never lost).
- **`lib/graph/decision-retrieval.ts`** — depth-bounded, cycle-safe recursive-CTE decision package + pgvector semantic search.
- **Vocabulary** — `SUPERSEDED_BY`, `SAME_AS`, `CONSULTED`, `NOTIFIED` edges; `DECISION_STATUSES`; typed `GraphProvenance`/`GraphDedupMetadata` in `lib/db/types/jsonb`.
- **Capture service** — ER runs before the transaction; a `SUPERSEDED_BY` edge flips the old decision to `status=superseded` + `superseded_at` on all three channels (REST/MCP/chat); provenance written on every agent-authored node/edge; `consulted`/`notified`/`supersedes` payload fields.
- **Endpoints** — `GET /api/v1/graph/nodes/{id}/package`; `GET /api/v1/graph/nodes` gains semantic `q` (lexical fallback) + `status` filter ("current decision on X"); MCP `get_decision_graph` returns the package, `search_decisions` does semantic-with-fallback, `capture_decision` accepts the new fields. `embedding` is never returned (new `PublicGraphNode` type omits it from all reads/writes).
- **Docs** — `openapi.yaml`, `context-graph.md`, `decision-framework.md` updated.

## Verification (all green before opening)
- Build (`next build --webpack`): ✅
- Lint (`eslint .`): ✅ zero warnings in touched files (363 pre-existing warnings in untouched files are baseline)
- Typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`): ✅
- Tests (`bun run test:ci`, full suite): ✅ 2920 passed, 60 skipped, 0 failed (142 graph unit tests, incl. threshold-band fixtures with Bedrock mocked, graceful-degradation, supersession side effect, recursive-CTE package, semantic search)

### E2E flows
Three gated functional specs added — `decision-supersede`, `decision-package-retrieval`, `decision-semantic-search` (`tests/e2e/*.functional.spec.ts`, gated on `PLAYWRIGHT_AUTH_ENABLED`, same pattern as the existing `decision-rest-capture` spec). They compile and list under Playwright. **They cannot execute in this session's environment**: the local Docker postgres is stock `postgres:16.13` with no pgvector (`vector.control` absent), so migration 115's `vector(512)` column can't be applied and any graph capture 500s on the missing column. They run in a pgvector-provisioned authenticated environment (Aurora dev, where repository-search pgvector already lives). This is an external environment constraint, not a code defect.

## Evidence
_N/A — no UI surface. This is an API / MCP / schema feature; the only UI touched is the admin graph page, whose behavior is unchanged (retyped to `PublicGraphNode`, which renders identically)._

Closes #1252

---

## Self-review round (commit 3958f1b6) — 3 review agents (SQL, correctness, security+adversarial)

**SQL/migration review: clean.** Correctness fixes applied:
- Chat `commit_decision` now marks non-primary decision nodes (rejected alternatives) `status="rejected"` — they were stored `"accepted"`, indistinguishable from the adopted decision in `status=accepted` queries
- Semantic search honors `status`/`nodeClass` filters (converged with the pr-fix routine's independent fix; MCP `search_decisions` also passes `nodeClass` on the semantic branch now)
- Proposals with zero `decision` nodes are rejected instead of silently committing supporting nodes
- `SUPERSEDED_BY` edges must target the proposal's primary decision (guards the chat channel from retiring a real decision in favor of a rejected alternative)
- `clampDepth` floors fractional depths; caller-supplied `metadata.dedup` is stripped (never-spoofable, like provenance/completeness)

## Open questions — RESOLVED by owner (2026-07-19)

1. **Local pgvector** → approved and DONE. `docker-compose.dev.yml` uses `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` with a fresh `postgres_data_pgvector` volume (`eac06120`); container recreated, migration 115 verified applied. This surfaced and fixed a latent `init-local.sh` bug (`61677ef8`): the manifest parser silently dropped every migration past the 50th on fresh local databases. **E2E evidence is now real: the full authenticated pre-push suite passed (241 specs) with the decision flows green** — supersede, package retrieval, semantic search (threshold recalibrated 0.4→0.3 from measured titan-v2 paraphrase bands), REST capture, chat page, admin view (assertions made entity-resolution-aware). Earlier SKIP_E2E bypasses are superseded.
2. **Rate limiting on session-auth semantic search** → accepted risk by owner; no throttle added.
3. **`agentId` provenance (self-reported, confidence 1)** → keep as-is by owner decision.
4. **Embedding backfill for pre-existing nodes** → won't do (owner decision); pre-#1252 nodes stay lexical-only.
5. **Dedup audit persistence on auto-reuse** → won't do (owner decision).

body:
Adds the PostgreSQL `point` (OID 600) and `lseg` (OID 601) geometric types with I/O, text/type casts, on-page datum storage, and their full self-contained operator/function set (distance `<->`, positional `<< >> |>> <<|`, `~=`, point arithmetic `+ - * /` with PG's overflow/underflow/div-by-zero errors, `?- ?|`, `slope`, `point()`/`lseg()`, and the lseg accessors `@-@ @@ ?| ?- # ## ?|| ?-|`, `<@`, and length-based `< <= = >= > <>`). All type math lives in the new `crabgresql-types/src/geo.rs`, reproducing PostgreSQL's observable behavior — output text, error text, SQLSTATE, and the fuzzy `EPSILON=1e-6` comparison semantics — per the clean-room policy. Operators lower to a single data-carrying `ScalarFn::Geo(GeoFn)` variant via new `resolve_geometric_op`/`resolve_geometric_unary` helpers, matching how the inet/money types are handled. `point` is intentionally not b-tree orderable (only `~=`) while `lseg` compares by endpoints (`=`) / length (`<`), matching PG. A new `suites/smoke/sql/geo.sql` smoke test was verified byte-for-byte identical to real PostgreSQL 18, and the whole workspace (709 tests) passes with no warnings.

The sibling geometric types (line, box, path, polygon, circle) and the cross-type operators that need them are not included here; they are the follow-up phases of the approved plan.

## Summary

Stabilizes the Claude bridge on OMP 17.0.5 by preserving provider registration across subagent extension loads, removing bridge-owned context variants, and delegating authentication entirely to the official Claude Agent SDK.

## Changes

- register `claude-bridge` on every extension initialization while retaining the first process-global stream owner
- release stream ownership only from the owning session shutdown

author: kalotrapezis
body:
Rebuilds the UI in **pure GTK 4** (no libadwaita) from the PixelRuller design kept at `Assets/VoiceGTK.pixelruller.json`, and ships it as `voice-gtk` **alongside** the existing Tk `voice` command. Both interfaces share the same engines, config file and control socket, so global shortcuts drive whichever is running.

![Old vs new](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kalotrapezis/Voice/feat/gtk4-ui/Screenshots/gtk4/old-vs-new.png)

## What's new

- **Sidebar + page stack** — Υπαγόρευση / Ανάγνωση / Σύσκεψη / Πρόχειρο, with Ρυθμίσεις in the hamburger menu, replacing the tab bar.
- **Native theming** — no hardcoded accent colours. Style classes (`.suggested-action`, `.destructive-action`) plus geometry-only CSS, so the app follows the desktop theme and accent in light or dark. Record buttons keep a semantic red.
- **Live waveform** — dictation and meeting capture draw the real mic level while recording, beside a running timer.
- **Modal dialogs** — delivery target, shortcut capture (records the combo you actually press), clear-clipboard confirm, native About.
- **Two-column clipboard grid** with thumbnails, pin, delete and read-aloud per card.
- **Mini bar** — undecorated always-on-top pill; the clipboard list expands inline and the main window collapses into it on close.
- **Settings persistence** to `~/.config/voicekbd/config` (the mic key stays compatible with `dictate.sh`).
- **Feature toggles** now hide a feature everywhere — sidebar page *and* mini-bar button — per the design note.

## Packaging

`build_deb.sh` installs `voice_gtk.py` + `Assets/SVGs`, adds the `voice-gtk` launcher and desktop entry, and depends on `gir1.2-gtk-4.0`. Also fixed a latent bug in the same script: backticks inside the unquoted control-file heredoc were being executed as shell commands.

## Verified

- Piper → whisper round-trip end-to-end.
- All five pages plus the mini bar screenshotted (screenshots use seeded demo clipboard data, never real history).
- `.deb` builds clean; contents and control file checked.

## Known limitations

- "Πάντα μπροστά" uses `wmctrl`, so it applies on X11. GTK 4 has no keep-above API on Wayland — needs a KWin rule for the *VOICE Mini* window title.
- The system-tray icon still lives only in the Tk UI.

## Why

Owner call to cut Claude-subscription-seat spend. Haiku is ~3x cheaper than sonnet (`$1`/`$5` vs `$3`/`$15` per Mtok, `src/lib/llm/pricing.ts`) → ~3x more extractions per Max quota window.

## Change

`CLAUDE_MODEL` default flipped `sonnet` → `haiku` in both layers (cron wrapper `export` + `.mjs` `process.env` fallback) across every `claude -p` caller:

- `filing-extractor` (metadata enrichment — doc_type/summary/facts)
- `tadawul-gapfill`, `adx-gapfill`, `bhb-financials`, `dfm-backfill`, `msx-stmt-extract` (datalake statement extraction)

`CLAUDE_MODEL` env override still works unchanged — nothing else touched.

## Risk / why it's safe to try

The statement extractors write into `lake.objects` and are protected by the existing hard validation gate (`validateExtraction`: accounting identity `assets = liab + equity`, magnitude ceiling, scale-swing/"Mubasher 1000x" detection) plus the source-rank downgrade guard (LLM rank-20 never overwrites XBRL rank-10). A lower-fidelity haiku extraction gets **rejected before persist**, never lands bad numbers — worst case is lower yield, not corrupted data.

## Plan

Watching accept/reject rate + extraction yield over the next hour post-deploy before deciding whether to keep haiku across the board or roll specific extractors back to sonnet.

body:
## Context

Audio should prefer a real recording, fall back across multiple sources, and only *generate*
a sound as a last resort — and the reader must always be told the source. Since **no Google
model generates realistic animal calls**, generation uses ElevenLabs Sound Effects and stays
off unless keyed.

## Changes

- **`ingest/audio.ts`** (new) `resolveAudio()` — priority chain, first real hit wins, each
  fail-soft: **Xeno-canto → iNaturalist observation sounds → Wikimedia Commons audio** (all
  open, no key).
- **`ingest/llm/audio.ts`** (new) `generateSpeciesAudio()` — last resort: the synthesis LLM
  writes a grounded SFX prompt → ElevenLabs renders it → stored + `media` row tagged
  AI-generated. No-op without `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`.
- **`orchestrator.ts`** — audio block uses `resolveAudio()` then the generator; sets
  `audioUrl` + `audioCredit`.
- **Disclosure:** new `species.audioCredit` column (migration `0002`, additive/idempotent),
  carried through `snapshot.ts` + `seed.ts`; the **Takeover** panel shows it and labels
  AI-generated audio distinctly.
- **Synthesis prompt** now emphasizes *combining complementary details*, choosing the most
  authoritative source only on a direct conflict (matches the "combine, else best" strategy).
- `env.ts` (`ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `INGEST_AUDIO_MODEL`), `types.ts` + `ratelimit.ts`
  (`commons`, `elevenlabs` providers), docs updated.

## Behavior

Real recording always wins and is credited to its archive/recordist/license. A species with no
recording anywhere gets an AI-generated call **only if** ElevenLabs is configured, always
labeled "AI-generated … not a real recording". Nothing changes on the public site until keyed.

## Verification

- `npm run build` — server **and** frontend both pass.
- Live source calls (iNat/Commons/ElevenLabs) are exercised on Railway (sandbox egress blocked);
  all paths fail soft to the next source or to the viewer's ambience.

author: ccrutchf
body:
## Why

Parallel FileStation **Download** calls saturated the appliance's shared `synoscgi` CGI backend and took the NAS down; an inner retry storm compounded it by re-fetching the same files 200–250×. This implements the infra team's mitigations at the client level.

## What

Opt-in request **throttle** on the core `SynologyClient` (`ThrottleConfig` + `with_throttle`), wrapping the transfer calls (`download`/`upload`):

- **Concurrency semaphore** — single-digit global cap (default 4).
- **Rate-limit belt** — spaces request starts (default 150 ms).
- **Full-jitter exponential backoff** — 1s→60s on transient/degraded responses.
- **Bounded per-file retries** — default 5, then the error surfaces (no unbounded inner loop).
- **Error classification** — HTTP 502/503/504, 407 (backend fail-closing), connection/read errors, and DSM 402 (busy, backed off *harder*) → retry; missing-file / no-permission / other DSM codes → **fail fast**.

### Wiring (bulk-on / mount-off)

| Consumer | Throttle |
|---|---|
| Python `Client`/`AsyncClient` | **on by default**; tunable/disable via `login(..., throttle=…, max_concurrency=…, …)` |
| FFI `syno_connect` (GUI) | **on**, concurrency + backoff + retry cap; belt off (`min_interval=0`) so a GUI-initiated mount's ranged reads aren't stalled; **C ABI unchanged** |
| FUSE/CLI mount | **off** (interactive prefetch stays responsive) |

### Docs

- Python `README.md` + `CLAUDE.md`: throttle knobs, the **Temporal contract** (don't nest an inner retry under Temporal's outer policy), and the **SMB/NFS** structural recommendation for bulk staging.
- `CLAUDE.md`: also adds a **TDD requirement** (red-green-refactor) for the repo.

## Tests

- **Core:** 8 new tests (502/407 retry-then-succeed, 402 hard backoff, 415 fail-fast-no-retry, `max_attempts` bound, semaphore concurrency cap, rate-gate spacing, unthrottled-unchanged) — 61 pass.
- **Python:** 3 new tests (kwargs accepted, `throttle=False`, permanent error not retried through the binding) — 69 pass.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` all clean.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Discussed an in-process, cross-platform **SMB transport** (pure-Rust, no OS mount) as the structural fix, with the HTTP API as fallback — deferred pending a feasibility spike against the NAS.

author: vrtgs
body:
Closes #397
 
Adds the option to install an AppImage into its own dedicated subfolder instead of the shared default AppImages folder. This is useful for AppImages that run in portable mode and expect to keep their data next to themselves, rather than mixed in with every other installed app.
 
**What's new:**
 
- A new "Install in its own folder" checkbox when integrating a single AppImage.
- The same option available when integrating multiple AppImages at once.
- A matching `--own-folder` flag for the CLI (`gearlever --integrate <file> --own-folder`).
- Once an app is installed, its details page shows whether it's set up this way, so it's clear which layout is in use.
- The setting is remembered across future updates of the same app.
- Removing an app installed this way now also offers to clean up its dedicated folder. If the folder only ever contained the app itself, it's removed automatically. If the AppImage left behind its own data in that folder, you're asked whether to keep or delete it.
- Added Arabic translations for all new interface text.

## The problem

Constraint was `^0.19 || ^0.20`, so the panel could not be installed alongside core 0.21 or 0.22. `composer require builtbyberry/laravel-swarm-filament` fails outright for anyone on a current core.

## Verified before widening

Every public contract the panel reads through still exists in core v0.22.0:

`InspectsDurableRuns` · `ReadableRunHistoryStore` · `SnapshotsMemory` · `StreamEventStore` · `ReadableAuditOutbox` · `ReadableSwarmAuditSink` · `SwarmOperator` · `DurableRunDetail` · `MemorySnapshot` · `DatabaseDurableRunStore` · `NoOpSwarmAuditSink` · `SwarmStreamEvent`

**Full suite passes against core v0.22.0 — 180 tests, 641 assertions.**

## Change

```diff
- "builtbyberry/laravel-swarm": "^0.19 || ^0.20",
+ "builtbyberry/laravel-swarm": "^0.19 || ^0.20 || ^0.21 || ^0.22",
```

Constraint only, no panel code changed. Patch release: **v0.2.1**.

## Context

Found alongside the same problem in `laravel-swarm-pulse` (pinned to `^0.17`) while auditing the docs site. Both companions had silently fallen behind core, so the documented install paths were broken. Worth a CI job on each companion that installs against the latest core, so a lagging constraint fails in CI rather than in a user's terminal.

author: keli-wen
body:
<!-- github-prose-style: Keep each logical paragraph/list item on one physical line; do not hard-wrap at 80 columns. -->

## Summary

Adds PageIndex-style structure retrieval as a **self-contained artifact** plus a **pure-agentic** reasoning retriever, and refreshes the design principles that shape both. After review the original "vectorless empty shell + library page-refill" design was replaced by a self-contained one, so the final shape is:

- **knowledge**: a shared `StructureTree` base and a source-bound `PaperStructureTree` whose leaf nodes carry their own page-cited text (internal nodes stay navigational). `from_draft` mints all identity, links, and citations, and copies minimal provenance (`ArtifactMeta`: `as_of` + a light source ref + `source_content_hash`) that is kept out of `id` / `content_hash`, so identity stays reproducible and the tree is storable standalone.
- **flows**: `PaperFlow(cfg)` is a **config-bound** flow — bind the cfg once, `build(input)` takes only the operand, and the cfg **type** selects the knowledge shape (`PaperStructureCfg` → `PaperStructureTree`). `paper_flow` remains the compatibility function for the semantic chunk/summary shape. A pipeline is pure processing and binds no library.
- **library**: stores a self-contained tree standalone via `put(tree)` / `open_structure(id)` (no source or chunk set required); SQLite schema `v5` drops the artifact→source foreign key with a migration; `resolve` returns a node's stored content with no query-time refill.
- **mind**: `AgenticRetriever(RetrievalCfg)` is pure-agentic — an LLM agent reasons over one self-contained structure and returns evidence **values** (content included; `locator` is optional provenance), with no library binding. Mechanical retrieval (semantic / BM25) stays in `library` / `rag`; a future hybrid path composes the two.
- **preprocess**: deterministic outline signals (headings, table-of-contents pages, printed-to-physical page offset) feed the single bounded structuring draft call.
- **defaults / robustness**: `PaperStructureCfg` and `RetrievalCfg` default to `gpt-5.6-luna`; `AgenticRetriever` wraps the SDK `MaxTurnsExceeded` in `RetrievalError` and raises `RetrievalCfg.max_turns` to 20 so agentic traversal has head-room.
- **design principles**: `contexts/design/mind/retrieval.md`, `operations/orchestration.md`, `operations/naming.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the `quantmind-dev` skill now state: bind config (not the operand) for batch reproducibility; the cfg *type* selects shape/strategy (typed dispatch, not a class hierarchy); artifacts are self-contained (content + provenance); persistence and retrieval are downstream and retrieval returns values; and `mind` is the reasoning layer while `rag` / `library` are the mechanical retrieval plane.
- **observability**: `scripts/verify_structure_e2e.py` is a live smoke that builds, persists, reopens, and retrieves under the default model, wired as a path-filtered, non-required `structure` job in `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`.

## Related Issue

Part of #95; design context in #122. Live-smoke follow-ups filed: #126 (structured output fails on `json_object`-only providers) and #127 (surface token-usage / cost).

## Verification

- `bash scripts/verify.sh` — pass: Ruff format + lint, basedpyright (0 errors), import-linter contracts, and 382 tests at 84.35% coverage.
- Live structure smoke: `python scripts/verify_structure_e2e.py` — PASS with `gpt-5.6-luna` (self-contained tree covering every page, `put` / `open_structure` round-trip identical, agentic retrieve returns evidence).

## Checklist

- [x] The title uses English Conventional Commit format: `type(scope): summary`.
- [x] The related issue or design discussion is linked when applicable.
- [x] `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes.
- [x] Every applicable live-network component smoke test passes, or this PR states why none applies.
- [x] Public behavior has focused tests, an example, and documentation where applicable.
- [x] The PR is complete, small, and contains no unrelated changes.

## Summary

Follow-up from #49 (DuckLake production implementation) — a plain Postgres client on the
`ducklake` catalog database only shows DuckLake's internal metadata (snapshots, file paths,
schema versions), not the actual billing data, since resolving that requires DuckDB itself to
read the Parquet files in S3.

Documents a way to get **full DBeaver functionality** (schema navigator, data grid, SQL editor,
autocomplete) against real DuckLake data, not just a bare `duckdb` CLI shell: DBeaver ships an
official DuckDB JDBC driver, and its "Bootstrap Queries" connection setting runs SQL
automatically on every connect, before loading navigator metadata — exactly what's needed to run
the same `INSTALL`/`CREATE SECRET`/`ATTACH` sequence `DuckLakeConnectionService` already runs,
once per DBeaver session instead of once per backend process.

New file `docs/runbooks/ducklake-dbeaver-setup.md`, cross-linked from the existing
[provisioning runbook](../blob/main/docs/runbooks/ducklake-catalog-provisioning.md). No
credentials in the doc — placeholders only, sourced from the same Infisical paths
`backend/docs/infisical.md` already documents.

## Test plan

- [x] Manually verified: DBeaver connected via the DuckDB driver + these bootstrap queries shows
      `lake.billing_line_items` in the navigator with real row data, confirmed by the user
- [x] `git diff` is docs-only

author: acoseac
body:
The two safe remaining audit quick wins (Q6 skipped, see below).

## Q2 — dedup the sox tmp-path computation (transcode)
`RunSox` computed `SidecarPath()` twice (once inside `SoxArgs`, once directly) and independently rebuilt the `.tmp` path that *had to* match the output arg `SoxArgs` handed sox. `SoxArgs` now **returns** the tmp path it computes, and `RunSox` reuses it (deriving `finalPath` by stripping the suffix). This drops the redundant `SidecarPath`/`sha256` recompute **and** removes the latent fragility — the rename target is now provably the exact path sox wrote. All callers updated: `RunSox`, `pool.processJob`, `cmd/bridge/upscale`, + 4 test callers; added a consistency assertion (`tmpPath == args[6]`).

## Q28 — unify the "All Tracks" childCount source (dlna)
The root-listing "All Tracks" `childCount` used `folderIndex.TrackCount()` (deduped by `trackByID`), while `BrowseMetadata` and the actual `allTracksObjectID` DirectChildren enumeration use the **raw** `lib.TrackCount()` / `lib.ListTrackInfos()`. On a TrackID collision they diverge — the exact childCount-vs-enumerated mismatch strict controllers reject. Now all three use `lib.TrackCount()` (the enumerated count).

## Q6 — deliberately skipped
Combining the two `ffprobe` spawns on the ffmpeg fallback touches the value that feeds decode.go's **load-bearing** length-complete-decode gate; the two clean scalar probes are more robust than one combined parse, and the saving is a single fork-exec on the fallback-only path. The audit explicitly permits skipping it.

## Gate
```
gofmt -l                          → clean
go vet ./internal/transcode/... ./internal/dlna/... ./cmd/bridge/...  → clean
go build ./...                    → clean
go test -race ./internal/transcode/ ./internal/dlna/  → ok
go test ./cmd/bridge/ (upscale)   → ok
```

Note: Gemini is at its daily review quota — my diff-review + local gate stand in; CI runs the full suite.

body:
Operator request: bring points over from other map apps, and get them back out.

## Import — *Profil → Punkte importieren*

1. Pick a file (`file_selector`): **GPX, KML, KMZ or zipped** — zip containers are unpacked, KML placemarks without a Point geometry (lines/polygons) are skipped, broken coordinates ignored, parsing is namespace-agnostic.
2. The found points appear as a list; **per point** a tap on *Anlegen* opens the familiar add-spot sheet **prefilled with position and waypoint name** — species/count/date are added per spot, done rows get ticked off. (Exactly the requested flow: der Pilz wird je Punkt separat angelegt.)

## Export — *Profil → Eigene Spots als GPX exportieren*

GPX 1.1, one `wpt` per **own** spot (deliberately no friend spots): name, full find history in `desc`, newest find date in `time`. Shared via the system share sheet; on platforms without it (desktop browser) the GPX goes to the clipboard — same fallback as the invite feature.

## Tests

GPX/KML/KMZ parsing incl. error cases, an **export→import roundtrip** (with XML escaping of names like `Hang & Bach <Nord>`), and an import-flow scenario (prefilled sheet → spot persisted → row ticked). Suite now **72 tests**.

Deps: `file_selector` (official Flutter package; `file_picker` had an unsolvable win32 constraint conflict), `xml`, `archive` (^3, pinned by pmtiles).

Version 1.14.0+31 → **1.15.0+32**.

author: weisiang329-eng
body:
Closes the two inventory-**VIEW** cross-company leaks from the isolation sweep (**A3 + B1**). Backend: one route handler change + one migration that rebuilds two views. **Not merged, not applied to any DB.**

## The leak

**A3 (CONFIRMED, live).** `GET /api/scm/inventory?showAll=true` reads `scm.v_inventory_all_skus`. That view `CROSS JOIN`s `mfg_products` × `warehouses` with **no company predicate** and exposed **no `company_id`**, so the handler deliberately skipped `scopeToCompany` on the showAll read (`if (!showAll) q = scopeToCompany(q, c)`). Result: a user in one company saw the **other** company's products, warehouse names, on-hand qty, valuation and main supplier. Live on staging today (22 warehouses across HOUZS + 2990; 1326 vs 334 products).

**B1 (CONFIRMED real).** `GET /api/scm/inventory/products` reads `scm.v_inventory_product_totals`. 0106 appended `company_id` and the route scopes the **outer** read — but the **inner** `inventory_balances` / `inventory_lots` sub-aggregates `GROUP BY product_code` **only**, so `total_qty` / `total_value_sen` sum **both** companies' books for any shared code.

### B1 code-collision finding — do codes collide? **YES.**
0106 left B1 unfixed reasoning *"codes are per-company today (master_codes, 0087)"*. **That premise is false.** `0087_master_codes_per_company` converted `suppliers.code` / `products.sku` / `warehouses.code` / `special_addons.code` to `UNIQUE(company_id, …)` — it **never touched `mfg_products.code`**, the column this view anchors on. `scm.mfg_products.code` has only a **non-unique** btree index (no unique constraint, global or per-company), and the multi-company design (0087/0089 headers) *expects* both companies to reuse codes. A read-only staging introspection found **17 codes already collide across the two companies today** — `CODY-(K)`, `CODY-(Q)`, `FENRIR-(K)`, `FENRIR-(Q)`, `JAGER-(Q)`, … The numeric contamination is currently **latent** (for the 3 shared codes that have stock, only 2990 stocks them, so old-sum == per-company-sum) and materializes the instant HOUZS also stocks a shared code — at which point both companies' rows show the combined qty/value.

## The view change (migration `0154_scm_inventory_views_company_scope.sql`)

Two `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` statements, **byte-faithful** to `pg_get_viewdef` dumped read-only from staging, plus minimal additions:

- **`v_inventory_all_skus`** — append `w.company_id AS company_id` (LAST column) and add `p.company_id = w.company_id` to the `WHERE` so a product only pairs with its own company's warehouse. The route then scopes the showAll read (removed the `if (!showAll)` skip). The inner `b`/`v` sub-aggregates already key on `warehouse_id` (company-unique), so they're unchanged.
- **`v_inventory_product_totals`** — add `company_id` to **both** inner sub-aggregates' `SELECT` + `GROUP BY` and to their join to `p`, so each product's totals use only its own company's balances/lots. Outer column list unchanged.

Both are additive `CREATE OR REPLACE` (existing columns keep name/type/order; A3 appends one column at the end) — **no DROP**, and nothing depends on either view. Safety checks (read-only, staging): `inventory_movements.company_id` is **NOT NULL** (0 nulls) so `inventory_balances`/`inventory_lots` never carry a NULL `company_id` → the tightened B1 join drops **no stock**; `warehouses.company_id` is nullable but has **0 nulls**, and an un-companied warehouse now fails **closed** (rows drop) rather than showing to everyone. Both rewritten bodies were parse-validated on staging with `SELECT … LIMIT 0` (read-only).

## Staging-first validation — **REQUIRED (do not merge until done).**
`v_inventory_all_skus` is **not in the repo's migration tree** — like the report views 0106 rebuilt, it was created by the direct scm-schema restore (`apply-scm-views.mjs` pulls 2990's `0050/0053/0054/0095`, none vendored here); its authoritative body lives only in the DB. Houzs CI pg-migrates **PROD** on every deploy and a failed file blocks **all** later migrations, so `0154` must first be applied to **staging** (`minnapsemfzjmtvnnvdd`, **NEVER** prod `anogrigyjbduyzclzjgn`) via the Supabase management API and verified — **same handling as PR #874.** I did **not** apply it anywhere (only read-only `pg_get_viewdef` / counts / `LIMIT 0` on staging to author a faithful body).

## Migration number note
`0154` is the next free number on `origin/main` at push time (max was `0153`). Sibling isolation-sweep PRs (consignment/PO, masters/config) are in flight and there is an `apply-0154-consignment.mjs` **helper script** hinting the consignment group may also want `0154` — **re-verify the number at merge** (number-race rule: pg-migrate tracks per-filename, gaps are fine, only a DUP breaks the ratchet). Renumber this file if `0154_*.sql` has landed by then.

## Testing
`backend/tests/inventoryShowAllCompanyScope.test.ts` drives the exported `listInventoryHandler` on a bare Hono app with an injected fake supabase + active companyId, pinning: both directions (company 1 sees only its SKUs/warehouses, company 2 only its own), the **colliding-code** case (`SHARED-(K)` returns each company its own qty 3 / 9, never 12 or the other's product name), and the unresolved-company degrade. The view SQL itself can't run in the harness (DB view) — its correctness was checked read-only on staging and is gated on the staging-first apply above. `npm run typecheck` clean; `vitest --no-file-parallelism` green (4/4; `companyWriteScope` 14/14 unaffected).

Out of A3/B1 lane, surfaced not changed: the same handler's `warehouses` enrichment read is unscoped and returns both companies' warehouse rows — but it reads the warehouses **table** (a master), same unscoped pattern as several other handlers here; scoping the warehouse master is the masters/config group's lane.

author: ngabantudev
body:
## Summary

Performance/UX/accessibility cleanup pass plus one real bug fix, from a broader audit against four goals: performance, modern civic-transparency UX, mobile/desktop responsiveness, and keeping the door open for a future full-stack submissions system.

- **Fixed a real correctness bug**: `parseMW` (MW-capacity parsing) was duplicated 3x with two different regexes — one truncated decimals, one didn't — so the filter slider's bounds/sort could disagree with the map's actual filter comparison. Unified into `src/lib/projectMetrics.ts`.
- **Fixed a news feed regression** (reported separately by the user, diagnosed via `git log`): the most recent `newsFeed.ts` change sorted by a "context relevance" keyword score first and used publish date only as a tie-break, silently undoing an earlier fix that made the feed date-ordered. Reverted to strict most-recent-first and removed the now-dead `CONTEXT_TERMS`/`contextScore` code.
- **Dead code removal**: an unused duplicate `FilterCapacity.astro`, pre-GL-migration marker/filter logic in `mapMarkers.ts` left over from before the map switched to MapLibre GL circle layers, and the now-unreferenced `lucide-static` / `@types/leaflet` dependencies.
- **SEO/meta fixes**: the `<title>`/description meta had stale copy calling the site an "interactive dark-themed map resume"; `ogImage`/`ignoreTitleTemplate` props were declared but never wired up. Added working OG/Twitter tags, theme-color, an inline SVG favicon (site had none), and preconnect hints for the tile server and R2 PMTiles bucket.
- **HTML/a11y fixes**: removed a duplicate `<main>` landmark (`index.astro` wrapped `MapParent` in `<main>` while `Layout.astro` already renders one), added visible keyboard focus rings to the icon-only toggle buttons (filter panel, news panel, theme selector, detail-panel close — none had any before), and tightened `any[]` prop types on `FilterStatus`/`FilterProject` to their real types.
- **Repo cleanup**: removed the unreferenced 8.6MB git-LFS file `mn-protected-lands.pmtiles`, superseded by the R2-hosted PMTiles layers the map now streams from.
- Gated a per-toggle debug `console.log` in the PMTiles sync path behind `import.meta.env.DEV`.

## Not included (flagged for a separate decision)

- News content is fetched at **build time** (`prerender = true` on the index page), so the initial feed is only as fresh as the last deploy, while the 24H/7D/30D/1Y range switcher fetches live. That's a freshness-vs-perceived-speed tradeoff, not something this PR changes.
- A full-stack community-submissions system (auth, moderation, spam prevention, schema) needs its own design pass before any code — not attempted here.
- Map labels reference a `"Open Sans Bold"` glyph that 404s against the current basemap style's font server (harmless fallback rendering, but worth a look).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` completes cleanly

- **BI & egress:** curated fresh-empty Metabase snapshots (byte/schema/freelist canary scan, consumer-coordinated swap), five honesty-block SQL models, thresholded aggregate delivery with DNS-pinned transport and captured-egress proof

author: veatra
body:
### Motivation

- Prevent accidental deletion of root, UNC roots, or targets redirected by ancestor junctions by strengthening path normalization and ancestor inspection.  
- Reduce noisy or misleading console output from `takeown` and avoid parser crashes from subshells and parentheses in batch parsing.  
- Make elevation and ownership operations more robust against special characters and cross-process delayed-expansion issues.

### Description

- Reworked canonicalization wording and switched to lexical path normalization using `%%~fi` while explicitly noting it does not dereference junctions.  
- Added strict target-type validation using `%%~ai` to ensure a file operation cannot be applied to a directory and vice versa.  
- Implemented `:FindReparseAncestor` to walk parent paths and block operations if any ancestor is a reparse point, with separate error signaling via `reparse_inspection_error_path` and `reparse_ancestor_path`.  
- Introduced same-drive TAKEOWN output filtering by building `same_drive_success_pattern` and adding `:TakeOwnershipOfFileFiltered` and `:TakeOwnershipOfDirectoryFiltered` subroutines that pipe `takeown` into `findstr` to hide per-item SUCCESS messages only for the target drive; preserved other messages and UNC behavior.  
- Hardened elevation call by exporting the script path into `elevate_script_path` and invoking PowerShell with `-NoProfile` and environment injection to avoid PowerShell parsing of special characters.  
- Misc fixes: redirect `cacls` output to `>nul 2>&1`, strip trailing backslashes except for drive roots, avoid parentheses that can break CMD parsing, and consolidate attribute extraction and link-detection logic.

### Testing

- No automated tests are included in this repository and no CI tests were run for this change.

author: os-zhuang
body:
Closes the root cause tracked in #3220 (follow-through on #3222 / #1591 / #3213). ADR-0103.

## Problem

`managedBy: 'system'` conflated two incompatible write policies:

1. **Engine-owned** — rows a platform service owns end to end, written only via `isSystem` / a service `SYSTEM_CTX` / a context-less engine call (jobs, notifications, approvals, sharing, automation runs, the messaging delivery pipeline, settings/secrets/audit).
2. **Platform-schema, admin/user-writable data** — the RBAC link tables (`DelegatedAdminGate`-governed), `sys_user_preference`, `sys_approval_delegation`, and the messaging config grids surfaced in Setup.

The bucket carried the same all-false affordance row as `better-auth`/`append-only` but, unlike `better-auth`, had **no engine enforcement** — a wildcard admin could raw-write engine-owned rows through the generic data API (ADR-0049 gap). #3222 could only patch two latent holes; this is the taxonomy fix.

## Approach — resolved affordance is the policy (no new enum value)

A new `managedBy` value would fall through to the fully-editable `platform` default on already-deployed Console clients. Instead, write policy is `resolveCrudAffordances` (bucket default + `userActions`), and *engine-owned* ≔ a `system`/`append-only` object granting no write. Guard, `apiMethods` reconciliation, and the `/me/permissions` clamp all key off that one contract.

## What's in the diff

- **Writable set declares `userActions{create,edit,delete}`** — `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_position_permission_set`, `sys_user_preference`, `sys_approval_delegation`, `sys_notification_preference` / `_subscription` / `_template`. Affordance only — `DelegatedAdminGate` / RLS / permission sets stay the authz.
- **Engine-owned objects locked to `apiMethods: ['get','list']`** where absent. `sys_secret` read-locked explicitly (an empty `apiMethods` array fails **open**).
- **`sys_import_job`** stays engine-owned — the REST import route writes its job rows `isSystem`-elevated (attribution preserved via the explicit `created_by` stamp).
- **New engine write guard** `assertEngineOwnedWriteAllowed` (plugin-security) — fail-closed on user-context generic writes to engine-owned objects; `isSystem` / context-less writes bypass. Wired into the security middleware alongside the other data-layer gates.
- **`reconcileManagedApiMethods`** now runs for every managed bucket (was `better-auth`-only) — the drift backstop.
- **`clampManagedObjectWrites`** now clamps `system`/`append-only` too.

## Audit finding (write-context, the guard's precondition)

Confirmed every engine-owned writer uses `isSystem` / `SYSTEM_CTX` / a context-less engine call (incl. the metadata-protocol repository, whose transaction context carries no `userId`). The audit **expanded the writable set from 5 to 8**: `notification_preference` / `_subscription` / `_template` are Setup nav grids users/admins author, so they joined the writable set rather than being locked down.

⚠️ Not to be confused with the row-level `managed_by` provenance vocabulary (`platform`/`package`/`admin`, ADR-0066) — a different axis, untouched.

## Verification

All green:
- `spec` (6795) · `objectql` (1023, incl. new reconcile cases) · `plugin-security` (521, incl. new `system-write-guard` suite) · `plugin-auth` identity-write-guard (15) · `plugin-hono-server` (92, updated fold/clamp) · `rest` (323) · `platform-objects` / `plugin-approvals` / `service-messaging` / `service-automation` / `plugin-sharing` / `metadata-core`.
- **Dogfood** `delegation-of-duty` + `showcase-permission-zoo` (18) — confirm delegated administration and direct permission-set grants under user context still work with the guard in place.

## Potentially breaking

A downstream/third-party `system` object that advertised generic write verbs relying on today's fail-open will have those verbs stripped (with a warning) and user-context generic writes rejected — declare `userActions` opening the verbs it legitimately takes. `better-auth` keeps plugin-auth's identity guard unchanged.

The Console copy refinements (badge/empty-state for the writable-system case) ship in the paired objectui PR; they are not required for correctness (the UI already honours `userActions`).

author: trungdong
body:
## Summary

PROV-JSON now encodes QualifiedName attribute values as xsd:QName typed literals per the PROV-JSON submission's §3.1.2 examples, instead of this library's non-standard prov:QUALIFIED_NAME type; documents using the legacy type (as emitted by 2.x, or written by hand) still decode correctly, so reading old documents is unaffected. Separately, a Literal explicitly typed prov:QUALIFIED_NAME is now resolved to a real QualifiedName at assertion time using the record's bundle namespaces, so a document built directly from such a literal and one round-tripped through PROV-JSON compare equal again; when the literal's prefix has no in-scope namespace it is left as an opaque Literal rather than rejected, per the existing #257 policy against assertion-time rejection.

- `encode_json_representation` emits `{"$": ..., "type": "xsd:QName"}` for `QualifiedName` values instead of `prov:QUALIFIED_NAME`
- `decode_json_representation` accepts both `xsd:QName` and legacy `prov:QUALIFIED_NAME`, resolving to a `QualifiedName` where the prefix is in scope and falling back to an opaque `Literal` otherwise
- `ProvRecord._auto_literal_conversion` resolves a `prov:QUALIFIED_NAME`-typed `Literal` against the record's bundle namespaces at assertion time; `xsd:QName`-typed literals keep today's opaque model-side behaviour (only the JSON codec treats them as QualifiedName values)
- Flips the #238 strict xfail in `test_conformance_dm.py`; adds encoder-shape and legacy-decode tests to `test_json.py`, including one pinning that an unresolvable prefix stays an opaque `Literal`

author: kamronbatman
body:
`ObjectPropertyList.AppendFormatted<T>(value, format)` treated **any** `{value:#}` as the cliloc marker (emitting `#<value>`). But cliloc numbers are integers — a `float`/`double`/`decimal` formatted with `#` is the standard custom-numeric (`#` = digit placeholder) format, not a cliloc reference, so those were being mis-marked.

Gate the marker on an integer value type:
```csharp
if (format == "#" && value is int or uint or long or ulong or short or ushort or byte or sbyte)
```

Now `{someFloat:#}` formats normally (passes `#` through to `TryFormat`); the marker/standard-format ambiguity narrows to the harmless `{0:#}` **integer** case (`#0`). Existing `AddLocalized(int)` / `{value:#}` (all `int`) are unaffected.

Adds `ObjectPropertyListSpanAddTests.HashFormat_OnlyMarksIntegers`: `int {value:#}` → `#<value>`; `double {value:#}` → `42.0.ToString("#")` (`"42"`, no `#`).

author: cx20
body:
## Summary

Makes the exported Trophy GLB render as true crystal in glTF viewers with transmission support (Khronos glTF Sample Viewer, Babylon Sandbox, model-viewer, three.js), while keeping the live authoring page's alpha-blend look intact.

- **Export-time crystal flip** (`setCrystalExportMode`): the Export GLB handler temporarily switches the three glass materials (`clearGlass` / `blueGlass` / `mileMat`) to physical crystal — albedo white, alpha 1, subSurface refraction ON — so Babylon's serializer emits `KHR_materials_transmission` / `KHR_materials_ior` / `KHR_materials_volume` (with attenuation) / `KHR_materials_dispersion`, then restores the live settings. Live rendering stays on alpha blending because Babylon's realtime refraction samples only the `.env` texture, which would hide the rings/inscription behind the glass.
- **Color via volume attenuation**: on export the cobalt blue comes from `attenuationColor`/`attenuationDistance`, so thicker glass reads deeper blue like the real trophy (same technique as the `DragonAttenuation` sample).
- **`globeLensFront`**: viewers refract only the frontmost transmissive surface, so the carved dimple showed its concave-lens distortion only from the back. A flat disc in front of the globe area, carrying the dimple sphere's normals, produces the same lens distortion from the front while keeping the silhouette flat.
- **`globeMapFront` (export-only)**: transmission samples a downscaled/blurred opaque-pass buffer, which dissolved the 2px continent dots seen through the glass. A crisp front map layer reproduces how the real etched globe reads from the front, over the lens-distorted background.
- Clear panel transparency raised (alpha 0.15 → 0.08).
- GLB/glTF re-exported.

Verified via headless export: `extensionsUsed` includes transmission/ior/volume/dispersion/unlit; live materials restore correctly after export.

author: raineorshine
body:
## Why

Tasks in Chronicle are cross-cutting: the same task can appear across several calendars. Organizing the left column first by calendar fragmented those tasks and buried the thing you actually want to see: where your hours are going. This reworks the sidebar into a single ranked list of tasks over the current time period.

## What changed

- **Sidebar is now a flat task list.** One "All Tasks" root plus every task, merged across calendars by task key, sorted by hours descending over the selected window (4/8/12 weeks). Each row shows its total hours, and tasks with subtasks stay expandable (subtasks are also merged cross-calendar and hours-sorted).
- **Chart segments merge to match.** At the top level the weekly stacked chart now renders one slice per task instead of splitting the same task per calendar, so the chart and sidebar tell the same story.

## How it fits together

- `ChronicleCore` gains `TaskSummary`/`SubtaskSummary` and `Database.taskSummaries(from:to:)`, which groups `daily_time` by task (and task+subtask) across all calendars. `segmentDailySeries(.task)` drops the per-calendar key namespacing and groups by `task_key` only.
- `DashboardStore` swaps the calendar hierarchy tree for a `taskList` that recomputes per window, with a simplified node-ID scheme (`all` / `task:<key>` / `sub:<key>:<sub>`) and drill/title/styling logic to match.
- `ContentView` replaces the calendar/task disclosure views with the flat list and adds a trailing hours label to each row.

## Notes for reviewers

- `HierarchySelection` already filtered by task key alone, so no schema or query-filter changes were needed for cross-cutting selection.
- `hierarchy()` and `CalendarNode` remain in `ChronicleCore` (still covered by `DatabaseTests`) but are no longer used by the app sidebar.
- Tests updated: the task-dimension test now asserts cross-calendar merge, and a new `taskSummaries` test covers window filtering, merge, subtask rollup, and sort order. All 28 ChronicleCore tests pass; both the app and extractor build clean.

author: zaxbysauce
body:
Closes #1896
Closes #1902

## Summary

Resolves issue #1896, which bundled four separable defects, plus two related bugs surfaced during the investigation and fixed on the same branch at the maintainer's request: `SCOPE_NOT_DECLARED` scope-binding activation, and an interpreter-`-m` shell-write false positive (#1902).

- **ACCEPTANCE-field encoding** (`src/hooks/delegation-gate.ts`): the coder/reviewer dispatch coverage check had no Unicode/mojibake tolerance and returned a bare, misleading error. `normalizeAcceptanceText` now canonicalizes Unicode (NFC) and folds the section sign `§`/its Latin-1 mojibake to "section" (symmetric, bypass-safe); a mismatch now returns a bounded diagnostic (first-divergence offset, expected/found snippets, an encoding-corruption hint) instead of a false "copy byte-for-byte" instruction.
- **Model quota failover** (`src/utils/provider-error-classification.ts`, `src/utils/model-dispatch-fallback.ts`): quota/rate-limit errors were misclassified as permanent because the transient classifier was duplicated three times, none recognizing quota; the fallback-model switch only existed in the guardrails tool-result hook, so the critic, reviewer, and coder-lane dispatch stages never failed over. Single-sourced the classifier (quota kept as a *separate* class, combined only in dispatch paths — never the tool-output path, so a shell "Disk quota exceeded" can't trigger a bogus fallback) and wired a shared retry+fallback helper into oversight, reviewer, and runner. The evaluation dispatcher classifies quota and retries the *same* model (no substitution — the model id is the benchmark subject).
- **Sandbox circuit-breaker diagnostics** (`src/hooks/guardrails/nontransient-circuit.ts`): the non-transient hard-stop message dropped the stored failure signal, so an operator couldn't tell a dead sandbox from a sub-agent refusing to act. The message now surfaces the actual signal plus category-specific remediation (points to `/swarm diagnose`, explains the in-memory/invocation-keyed reset semantics). The immediate hard-stop and no-self-clear design (invariant 9 / issue #1875) is unchanged.
- **Model-divergence detection** (`src/state.ts`, `src/session/snapshot-{writer,reader}.ts`, `src/hooks/guardrails/messages-transform.ts`): the architect's active model is UI-driven by design, so nothing surfaced a silent switch across an interrupt. The observed model is now persisted (deliberately excluded from the transient-reset field set, so it survives rehydration) and the architect session gets a one-shot advisory on a genuine cross-interrupt change, gated on no swarm-initiated fallback being in play.
- **`SCOPE_NOT_DECLARED` scope-binding activation** (`src/index.ts`): the event handler that activates a coder's scope binding required `metadata.parentSessionId`, a key 1.1.x-era OpenCode runtimes never emit (verified against upstream `sst/opencode` `task.ts` at the pinned SDK version) — activation was unsatisfiable and every default-mode coder write failed `SCOPE_NOT_DECLARED`, immune to session resets. Parent identity now comes exclusively from the SDK-required `part.sessionID` (no metadata fallback; empty ids fail closed) — this is also a security hardening, since the old code would activate from attacker-controllable metadata.
- **Interpreter-`-m` shell-write false positive** (`src/hooks/shell-write-detect.ts`, `src/hooks/guardrails/tool-before.ts`, #1902): the write-scope guard flagged every interpreter eval flag — *including `-m`* — as a null-path write, then hard-blocked any null resolved path with a misleading `BLOCKED: … unresolvable path target` error, *before* scope/authority checks and regardless of `guardrails` config. This hard-blocked every `python -m pytest` / `python -m ruff` (even the swarm's own `test_runner`-generated commands) on all platforms — the wall the #1896 reporter hit. `python -m <module>` runs an installed module as a program (equivalent to invoking `pytest`/`ruff` directly), so it is no longer treated as an unverifiable write; inline `-c`/`-e`/`-r` eval stays flagged and unconditionally fail-closed, so the eval-bypass guard for scope/config zones is unchanged. The null-path block is now discriminated by category: a bare here-doc marker (stdin, not a write) is skipped, and interpreter-eval and dynamic `$VAR`/`$(…)` redirect targets keep failing closed with accurate, actionable messages. Cleared by an independent adversarial reviewer *and* a separate critic (both could not break the eval-bypass property).

Every defect went through localization → fix plan → independent plan critic → implementation → independent implementation review → independent final critic, with re-review after every post-approval change. Full trace: `.agents/issue-traces/1896-acceptance-field-model-failover/`.

## Invariant audit
- 1 (plugin init): not touched — the `src/index.ts` change is inside the `event` callback registered on the returned plugin object (line ~1352), not on the awaited `initializeOpenCodeSwarm` critical path; no new synchronous/awaited init work added.
- 2 (runtime portability): touched — two new files (`src/utils/provider-error-classification.ts`, `src/utils/model-dispatch-fallback.ts`) use only Node-safe APIs (`setTimeout`); grep confirms no `bun:` import or `Bun.*` call in either. The #1902 change adds no APIs. `bun run build` succeeds; `node --input-type=module -e "await import('./dist/index.js')"` succeeds.
- 3 (subprocesses): not touched.
- 4 (.swarm containment): not touched — no new `.swarm/` path creation; snapshot changes are additive fields on the existing `session/state.json` shape.
- 5 (plan durability): not touched.
- 6 (test_runner safety): not touched — all validation used shell `bun test`/`bun run test:unit:ci`, never the `test_runner` tool with a broad scope.
- 7 (test writing): touched — all new/modified tests use `bun:test` only. `bash scripts/check-test-file-cap.sh` → 0 new-file violations, 0 ratchet violations (incl. the #1902 additions to `tests/unit/hooks/guardrails-shell-write.test.ts`).
- 8 (session state): touched — `lastObservedModel`/`lastObservedProviderID` are two bounded strings keyed on the existing per-`sessionID` `AgentSessionState`, excluded from `TRANSIENT_SESSION_FIELDS`. The #1902 change adds no session state.
- 9 (guardrails/retry): touched — quota is a class distinct from generic transient status codes, combined with the narrow pattern only inside the *dispatch* classifier (never the tool-output classifier). The non-transient circuit's immediate hard-stop / no-self-clear (issue #1875) is unchanged. Scope-binding activation is strictly hardened (tool-controllable metadata excluded from parent-identity). The **#1902 interpreter-`-m` change is a guard-scoping fix**: `-m` module runs are reclassified as non-eval (equivalent to the already-allowed `python script.py`, which this guard never covered), while inline `-c`/`-e`/`-r` eval stays *unconditionally* fail-closed — the config-zone/scope eval-bypass regression tests are unchanged, and the OS sandbox wrapper remains the runtime containment. `checkDestructiveCommand` (which runs before the write-scope guard) never consulted the eval category, so nothing destructive is re-enabled.
- 10 (chat/system msg): touched — all new advisories use the existing `pendingAdvisoryMessages` queue and collapsed system message; verified end-to-end in `tests/unit/hooks/model-divergence.test.ts`.
- 11 (tool registration): not touched — no new tool, agent, command, or status. `bun run scripts/check-tool-registration.ts` → "108 tools, coherent."
- 12 (release/cache): touched — three fragments added (`docs/releases/pending/1896-acceptance-encoding-model-failover.md`, `docs/releases/pending/scope-binding-activation-event-shape.md`, `docs/releases/pending/1902-interpreter-module-run-shell-write.md`), every concrete reference ground-truth-verified against source. No hand-edit of `package.json#version`, `CHANGELOG.md`, or `.release-please-manifest.json`.

author: asaomaro
body:
> ⚠️ **PR #95 の上に積んでいます**（base は `feature/core-debt-payoff`）。#93 → #94 → #95 の順にマージしてから base を切り替えてください。

## 背景

SQL の読み取りは揃いましたが、**IBM i へデータを入れる手段がありません**でした。ACS の「データ転送」は双方向で、片道のままでは代替になりません。PR #94 で CSV アップロードの UI を見送ったのも、この土台が無かったためです。

## 原典の確認

AGENTS.md の「知識ベースや類推で書き始めない」に従い、**原典を取得して直読**しました（`archived/jtopenlite/ddm/` 15 ファイル 4,361 行）。**逐語移植はしていません**（IBM Public License 1.0 の互恵条項）。バイト配置・定数・手順という事実に基づいて書き起こし、参照コメントでクラス／メソッド名を明示しています。原典のソースはリポジトリに取り込んでいません。

## 変更

**DDM は他のホストサーバーと握手が違いました。** signon/database/command/netprint/IFS は `0x7001`→`0x7002` ですが、DDM は **EXCSAT → ACCSEC → SECCHK**（DRDA 系）で**ポートも 446**。`startHostServer()` は使えません。

ただし**資格情報のバイト化とパスワード置換値は共通**で、原典自身が `// Copied from HostServerConnection.` と書いているため既存実装を再利用しました。

**`DDMField`（1,220 行）は移植していません。** 列レイアウトは `QSYS2.SYSCOLUMNS` から計算します。移植量が桁で減るうえ、**検証が別経路になる**のが利点です（DDM で書いて SQL で読み返すので、配置計算が誤っていれば露見する）。

## 検証

実機（PUB400・TLS）で**書いた経路と別の経路で確認**しました：

```
2. レイアウト（SQL 由来）: NAME:char@0+10 QTY:packed@10+3 AMT:zoned@13+7 SEQ:int@20+4 NOTE:char@24+5 = 29 バイト
3. open: recordLength=29 increment=34 nullMapOffset=29
   ✅ SQL 由来のレコード長がホストの申告と一致
5. SQL で読み返し:
   {"NAME":"ALPHA     ","QTY":"12","AMT":"34.56","SEQ":1,"NOTE":"ok   "}
   {"NAME":"BETA      ","QTY":"-7","AMT":"-0.01","SEQ":2,"NOTE":null}
   {"NAME":"          ","QTY":"0","AMT":"0.00","SEQ":3,"NOTE":"     "}
```

負数・小数・ゼロ・空文字・**NULL**（空文字と区別されている）が往復します。テストは core 508 件（新規 30）。

### 実機検証が見つけた、自分の原則違反 2 件

1. **DBCS が黙って壊れて書かれた。** `encodeChar` がコーデックの `substituted` を無視しており、CCSID 37 に日本語を渡すと `` が保存されました。spec の「黙って壊れた値を書かない」に**自分で違反**していました。単体テストは SBCS しか試しておらず捕まえられず、実機の読み返しで発覚しました。
2. **NULL 指標マップが反映されていなかった。** `buildDdmRecord` は `null` を受け付けるのに、`buildS38Buf` は常に非 NULL で埋めており、**API が嘘をつく**状態でした。

どちらも修正し、実機で再確認しています。

### 副産物：CL 経由 RUNSQL の落とし穴

**`DECIMAL(5,0)` は通らず、`DECIMAL(5, 0)`（カンマ後に空白）なら通ります。** `CHAR(10)` は通るので括弧自体は問題なく、括弧内のカンマ直後に数字が続く形が CL の解釈で壊れます。DDM とは無関係ですが、`host_command` で RUNSQL を使う人が確実に踏むので backlog に記録しました。

## 対象外・未検証

- **読み取り・キー付き・更新・削除は実装していません**（読み取りは SQL がある）
- **バッチ書き込み未対応**（1 件ずつ・ブロッキング係数 1）。plan の撤退ライン「まず動いて検証済みのものを出す」に従いました
- `SMALLINT` / `BIGINT` の実機往復は未検証（単体テストのみ）
- 失敗時の途中状態は設計上巻き戻らないと分かっていますが、実際に失敗させて確かめてはいません

## レビュー結果

must 1 / should 2 / nit 3。must と should は修正しました。

body:
Hi, this is Claude (the AI assistant that worked on this branch).

Renders the task PR's GitHub review threads read-only inside the diff viewer and adds a collapsible **Conversation (N)** block of top-level PR comments at the top of the stream. Everything is read-only — no writes to GitHub of any kind.

## What's included

- Review threads render inline on their diff lines in **branch mode**, visually distinct from local inline comments (author login, GitHub glyph, timestamp, markdown-rendered body). Unresolved threads are expanded by default; resolved ones sit behind a toggle.
- Threads that no longer match the rendered diff collapse into per-file **Outdated review threads** groups instead of silently disappearing.
- Every thread and comment deep-links out to GitHub; a per-thread **Send to agent** button pushes the thread into the task terminal as a fix prompt.
- GitHub threads can be opted into the existing XML review export alongside local inline comments, tagged with an `origin="github"` marker.
- The yellow **"N unresolved comments"** row in the PR status popover (desktop popover **and** mobile bottom sheet) is now a deep link that opens the branch diff scrolled to the first unresolved review thread; it forces branch mode over any stored diff-mode preference and degrades to the thread's file when the thread is outdated.
- Data comes from a new cached RPC (GraphQL via `gh`) fetched on diff open / manual refresh — no polling changes.

Markdown rendering uses `marked` + `sanitize-html` (DOMPurify was unusable under happy-dom) — see `decisions/139-pr-comment-markdown-sanitizer.md`. UX rationale in `docs/ux/UX_DECISIONS.md`.

author: bd-viget
body:
## Summary

Two related fixes, both surfaced while building out design tokens for a project scaffolded from this starter:

- **`vite.config.js`**: `server.origin` was hardcoded to port `5273` while `server.port` resolves from `VITE_PRIMARY_PORT` (defaulting to `5273` only if unset). Any project that sets a custom `VITE_PRIMARY_PORT` (e.g. to avoid port collisions between multiple local DDEV sites) ends up with an HMR client trying to connect on a port nothing is listening on. File changes never reach the browser — the dev server *is* serving correct, up-to-date content the whole time, it just silently never notifies the browser to refetch it, so it looks broken. `origin` now derives from the same `VITE_PORT` constant as `port`, so they can't drift apart again.

- **`fluid-font-calculations.cjs`**: replaced the hardcoded `FLUID_TOKENS` array with `discoverFluidTokens()`, which checks a shared `SIZE_SUFFIXES` scale with no prefix (the body scale) and once per `SUPPORTED_FILTERS` prefix (e.g. `headline-lg`), keeping only the combinations that actually have a `--fs-{token}-min/max` range defined in `font-sizes.css`. This means a project can add a `headline`/`ui` scale (or new sizes) purely by adding CSS — no plugin code changes needed. Verified this produces byte-for-byte identical output to the old hardcoded list against the starter's current `font-sizes.css`.

- New `src/theme-json/helpers/font-scale.cjs`: `SIZE_SUFFIXES`/`SUPPORTED_FILTERS`/`fontNames`/`fontSlugs` moved here from `fonts.js` so both `fonts.js` and the plugin source from one place instead of maintaining separate copies. It's plain CommonJS so the plugin can `require()` it directly and `fonts.js` (ESM) can import its named exports via Node's standard CJS interop — avoiding a circular require between the two (fonts.js already requires the plugin for other helpers).

Scoped intentionally narrow: no design-token values (colors, sizes, fonts) are part of this PR, just the two mechanism fixes above.

## Test plan
- [ ] `discoverFluidTokens()` produces the same 6 tokens (`sm, base, md, lg, xl, 2xl`) as the old hardcoded `FLUID_TOKENS` list against the current `font-sizes.css`
- [ ] `npm run dev` under DDEV with a custom `VITE_PRIMARY_PORT` set — confirm HMR updates reach the browser without a manual hard refresh
- [ ] `theme.json` builds successfully via `vite build` / the dev server's `configureServer` hook
- [ ] Existing `getFontSizes()` output (body scale slugs) is unchanged

body:
## What

Replaces the Daily view's two fixed windows (Last 24h / Since yesterday) with a **selectable date-time range**:

- **Three working-day presets** — Today, Yesterday, and the working day before that (labelled by its full weekday name), each spanning one whole calendar day `[00:00, next 00:00)`. Yesterday / day-before **walk back over weekends** (Monday → Friday / Thursday); Today is literal and **disabled on weekends**.
- **Custom From/Until** datetime inputs (minute granularity, Europe/Berlin), honoured verbatim including weekend transitions. Editing either re-queries.
- **Default** is Today, falling back to Yesterday when Today is disabled.
- **Invalid range** (From ≥ Until or malformed) shows an inline error and renders no results — no silent fallback.
- State round-trips as `?preset=today|yesterday|day-before-yesterday` or `?from=…&to=…`. The resolved range drives the digest, "tickets I created" and the cards uniformly.
- Each preset button carries a hover `title` with the concrete date it maps to.

## How it works

One `<form>`: preset buttons GET `?preset=<key>` (preset mode); editing From/Until GETs `?from&to` with no preset (custom mode); a hidden `preset` input round-trips the active mode across an assignee change. HTMX-only, no inline JS.

## Tests

- Unit tests cover preset resolution across **every weekday** (incl. Monday walk-back and weekend Today-disabling), the default selection, custom-range parsing, and the invalid-range error path.
- Integration tests updated for the preset model (presets, custom range, invalid range, URL round-trip). `make check` passes.
- Acceptance-reviewed against the running app: presets, hover titles, custom-range editing, inline error, URL round-trip.

Closes #90

author: steipete
body:
## Problem

On the live team instance the Control UI throws a recurring **caught** error on nearly every gateway WebSocket event:

```
[gateway] event listener handler error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'role')
  at ... chat-message chunk <- chat-page event handler <- Ce.handleMessage <- WebSocket
```

It's caught by the gateway event dispatcher (no white-screen — Model Setup and avatars render fine), but it floods the console and some chat/transcript updates can fail to process.

## Root cause

`normalizeMessage`, `isToolResultMessage`, and `isStandaloneToolMessageForDisplay` take `unknown` input, cast it to `Record<string, unknown>`, then read `typeof m.role`. `typeof` guards the *property value*, not the *object* — `typeof m.role` still evaluates `m.role`, so when `m` itself is `undefined` it throws `reading 'role'`.

`groupMessages` calls the raw `normalizeMessage(item.message)` (chat-thread.ts:396), and `item.message` is `unknown` — absent for a pending send or a malformed transcript row (this path grew with the durable-rolling-transcript work + author-avatar grouping). The codebase already had a `safeNormalizeMessage` try/catch wrapper acknowledging this hazard, but the grouping path used the unguarded entry point.

## Fix

Coerce non-object input to `{}` at the source (`asMessageRecord`), so every downstream `typeof m.<field>` check works and role degrades to `"unknown"` instead of crashing. Behavior is byte-identical for valid object input.

## Test

Added a regression block asserting the three entry points never throw and return safe defaults for `undefined | null | string | number | boolean`. Full UI vitest project green (the one failing `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` is an unrelated ~40s timeout flake under full-file load — it passes in isolation and doesn't reference the normalizer).

author: wbarnha
body:
## Description

Fixes [faust-streaming/mode#36](https://github.com/faust-streaming/mode/issues/36)
("faust hijacks console output"). A user who configures `structlog` (or a plain
`logging.basicConfig()`) before starting a faust worker finds all output
re-prefixed with `[date] [pid] [LEVEL]` once the worker starts, destroying their
formatting.

Root cause: `mode.utils.logging.setup_logging()` unconditionally does
`logging.root.handlers.clear()` and reconfigures the root logger with mode's
colorlog formatter. `mode.Worker` **already** gates this behind
`override_logging: bool = True` — `Worker(..., override_logging=False)` skips
`_setup_logging()` entirely. The gap is on the faust side: its CLI
(`Command.worker_for_service()`) built the `Worker` with a hardcoded kwarg list
that never passed `override_logging` through, and there was no CLI flag — so
anyone running the standard `faust worker` command couldn't reach a lever that
already existed one layer down.

This adds `--override-logging/--no-override-logging`, following the exact
`compat_option` pattern already used for `--loglevel` / `--blocking-timeout` /
`--console-port`:

```
CLI flag -> State.override_logging -> Command._override_logging
         -> Command.override_logging property (default True) -> Worker(override_logging=...)
```

The default is `True`, matching `mode.Worker`'s own default, so existing
behavior is unchanged. **No `faust-streaming/mode` change is needed** — the
parameter already exists there.

## Changes
- `faust/cli/base.py`: new `State.override_logging` field, the
  `--override-logging/--no-override-logging` `compat_option`, the
  `Command._override_logging` attribute + `__init__` read, the public

author: michaelviu
body:
Re-targets the static-system-prompt work onto `main`. (Supersedes #338, which was accidentally merged into `feat/ai-sdk-boundary` instead of `main`, so the change never reached `main`. These are the same two commits, cherry-picked onto `main`.)

Makes the system prompt **100% static** so it stays in the prompt cache and is never busted — the operator's rule: no dynamic content in the system prompt.

## What changed
- **System prompt = static core only**: identity · tool-playbook · module-model · staging · **subagents (now static)** · memory · the static `## Skills` index. Every volatile site-state block is gone.
- **Live state on-demand**: pages, modules, theme, structured sets, content library, layouts, redirects, locales, users/roles, foreign locks are no longer dumped into the prompt — the AI fetches what it needs via the existing `list_`/`get_` tools; results land in the append-only message history. `buildSystemContextBlocks` no longer performs those reads.
- **Current page + cold-start status ride the USER message**, never the prompt: injected on the first turn and again only when they change (djb2 signature vs the last `<!--marker:-->` in history), persisted so the check survives turns.
- **Deleted dead builders**: `context/catalog.ts`, `context/domains.ts`, `context/foreign-locks.ts` (+ test), `context/site.ts`, `buildAllPagesBlock`, `buildPostCatalogueBlocks`. Dynamic plugin / plugin-context blocks dropped.
- **CLAUDE.md §11 rewritten** to "the system prompt is 100% static; state on-demand; current page + status on the user message".

## Verified
- `tsc` clean; admin-core **605 pass** (1 pre-existing DB-state flake: bootstrap-publish needs 0 published pages globally; clean DB passes).
- **Live e2e-livedit A/B** (real API, clean DB per arm, logs truncated per run): **both arms 7/7** — the AI completes every scenario fetching state on-demand. Wire confirms the static prompt (`# Engaged skills`/`# All pages` = 0, `skills-index` present).
- **System prompt 28.8 KB → 16.0 KB, now fully cached** (Arm A cache-hit 86% → 91%).

## Honest trade-off
Removing the context blocks adds state-fetch round-trips: turns rose (Arm A ~27→35, Arm B ~25→39) while cost stayed ~\$1.5. With an already-small static prompt the tool-search-vs-all-tools gap narrows and can flip run-to-run (variance) — the win is cache purity + never-bust + a smaller prompt.

## Follow-ups (noted)
- The block formatters in `system-prompt.ts` (`formatModulesBlock`, …) are now unused but still unit-tested — candidate for removal.
- Plugin `promptContext` dropped with the dynamic blocks; a plugin needing to surface state should expose a tool.

body:
Closes #88. From the rendering audit — a regression from #86/#87.

## Problem

The begin/end edge-label feature rendered Capella's placeholder value `"."` literally, producing a stray "." glyph at each end of association-style edges (20 of them on [PDFB] Perform remote diagnostic alone). The aird persists `beginLabel="."` / `endLabel="."` 18 times each — Capella uses `"."` for an end label a mapping declares but the element leaves empty.

## Summary

Autonomous dependency-upgrade pass across every ecosystem in the repo.

### npm / pnpm: no actionable upgrades this cycle

Every direct dependency across the workspace (root plus `sdk`, `cli`, `mcp`, `web`, `vscode`) is already at its latest stable release. This repo runs a daily deps upgrade and #292 merged yesterday, so the tree was already current.

- `ncu --deep --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/` reports all 5 packages match latest.
- `pnpm 11.15.0` was published inside the 7-day release cooldown, so `packageManager` intentionally stays at `11.14.0`.

### GitHub Actions: Pages deploy actions bumped to newest generation

`checkout`, `setup-node`, `upload-artifact`, and `pnpm/action-setup` were already pinned to their latest SHAs. The Pages deploy actions were a few generations behind, so this PR moves them forward (SHA-pinned, verified against each release tag):

- `actions/configure-pages` v5 -> v6.0.0
- `actions/upload-pages-artifact` v3 -> v5.0.0
- `actions/deploy-pages` v4.0.5 -> v5.0.0

The only breaking change in this set is that `upload-pages-artifact` v4+ excludes dotfiles from the uploaded artifact. Verified non-impacting for this deploy: the web `public/` folder has no dotfiles (no `.nojekyll`), and vite's `base: "./"` emits `assets/` paths, so no `_*` or `.*` files are dropped from the published site.

## Validation

- `pnpm -r typecheck` green

## Summary
Phase-2 of `ailang fmt`: lossless comment preservation so the formatter stops refusing the ~94.7% commented corpus. Phase-1 (printer + CLI) already shipped; this adds a token-anchored comment envelope + deterministic attachment.

Mission iteration 63 (V1 mission #399). Design doc unparked by Mark (option (b)). Sprint-evaluator (sonnet, generator≠judge vs the opus executor) **PASS 78/100 round 1**.

## Milestones
- **M0** — printer child-list code audit → verified 39-site inventory folded into the design doc (proves the attacher-totality objection concrete).
- **M1** — lossless collector (byte-exact spans) + token-anchored envelope (rune-walk anchors, literal clamping, bracket matching, hard left wall) + **interpolation FAIL-CLOSED carve-out** (comment inside `${…}` → exit 2, byte-identical, never silently deleted).
- **M2** — deterministic attachment (rules 1–5) + totality (fail-closed) + emission interleaving + per-rule idempotence.
- **M3** — marker property test + corpus gate + `HasComments` refusal removal (only after gates green) + exit-code split (3=parse, 2=operational) + docs.

## Corpus gate (V22)
386 parse-valid files → **327 formatted, 0 comment-loss, 0 Phase-2 round-trip regressions, interpolation-refusal 0/386**, idempotence 299/299.

## Calibrated boundaries (both fail-closed, never lossy — documented in Future Work)
1. **15.28% (59/386) inline-interior refusal** — comments interior to `let … in` chains the parser collapses to a single expression with no stable idempotent boundary → refuse (exit 2, byte-identical) rather than relocate. Follow-up sub-sprint tracked.
2. **28 pre-existing Phase-1 `properties[...]` printer round-trip bugs** surfaced (verified not caused; fail comment-free round-trip on origin/dev too) — separate out-of-scope item.

## Verification
- `go test ./internal/format/ ./internal/lexer/ ./internal/parser/ ./cmd/ailang/` → all green
- `make lint` clean for touched packages · `make check-file-sizes` green · `make verify-examples` green
- `internal/ast/print.go` untouched; parser token stream byte-identical.

body:
## What this adds

A social layer over the static site — two Supabase-backed, world-readable UGC
features, both **instant-publish with report + auto-hide-past-3-reports**
moderation, free to post but account-required.

### Community recipes
Users submit their own recipes (with one photo, downscaled to WebP in the
browser — also strips EXIF) that **merge into the board's `RECIPES` array**, so
the modal, weekly plan, reviews, ratings, favorites and PDF all work on them
unchanged. They're mixed in alongside house recipes, flagged with a `COMMUNITY`
stamp, behind an optional "community only" filter, with a "your recipes"
edit/delete section on the profile page. Backed by `user_recipes` +
`recipe_reports` + a `recipe-photos` Storage bucket.

### Forum
A standalone page (`forum.html` / `forum.js`) for meal-prep + fitness-journey
discussion — threads + flat replies, category filter, hash-routed
(`forum.html#t-<id>`). Reading is public; the first sign-in is on the board
(OAuth redirect constraint), so signed-out visitors get a "sign in from the
board" prompt. Backed by `forum_threads` + `forum_replies` + `forum_reports` +
a `forum_thread_meta` reply-count view.

### Shared
`store.js` data layer, `community-ui.js` submit/report dialog, RLS-only
migrations (report counts read via `SECURITY DEFINER` functions so a reporter's
identity never leaks), `legal.html` disclosure, masthead links, sync-web
allowlist, cache-bust bumps, docs.

## Migrations — already applied ✅
Both `supabase/migrations/20260719000000_community_recipes.sql` and
`20260719000001_forum.sql` have **already been run against the live MISE
project** (via the SQL editor) and verified: the anon client reads
`user_recipes`, `forum_threads`, and `forum_thread_meta` successfully. Merging
this PR ships the frontend that uses them.

## Verified
- Both features render + function against the migrated database (local preview).
- Graceful degradation confirmed (board/forum work with tables absent).
- All new/changed JS passes `node --check`; no console errors on board or forum.
- A pre-commit adversarial review (security / correctness / consistency) ran;
  its confirmed findings were fixed in this branch (see below).

## Review fixes included
- Report writes use `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (needs only INSERT) so reporting
  works regardless of an UPDATE grant on the private reports tables.
- `openFromHash` no longer reopens a recipe modal the user has closed, while
  still resolving a community deep-link once the async list lands.
- Community recipe difficulty now matches the recipe tool's hands-off discount.
- Forum compose/reply is gated on a real backend (not the demo profile).

## Known low-severity follow-ups (not blocking)
Raw-API abuse only — the app's own UI never triggers these:
- The public `author` name is client-settable (byline impersonation).
- `created_at` is client-settable (feed-order pinning).

Both are fixable with a small hardening migration that forces the values
server-side; happy to add it as a follow-up.

author: lantos1618
body:
The ownership checker was over-free-**sound** (catches double-free/UAF) but under-free-**blind** — forgetting to release an owner was silent. This closes it. An owner created locally and not discharged before the function returns is `error[leak]`, pointing at the creation site:
```
error[leak]: owner created here is never released or moved before the function returns
      o := a.new_in(...).expect("own")
      ^
hint: release it (`o.release_in(a)` / `o.drop_in(a)`), move it into a consuming call, or return it
```
This is the external reviewer's "#1 cause of leaks" — now a compile error, with **zero new syntax** (the Zen-shaped answer instead of `defer`: cleanup stays explicit and visible; the compiler just checks you did it).

## Real leaks found
The **Rc and Arc harness value-cases** cloned a refcount (`r2 := r.rc_clone()`) and never dropped it — a genuine leak the `Own` cases got right. The detector caught its own standard library. Fixed both (value-neutral).

## Soundness posture (conservative v1, zero false positives)
Flags a top-level `o := <fresh owner production>` whose name is **never read again** anywhere. Because the read-scan is exhaustive over every expression shape, any real discharge — release, move into a consuming call, return (incl. wrapped `ok(o)`/`.Some(o)`/`Box(o:o)`), send, out-param store — necessarily *names* the owner, so "never named again" is a sound proof of leak with no escape-analysis blind spot. Field/alias borrows (`o := b.field`) excluded by the fresh-production gate. Deferred to v2 (honest under-reports): nested-block owners, pure-read-then-leak, leak-on-some-paths. **Whole-tree sweep: 729 files, zero false positives.**

## Verification
harness ALL PASS · difftest 215 cases zero diffs (proves no FP / no behavior change on non-leak corpus) · seed byte-exact fixpoint · fmt clean · 7 fixtures (1 reject + 6 accepts incl. param-owner, return-owner, move, field-borrow).
