body:
Two related changes on this branch.

## 1 — Migrate attribute flags: `side`/`position` → `side`/`direction`/`location`

```
[side:true|position:true]  ->  [side:true|direction:true|location:true]
```

| flag | canonical values | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `side` | `sol` / `sağ` | left / right |
| `direction` | `ön` / `arxa` | front / rear (was `position`) |
| `location` | `daxili` / `xarici` | **new** — inner/outer CV joint, engine vs. gearbox mount, lambda before/after catalyst |

- **`data/SLOVAR_FINAL.txt`** — replaced with the v2 three-flag dictionary.
- **`parser.py`** — reads three flags; `Part` gains `direction_flag` / `location_flag`.
- **`attributes.py`** — `detect_position` → `detect_direction`; added `detect_location` (`daxili/xarici/iç/çöl/inner/outer/внутр/наруж`, plus `до/после` for the lambda sensor).
- **`matcher.py`** — `attributes` is `{side, direction, location}`; `needs_clarification` covers all three.
- **`build_html.py` + `matcher_tool.html`** — JS port + funnel updated (new `Daxili / Xarici` chips).
- **Collision fixes** — v2's simplified wording reintroduced 11 name/synonym collisions (`(mühərrik)`, `(paket/disk)`, bare `(EVAP)` …); restored the disambiguating qualifiers so `check_collisions.py` and the integrity test stay green.

## 2 — Reference-JSON in / filled-JSON out funnel (`JsonMatcher`)

```python
match(part_json: dict) -> dict
```

Takes the full reference object the Seller model emits and returns the *same object* with only the deterministically-decidable fields filled — everything else (`shop`, `brand`, prices, `oem_code`, …) passed through untouched. The input dict is never mutated.

- Fills `part_id` / `category` / `subcategory` (two-layer funnel) and `side` / `direction` / `location` (from `raw`).
- `part_name: null` → containment fallback over `raw`: fills `category` if it resolves to exactly one, leaves `part_id` / `subcategory` null.
- **`slovar_matcher/json_api.py`** — new `JsonMatcher` + module-level `match()`.
- **`category.py`** — `categories_in_text()` helper for the null-`part_name` path.
- **`cli.py`** — `--json '<obj>'` (or `--json -` for stdin) mode alongside string mode.
- **`matcher_tool.html`** — JSON in/out card at the top of the page, verified identical to the Python funnel via node.

Spec example:

```json
{ "part_name": "Amortizator", "raw": "sol qabaq amortizator", "...": "..." }
->
{ "part_id": "AS-001", "category": "Подвеска",
  "subcategory": "Amortizatorlar / dayaqlar",
  "side": "sol", "direction": "ön", "location": null, "...": "..." }
```

- `python -m pytest tests/ -q` → **60 passed** (51 existing + 9 new JSON-funnel tests)
- `python scripts/check_collisions.py` → **OK, no collisions**

author: poool1717
body: ## Resumen Un informe con fotos ocupaba **27 MB en base de datos** porque `SecAnexos` (`components/Peritia.jsx`) guardaba cada archivo subido como *data URI* base64 dentro del JSONB `anexos`. Además `saveToSb` reescribía ese JSONB completo en cada guardado (debounce de 5 s), generando ~3 GB de IO por sesión de edición larga — esto ya provocó un outage por bloat de PostgreSQL. Este PR mueve los archivos a **Supabase Storage** y deja en el JSONB únicamente la URL pública. ## Cambios - **Nuevo bucket `anexos`** (`supabase/migrations/20260719120000_anexos_storage_bucket.sql`): público en lectura; políticas RLS en `storage.objects` — INSERT y DELETE solo para el usuario autenticado propietario de la ruta (`{user_id}/{informe_id}/{tab}/{timestamp}-{nombre_sanitizado}`, comprobando que el primer segmento coincide con `auth.uid()`). - **`addFiles` (SecAnexos):** ya no usa `FileReader.readAsDataURL`. Sube cada archivo con `POST /storage/v1/object/anexos/{path}` (mismo patrón de headers que el helper `sbDb`: `apikey` + `Authorization: Bearer {token}`) y guarda en `item.url` la URL pública (`.../storage/v1/object/public/anexos/{path}`). Límite de 10 MB por archivo con mensaje claro si se supera; indicador "Subiendo…" mientras la subida está en curso; banner de error visible si falla (el archivo no se añade si la subida falla). - **`delI` (SecAnexos):** borra también el objeto en Storage. Si el borrado remoto falla, el item se elimina igualmente del JSONB (no bloquea la UI) y el error queda registrado en consola. - **Propagación de props:** `SecAnexos` recibe ahora `token`, `userId` e `informeId` desde `ReportEditor` (que ya recibía `token`/`user` de `App`). - **Forma del objeto de anexo sin cambios** — `{id,name,url,type,caption,cat}`. El preview (`SecInforme`), el export PDF y el export Word solo leen `item.url` en ``/`

body:
## Folds the missing gap into DR-007 (#300)

DR-007 hardened acts 1–4 but its audit missed the gap that actually **starves Gold**: the resident lacks `karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt`, so Karpenter voluntarily disrupts (consolidation/drift) its Spot node **every few minutes**, SIGTERM-draining it before a full ~15–20m silver→gold tick completes. Silver stays fresh (jobs complete across restarts); **Gold never gets written**. DR-007's P1 boot-preflight can't catch it — it's a runtime scheduling eviction, not a boot dependency.

**Fix:** `karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt: "true"` on the resident pod (same protection the cron/v4-identity transform pods carry). Rendered unconditionally + a `podAnnotations` value for extras.

**DR-007 doc updated:** GAP 10 in the audit table, P6 in the fix section, and the P5 orphan-prune is now **gated** on this (don't prune `v4-medallion` until do-not-disrupt is deployed and the resident completes full ticks — else the prune re-starves Gold).

Verified: helm renders the annotation; YAML valid; mirrors the working cron pods. Promotes to master **with DR-007** (both on release) as one consolidated landing.

**Prod now:** `v4-medallion` cron re-instated as the safety writer → Gold fresh. Resident runs Silver alongside (safe idempotent overlap). Prune the orphan only after this deploys + a clean tick is observed.

## What

Two more worked examples in the load-test runbook, as requested:

- **7. IPFIX-only fidelity** — a dedicated IPFIX recipe, highlighting its cleanest run-isolation lever (Observation Domain ID) and that its data-record sequence legitimately starts at 0 at T0.
- **8. Mixed flow-protocol fleet (20% v5 / 20% v9 / 60% IPFIX)** — a realistic mixed fleet.

## The key modeling point (example 8)

A scenario targets **one protocol** (MVP: one active scenario at a time), so a mixed workload is **not** a single multi-protocol scenario. It's modeled as:

1. A **device-count split** (2 / 2 / 6 for a 10-device 20/20/60 mix) configured with **per-device `flow` blocks** — because seed flags apply one protocol to the whole auto-start batch.
2. **One scenario per protocol, run back-to-back** (a terminal scenario is transparently replaced, so the single active slot frees between runs).
3. Reconciled per protocol on the `(protocol, source_ip, collector)` key.

The example notes the fleet exports all three the whole time — a scenario just measures one subset's window at a time — and how to weight by traffic (proportional `rate`) rather than device count.

author: monotophic
body:
# PROF: DISK-CLASS — per-load cold/warm disk instrumentation

*Authored by Fable 5 in Claude Code, analysis in partnership with @Monotophic.*

## Re-derived onto the #391 split (this revision)

This branch (`e7/disk-class-instr-rebased`) re-derives the original
`e7/disk-class-instr` @ `de6dd6d` (base `caa49f7`) onto `origin/dev` @ `61004dc`,
after PR #391 split `c/glm.c` into `c/colibri.c` + `quant.h`/`sample.h`/
`kv_persist.h`/`telemetry.h`/`grammar.h`. Semantic equivalence, not a copy: same
events, same accounting, re-sited onto the new tree.

- **Placement:** unchanged — everything stays in `c/colibri.c`. `telemetry.h`
  (new in #391) is the dashboard/stats module (`HWINFO`/`TIERS`/`EMAP`/`HITS`
  protocol lines + usage persistence); `prof_report()`, `expert_load_impl()`,
  `moe()`, `g_prof_io` and `g_edisk_ns` all stayed in `colibri.c` after the
  split, so DISK-CLASS's aggregation and printing follow them there.
- **Read path:** #362 (prefetcher-v3, `22509fc`) turned out to be testbed-only
  scope per its own merge message ("glm.c untouched") — confirmed zero
  `c/glm.c` changes in that merge's diff (only `c/olmoe.c` + tooling). The
  seven `expert_load()` call sites this patch touches are structurally
  identical to the pre-split tree; DISK-CLASS still counts demand loads only.
- **One real drift, unrelated to #362:** #417 (`cfcc742`) fixed the exact
  "Metal pre-routed FASE A never bumps the real `elast`/`eaccess_clock`"
  defect this feature's comments used to describe as a documented,
  deliberately-unfixed upstream issue — the real clock now ticks in FASE A
  too. The private `elast_dc`/`eaccess_clock_dc` clock is kept anyway (its
  job was never only to route around that freeze — it also snapshots
  pre-bump state so a call's own routing bump can't contaminate its own
  classification, and keeping DISK-CLASS's bookkeeping fully separate from
  stock `elast` state is what makes "byte-identical with `PROF=0`" provable
  by construction). Code comments referencing the old defect are updated to
  point at the fix instead of describing a bug that no longer exists.
- File references below updated from `glm.c` to `colibri.c` where applicable.

## What this adds

One new `PROF=1` line that splits every routing-driven demand expert load into **cold**
(not recently routed) vs **warm** (recently routed — plausibly still in the page cache)
and reports, per class and per profile window:

```
[PROF] DISK-CLASS (recency split): cold N x GG.GG GB @ T.TT GB/s-thread, wall WW.Ws @ A.AA GB/s-wall, avg-conc C.C (direct n/N) | warm ... | disk-busy S.Ss (P% of window)
```

**Read the header literally: cold/warm is a RECENCY classification, not measured
page-cache residency.** When we checked this heuristic against ground truth
(`mincore()` residency probing, separate experiment), the two disagreed on **41% of
classified loads**. The split is stable and meaningful as a *lens* — the per-class
byte/time/concurrency numbers are exact regardless of the labels' semantics — but no
consumer should treat "warm" as "guaranteed cached" (which is also why this PR ships no
policy on top of it; see below). The `(recency split)` tag in the line itself is there
so a log reader can't miss this.

- **loads / bytes** per class (weights + scales, same convention as the `expert I/O` line);
- **GB/s-thread** — bytes / thread-seconds: the per-read service rate, on whichever
  thread ran the read (PIPE workers, OMP loaders);
- **wall / GB/s-wall** — a per-class *busy-wall* tracker (an in-flight counter whose
  0→1 transition stamps a start and whose 1→0 transition accumulates the interval) and
  bytes / busy-wall: the aggregate rate the disk actually delivered while at least one
  load of the class was in flight;
- **avg-conc** — thread-seconds / busy-wall: mean overlap depth of the class;
- **direct n/N** — how many of the class's loads were *actually served* by the uncached
  twin fd (under `DIRECT=0` this reads `0/N` for both classes and confirms the split is
  a pure page-cache-locality signal, not an fd artifact; under `DIRECT=1` it shows what
  blanket direct is doing to each class);
- **disk-busy** — combined busy-wall (either class in flight) as a share of the profile
  window: the disk's demand-read duty cycle.

Zero behavior change: the fd choice is untouched, the line prints only under `PROF=1`
and only when classified loads exist, and with `PROF` off the instrumentation compiles
to a handful of untaken branches (verified by line-by-line inspection of every new
branch's gate in this revision — see Testing below; the original branch additionally
verified this empirically against a no-model baseline on `caa49f7`).

## Why two rate units (the hard-won part)

Thread-second rates and wall-aggregate rates answer **different questions**, and using
one where the other is needed produces confidently wrong conclusions — we did it, which
is why the units are now in the field names. A class of N slow reads that overlap can
deliver more aggregate bandwidth than N fast reads that serialize; per-thread service
rates cannot see that. In our first measurement run the thread-second numbers appeared
to refute a hypothesis that the wall-aggregate numbers then confirmed was about
concurrency structure, not per-read speed. `GB/s-thread` tells you what one read costs;
`GB/s-wall` tells you what the disk is actually delivering; `avg-conc` is the bridge
(their ratio). All three are printed so no reader has to re-learn this the hard way.

## Why measure this at all (motivation numbers, our logs)

On our reference setup (GLM-5.2 int4 on an M5 Max, macOS 26.5, model streamed from
NVMe), a 256-token decode window classified as: **cold ~1062 GB (~71% of the 1491 GB
classified) at 14.2–14.5 GB/s-wall over a 73–75 s busy-wall at avg-conc ~3.3, with the
disk idle ~39% of the window** (logs: our overnight R1 bracket runs, 2026-07-19). That one line characterizes decode as
near-serial — a cold-read phase at the disk's practical concurrency ceiling followed by
a compute phase with the disk parked — which is the load-bearing fact for any I/O
overlap or prefetch work on MoE streaming engines. Getting it previously required
DTrace-level tooling; now it is one `PROF=1` run.

## The classifier, and why it ships without a policy

Cold/warm is decided by a **private per-expert recency clock** (`elast_dc`,
`eaccess_clock_dc`), ticked at routing time in **both** FASE A paths, with a pre-bump
snapshot (`elast_pre`, guarded once-per-call by a `touched[]` bitmap) so prefill's giant
first-touch burst cannot classify itself warm off its own routing bump — a trap that
otherwise silently inverts the labels exactly where they matter most.

Two honest disclosures:

1. **Why a private clock:** at the time this was first written, the engine's real
   recency state (`elast`/`eaccess_clock`) was never bumped on the Metal pre-routed
   decode path — an upstream defect (Metal-decode LRU/repin recency ran on
   prefill-frozen scores). That defect has since been reported and **fixed upstream**
   (#417, `cfcc742` — FASE A now bumps the real clock too), so the private clock is no
   longer the only way to get correct per-mode recency. It is kept anyway: it also
   snapshots pre-bump state so a call's own routing bump can't contaminate its own
   classification (a separate concern from the freeze bug), and keeping DISK-CLASS's
   bookkeeping fully decoupled from stock `elast` state is what makes "`PROF=0` is
   byte-identical" provable by construction rather than by argument against a shared,
   evolving array.
2. **Why measurement WITHOUT policy:** we also built and measured an fd-choice policy on
   top of this classifier (cold → uncached fd). It is not in this PR because the
   premise was **refuted** on our hardware — cold buffered reads were not the
   bottleneck — and because the recency heuristic itself, checked against page-cache
   ground truth (`mincore()` residency probing in a separate experiment), **disagreed on
   41% of

author: elkaix
body:
## Summary

Closes the cross-process cleanup-journal race that an independent review of the 0.21.0 recovery reconciliation and CodeRabbit both flagged: recovery's torn-tail truncation could erase a cleanup intent a concurrent process had just appended and fsynced (worst case a leaked `prune-backup` ref — durability, not a trust break, but real).

## Fix

A new **state-dir-scoped cross-process file mutex**, `acquireCleanupJournalLock()`, keyed by a fixed `sha256` (so `reclaimLocks` reclaims it like any dead lock, and it never collides with repository-identity checkout locks). Every journal mutation now holds it:

- prune's `appendCleanupRecord` (artifact-store)
- recovery's completion/rollback `appendCleanupRecord`
- recovery's torn-tail `truncateCleanupTornTail`

and `replayInterruptedPrunes` **reads and repairs the journal as one critical section** under the mutex, so no concurrent append can land between the read and the truncate.

## Why it's deadlock-free

The journal mutex is a **leaf lock**: it is always acquired last and released before any other lock op. Ordering is invariant — `recovery.lock → checkout-lease → journal-mutex`, or `journal-mutex` alone. It is never held while acquiring the checkout lease or recovery lock. In-process writes remain serialized by the existing `enqueueCleanupJournalWrite` chain.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0
- `npx vitest run` — 889 passed / 12 skipped (+1: new mutual-exclusion + reclaim test for the mutex, runs on all platforms)
- `bash scripts/validate-release.sh` — pass
- `claude plugin validate .` — pass

Release **0.22.0** (PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged — no wire change).

## Note

Branch name says "per-repo"; after investigation the per-repo-journal approach was rejected (null-`repoRoot` records have no repo/lease to key on, plus a format migration), and the maintainer chose the dedicated mutex. The code and this PR implement the mutex.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved crash-recovery for the cleanup journal by serializing intent and completion/rollback writes across processes.
  * Prevented corruption/loss during torn-tail truncation repair by running repair reads/writes in one cross-process critical section.
  * Added deadlock reclaim during startup recovery for stale cleanup-journal mutexes.

* **Release**
  * Updated runtime, plugin, and marketplace versions to **0.22.0** and refreshed the README version badge.
  * Documented the **0.22.0** cleanup journal crash-recovery fix in the changelog.

author: jarllyng
body:
Completes the 1.1 story: the AUv3 tap now feeds the per-bin scenes. Previously it sent only 3 bands + BPM, so Spectrum Ring and the new Ridgeline barely reacted on the DAW path — the workflow the product is built around.

## How
- **Kernel**: channel-0 samples mirror into a 4096-float tap ring on the render thread (plain stores, the existing benign-race convention — no locks, no syscalls). `copyTapWindow()` exposes the newest 2048 samples.
- **PluginSpectrumAnalyzer** (new): vDSP FFT + the app analyzer's exact shaping (log-spaced 64 bins, log1p compression, running-max normalization, attack/release smoothing) so bins look identical whichever side produces them.
- **PluginOSCSender**: one `/echolume/audio/spectrum` message (64 floats, ~350 B) every other tick ≈ 30 Hz, matching the app's own FFT cadence. FFT + send run on the sender's utility queue (#51 invariant preserved).
- **App**: `handlePluginAudio` ingests spectrum frames into the VisualParamsProvider; the local input's spectrum publisher is suppressed while the plugin drives, same as the band publishers.
- Backwards compatible: band messages unchanged; an older app ignores the unknown address.

## Verification
- **App ingest**: injected synthetic 64-bin OSC frames — the Ridgeline terrain drew exactly the injected pattern while the live mic was suppressed (screenshot).
- **Plugin end-to-end**: ran `auval -v aufx etap Iamj` with the app in Live — auval's render signals flowed kernel ring → plugin FFT → OSC → app → GPU history → shader, producing live broadband terrain (screenshot). **AU VALIDATION SUCCEEDED.**

author: mat-arda-cards
body:
Docs only. No behavior change.

## The wrong claim

Four places said a release started without a working `DATABASE_URL` fails safely because **"Render keeps the previous release serving."**

That is **false for these two services**, and planning the production cutover around it is dangerous.

Both `explore-kingston` and `explore-kingston-staging` mount a **persistent disk**. A disk can be mounted by only ONE instance, so Render must stop the old instance before starting the new one. There is no old release still serving to fall back to — a release that never reports healthy takes the service **DOWN**.

## Found by doing it

The E06 release was pushed to staging on 2026-07-19. Staging's `DATABASE_URL` had never been set (it had been running E03-era code that didn't need one), and the service went **502 on every path** rather than continuing to serve its previous release.

`/api/health` behaved exactly as designed — 503 when `dbOk:false`. The wrong part was the belief about what Render *does* with that.

## Why it matters beyond staging

The production cutover step is the same shape — paste `DATABASE_URL` into the dashboard, which triggers a deploy. So the same failure is available to it, **on the live site, during a content freeze**, with the runbook actively reassuring the operator that it can't happen.

## Changes

- `render.yaml` (both services), `docs/DEPLOY.md`, `docs/OPERATIONS.md` — corrected the claim, with the disk reasoning so nobody re-derives the wrong conclusion.
- `docs/RUNBOOK-CUTOVER.md` — new **PRE-FLIGHT** step that validates the exact URL from the operator's laptop before it's pasted into Render:

  ```bash
  URL='<the exact production pooled URL you are about to paste>'
  psql "$URL" -c "select 1"
  psql "$URL" -c "select count(*) from record"
  psql "$URL" -c "select current_database(), inet_server_addr()"
  ```

  A typo, truncated paste, stale password, or wrong Neon branch surfaces there — while the site is still up and nothing has changed. Plus a rollback note (Render's Rollback restores the pre-substrate release, which runs without `DATABASE_URL`; the importer is idempotent so retrying is safe).

author: 74nu5
body:
Premiers tests pour `SettexCompletionHandler` — **699 lignes**, le plus gros fichier du serveur de langage, la fonctionnalité la plus visible des deux extensions, et jusqu'ici **sans aucun test**.

## Ce qui est couvert

Sept tests sur ce qu'un utilisateur voit à chaque position du curseur : les propriétés d'un objet après un point (restreintes à cet objet, pas à ses frères), les variables et environnements déclarés, la liste de mots-clés, une requête sur un URI jamais ouvert — que le client peut réellement produire et qui doit dégrader plutôt que lever — et un document à moitié écrit, qui ne doit pas planter.

## Un test qui consigne une limite, pas un comportement

Propriétés et variables viennent toutes deux de l'AST évalué. **Tant que le fichier ne parse pas — c'est-à-dire la plupart du temps où l'on veut de la complétion — seule la liste statique de mots-clés est proposée.** Le gestionnaire dégrade sans échouer, mais il n'aide pas.

C'est verrouillé par un test qui commencera à échouer le jour où quelqu'un l'améliorera.

## Deux hypothèses fausses, attrapées avant de devenir des garanties

La complétion de propriétés **exige que le document parse** : le `Server.` incomplet que j'avais écrit d'abord ne produisait rien.

Et le cas du **mot partiel** ne se comporte pas du tout comme je le supposais. J'ai **supprimé** ce test plutôt que de l'affaiblir jusqu'à ce qu'il passe — épingler un comportement non confirmé serait une supposition déguisée en vérification, exactement le défaut que la dernière revue a trouvé dans deux tests existants.

## Portée

Ceci couvre **un** des cinq gestionnaires sans tests. Definition, document symbol, synchronisation de document et fichiers surveillés restent à faire.

391 → **398 tests**.

author: nikoz99
body:
First step toward the Helm chart (NOT-19). The dashboard ships as a static
bundle, so reading `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` / `PUBLIC_AUTH_URL` through
`$env/static/public` fixed the origins at build time — fine when we own the
hostnames, unworkable for a chart that publishes one image for every
self-hoster's domain.

Origins now resolve in `src/lib/runtime-config.ts`:

1. `window.__notifbuddy`, set by an inline marker script in `app.html`
2. the build-time `PUBLIC_*` vars — the existing path, unchanged

So the Cloudflare deploy and `vite dev` behave exactly as before, and the
self-host image can be built with those vars empty.

### Why inline rather than a `/config.js` file

A separate file has to be served `no-cache` (it changes per install and per
upgrade), so it puts an uncacheable blocking request on the critical path of
every page load — roughly 1 RTT before the app modules can execute, paid by
every deploy including the ones that don't need runtime config. The inline
marker costs ~40 bytes of HTML and zero requests; the SPA shell is already
`no-cache`, so nothing new becomes uncacheable. Net effect on our own
dashboard is one request fewer than `main` today.

The self-hosted dashboard image rewrites the marker line at container start
(entrypoint lands in the follow-up PR with the Dockerfile).

### Verified

- `npm run check` — 0 errors
- normal build bakes the origin into the bundle; empty-env build leaves no
  baked origin, so the self-host image builds without knowing hostnames
- the marker survives the build on its own line, and a line-addressed `sed`
  replaces exactly it, leaving all 26 `modulepreload` links intact

author: copilot
body:
PR #338 attempted to optimize startup by reusing known partitions/indexes instead of fully rescanning on every open. This change reintroduces that optimization from scratch with a best-effort snapshot model: restore fast when possible, then reconcile lazily with current filesystem state.

- **Startup snapshot model**
  - Added persisted startup-state file: `.<storage>.startup-state.json` in `indexDirectory`.
  - Snapshot contains known partition file names and secondary index names (`versioned` payload).

- **Fast restore on open + lazy reconciliation**
  - `ReadableStorage.open()` now attempts snapshot load first.
  - When snapshot is present/valid, storage opens immediately from known state and kicks off `scanFiles()` in background to discover drift/new files.
  - When snapshot is missing/invalid, startup falls back to full scan behavior.

- **Known-state tracking**
  - Added explicit tracking for known secondary indexes (`knownIndexes`) and unified registration path (`registerKnownIndex`).
  - Partition/index discovery paths now funnel through known-state update hooks.

- **Writable-only persistence**
  - Added `onKnownStateChanged()` hook; `WritableStorage` overrides it to debounce snapshot writes.
  - Snapshot persistence is best-effort and runs on state changes and close.
  - `ReadOnlyStorage` does not persist startup state (read-only remains non-mutating).

- **Race hardening for lazy scans**
  - Background scan callbacks guard against close-time races and rename/delete windows while reconciling filesystem state.

```js
const storage = new Storage('storage', { dataDirectory, indexDirectory });

storage.open(); // restores known partitions/indexes from .storage.startup-state.json when available
// Full filesystem reconciliation continues lazily in background.
```

author: mattias800
body:
## Goal

Advance #1054 by implementing the precisely identified Astro Bot title-shader blocker: compiler-generated PC-relative scalar tables consumed through `s_buffer_load_dword*` SMEM instructions.

This PR also retains the native-Linux investigation handoff on the branch. It does not claim nonblack Astro graphics yet; the Astro dump is not present on this host, so the next live shader frontier remains to be measured separately.

## Failure and contract

Astro's title pixel shader constructs a bounded four-word buffer descriptor from `s_getpc_b64`, with a 64-byte literal table just after `s_endpgm`, then performs scalar buffer loads using a tracked SGPR byte offset. Prosper already proved and folded the analogous MUBUF idiom, but SMEM killed its destination facts without recognizing the PC-relative descriptor. The first `s_getpc_b64` therefore rejected at PC 221.

Arbitrary PC values must remain unsupported. A scalar table is accepted only when the existing forward proof establishes:

- the low address comes from `s_getpc_b64` plus a constant;
- the paired high word comes from `s_addc_u32 ... + 0`;
- descriptor length and configuration words are known constants;
- no branch enters after the newest contributing fact;
- the table is aligned, nonempty, at most 1024 bytes, and completely inside the readable shader window;
- the SMEM opcode and SOFFSET form are supported.

Emission uses the real tracked SOFFSET plus the instruction byte offset, returns zero out of bounds, writes every consecutive SGPR result, and drops stale descriptor provenance. Unproven offsets and unrelated `s_getpc_b64` uses still reject.

## Cache ownership

The narrowly proven post-`s_endpgm` table span participates in the immutable shader copy and cache key. Mutating a selected scalar-table word produces a cache miss and changed SPIR-V.

## Deliberately unaffected

- external SMEM resource binding
- existing PC-relative MUBUF folding
- generic or pointer-producing `s_getpc_b64`
- unsupported scalar stores, negative offsets, oversized/truncated tables, and untracked SOFFSET values
- AGC registered shader-size scanning

## Risk

This is reverse-engineered shader-address behavior. The implementation stays fail-closed outside the exact compiler idiom and is covered by execution, bounds, negative-control, and cache-identity tests. The remaining limitation is lack of a local Astro dump for a live PC-221/next-frontier run on this host.

## Author verification (`6d3defe`)

- `cmake -S prosper -B prosper/build-linux -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DGAME_DUMP=/home/mattias800/repos/ps5ys/PPSA24651-app0`
- `cmake --build prosper/build-linux -j8`: pass
- `ctest --test-dir prosper/build-linux --output-on-failure -j8`: 120/120 pass
- `test_rdna2_to_spirv`: pass, including dynamic offset, consecutive result, truncated tail, broken high half, untracked offset, and code-span checks
- `test_shader_recompile_cache`: pass, including SMEM tail ownership and table-mutation cache miss
- production negative control: disabling only the new SMEM proof match makes both new positive test groups fail; restored before commit
- `PROSPER_GAME_ROOT=/home/mattias800/repos/ps5ys python3 tools/snapshot/snapshot.py check`:
  - Messenger: 29/29 qualifying, structural, and nonblack; 8 pixel changes
  - Evergate: 9/9 qualifying, structural, and nonblack; 8 pixel changes
  - Dead Cells: 44/44 qualifying, structural, and nonblack; 43 pixel changes
  - Blasphemous II: 98/98 qualifying, structural, and nonblack; 97 pixel changes
- `git diff --check`: pass

Independent Fable/xhigh review is required before merge. No screenshot is attached because this is a shader-correctness frontier advance, not yet visible Astro progression.

author: chechooxd
body:
## Resumen
Cierra la sección **Transversal** del roadmap (todo excepto ESM, diferido a v3.1 por decisión del owner) y deja el repo listo para publicar la v3.0.0. Este PR estrena el CI sobre sí mismo: **primera validación end-to-end del código contra bases de datos reales**.

## CI (GitHub Actions)
- **Unit**: matrix Node 18/20/22 — build + typecheck + lint + `jest --coverage` (205 tests).
- **Integration**: Postgres 16 como service container + Mongo 7 replica set de un nodo (arrancado con `docker run --replSet` + `rs.initiate`, porque los service containers no aceptan args de comando). Corre las suites de integración completas: CRUD, realtime (LISTEN/NOTIFY y change streams), query engine, transacciones y relaciones contra bases vivas.
- **Docs**: typedoc generado como artifact.

## Nuevo: suite de integración de MongoDB
Paridad con la de Postgres (CRUD + realtime + query engine + transacciones + relaciones), opt-in con `INDIGODB_INTEGRATION=1`.

## Bug real encontrado al escribir esa suite
Los joins de `include` usaban `Map` con igualdad **por referencia** — los ObjectId de Mongo deserializan como instancias distintas entre queries, así que contra datos reales el eager loading devolvía arrays vacíos/null en silencio. Los tests unitarios no lo detectaban porque reutilizaban la misma instancia. **Corregido** normalizando claves con `String()` + test unitario con instancias distintas del mismo id + cobertura viva en la nueva suite de integración.

## Lint + formato

author: chuenchen309
body:
Fixes #341.

With `namedtuple_as_dict = True`, a `NamedTuple` field that has a default cannot be deserialized from a dict that omits that key — it raises `InvalidFieldValue`, even though the default (`as_list`) engine correctly falls back to the default for an omitted trailing element:

```python
ListForm.from_dict({"p": [5]})        # -> Point(x=5, y='default')   OK
DictForm.from_dict({"p": {"x": 5}})   # -> InvalidFieldValue          before this change
```

**Root cause** (`mashumaro/core/meta/types/unpack.py`, `unpack_named_tuple`): when the NamedTuple has defaults, the generated unpacker catches an exception so the NamedTuple's own defaults fill missing values — but it caught only `IndexError` (raised by list access on a short list). Dict access on a missing key raises `KeyError`, which escaped and was wrapped as `InvalidFieldValue`. The as_list behavior is the tested contract (`test_dataclass_with_named_tuple_with_defaults`); the as_dict path was never extended to it.

**Fix**: catch `KeyError` as well.

```python
-        with lines.indent("except IndexError:"):
+        with lines.indent("except (IndexError, KeyError):"):
```

**Verification** (re-runnable from the diff): added `test_named_tuple_as_dict_with_missing_default_key` (using the existing NamedTuple test entities) — it fails on the current tree (`InvalidFieldValue`) and passes with the fix. A missing *non-default* key still errors, and the no-defaults branch is unaffected (it doesn't generate this fallback). Full suite green.

---

The human account holder reviews every change and is accountable for it. The verification above is real and re-runnable from the diff. If this isn't the kind of contribution you want, say so and I'll close it.

author: gabrielassisxyz
body:
## What

Closes the three items the agent-ergonomics pass-2 follow-up had parked in *"needs a decision"*, which between them blocked the entire remaining apply batch. Documentation only — no code changes.

## Why

Each of the three was filed as a preference call. Reading the code showed that two of them were not, and that the third rested on a claim the code contradicts.

**`ingest queue resolve` — the fence is in the API, not the CLI.** `ResolveReview` treats `""` and `"Skip"` identically and both run `DeleteIngestReview`, so an empty action permanently destroys a review. The CLI's matching default is deliberate and commented: inventing a different one would make the CLI resolve reviews differently from the API it is a client of. That reasoning holds, so fixing only the CLI would have created exactly the divergence the comment exists to prevent. Decided: refuse the empty action at the API and let the CLI inherit it. Rejected a deprecation window — the web UI always sends an explicit action, so the empty-action path has no consumer to deprecate for.

Renamed the shell token `skip` → `discard` alongside it. The two defects share one root: an action meaning "discard permanently" was both the implicit default *and* named after postponing something. The wire value stays `"Skip"`; only the shell-facing token moves, through the translation map that already exists for `create-page`.

**`inbox prep` — the finding was wrong.** It was recorded as "mutates by default; the expensive LLM path is the default". `Prep` short-circuits on an existing prep edge before constructing any prompt, so the bare form and `--show` differ only for a never-prepped capture, and neither costs anything on an already-prepped one. The pair is coherent (get-or-create / get-if-exists); what is defective is that the help never says so. Kept as a *corrected finding* rather than deleted, so a later pass does not reopen the question from the same false premise.

**`task create` — not a taste call.** It was filed as an inconsistency between two defensible designs: `task create` joins stray positional args into the title, `project create` rejects them. But the comment defending the join says the slip is harmless because "the title is echoed back on success anyway", and that verb echoes only the id. Node ids are bare UUIDv7 (`ids.New()`), so the output carries nothing a reader can verify. The asymmetry also has a cause: `project create` can afford strictness because it has `--title`; `task create` has no such escape hatch. Resolved by completing the verb — echo the title, add `--title` — rather than forcing one style onto both.

## Rejected alternatives

- Deprecation warning before refusing the empty action — ceremony with no beneficiary.
- Inverting `inbox prep` to read-by-default, or splitting it into `prep make` / `prep show` — both trade one surprise for another against a fence the code justifies.
- A `--yes` gate on `prep` — it destroys nothing, and using the gate there would dilute the signal it carries on `inbox reopen` and `inbox batch apply`.
- Making `task create` strict like `project create` — reachable only *after* `--title` exists, which makes it a follow-on rather than an alternative.

## Also

Adds a standing note to re-check the CLI whenever the ingest screen or flow is reworked. The two are clients of one contract and the CLI is the one that gets forgotten, because it has no screen to look wrong on.

body:
## Phase

Issue #677. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-19-stop-ratchets-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-19-stop-ratchets.md`.

## Summary

Add deterministic engine-managed stepped and time-tightening stop ratchets with shared paper/live behavior, durable restart state, and venue-position modification where supported.

## Changes

- add stepped MFE and interval-based tightening syntax, AST models, compiler validation, and request models
- manage monotonic stop transitions in OrderManager for long and short positions, including gap-crossed milestones and floor clamping
- persist ratchet cursors, high-water marks, elapsed intervals, and stop levels using backward-compatible journal defaults
- restore ratchet state without generic OCO records masking dynamic stop state
- route live position modifications through broker capabilities while keeping engine-side triggering identical in paper and live modes
- document the behavior, invariants, restart model, and implementation plan

## Tests

- add parser and compiler tests for stepped and time-tightening stop declarations
- add OrderManager behavior tests for long/short transitions, gaps, monotonicity, floors, attached brackets, and venue modification
- add persistence and restart collision tests plus a paper end-to-end parity test
- Local: `./gradlew build -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=daemon` green, 3,723 tests passing, 3 skipped
- Local: `./gradlew test -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=daemon` green

## Backwards compatibility

Ratchets are optional and existing fixed, trailing, and armed stops retain their behavior. Existing journals decode with defaults for the new optional fields. `ENTRY` and `BREAKEVEN` are contextual ratchet targets rather than global reserved keywords, preserving existing identifiers.

## Out of scope

- volatility- or indicator-driven stop policies
- venue-native ratchet primitives beyond position stop modification

## Risk

Medium. This changes the tick hot path, but active work is keyed by order ID, time tightening is O(1), stepped milestones are consumed only once, no historical/global scans or blocking I/O were added, and venue calls remain asynchronous and occur only on tightening transitions. Persistence is written before an asynchronous venue modification.

Closes #677

author: velicanu
body:
Last of the four E2E slices. Losing every device means signing up again; this is what reattaches the old identity's history to the account the person can actually sign for. The server can't vouch for them — so the group does.

## What the fold does

Every reference resolves through an alias map: payers, splits, settlements, comment authorship, and the split recipe's participants, item claims and weights. Two details that matter:

- **Shares are summed, not overwritten.** An expense can legitimately name both identities once an edit lands after the loss, and that person owes the total of the two.
- **Merges chain**, so losing an account twice still works.

## The cycle case, and why it took two goes

A merge cycle is nonsense data, but it still has to fold to *something every client agrees on*. My first attempt stopped mid-walk, which made **both** ends vanish and took their balances with them — balances stopped summing to zero. Fixed by collapsing a cycle to its lowest id.

Then the mutation sweep caught something better: **removing that lowest-id rule failed no test.** The existing cycle test only ever resolved one end first, and either end *alone* folds consistently. But which end gets resolved depends on the order the merges arrive in — so two clients could pick different survivors for the same ledger. That's precisely the divergence this whole append-only design exists to prevent, and it was invisible until I tried to break it. There's now a test that folds both arrival orders and asserts they match.

## Testing

207 tests (37 backend, 170 JS). Seven mutations, all caught after that gap was closed:

| Mutation | Failures |
|---|---|
| Shares overwritten instead of summed | 2 |
| Merged member stays a live member | 2 |
| Settlement `from` unresolved | 1 |
| Comment author unresolved | 1 |
| Cycle has no canonical survivor | 1 *(survived first pass)* |
| Recipe participants unresolved | 1 |
| Recipe weights clobbered | 1 |

## UI

A deliberately plain "someone lost their account?" control on the group page, with two pickers. It's an identity-level claim, and while any member can already edit any expense, this one is easier to miss after the fact — so it says plainly that everyone sees it and it can't be undone. The merge event is encrypted like everything else; who was merged into whom is not the server's business.

## Note on this branch
The working copy hit filesystem corruption mid-way (nine zero-length git objects, including HEAD). Recovered by re-cloning and reapplying the four changed files; `git fsck` is clean and the full suite passes. Nothing was lost, but worth knowing the branch was rebuilt rather than continuous.

author: jamesc
body:
Linear: https://linear.app/beamtalk/issue/BT-2941

## Summary

Follow-up from Claude review bot feedback on [PR #3056](https://github.com/jamesc/beamtalk/pull/3056) (BT-2932 — wire full cross-module `AliasRegistry` into codegen call sites).

`handle_inline_protocol_definition` in `crates/beamtalk-compiler-port/src/main.rs` called `generate_module` without `.with_pre_loaded_aliases(...)`, so a protocol module's `alias_registry` at codegen time was always the empty module-local registry — a protocol source file never declares its own `type Name = ...` (that's a separate top-level declaration), so every alias a protocol method signature could reference is necessarily cross-module/pre-loaded. This meant a protocol module never emitted `-type` attributes for cross-module aliases at all, instead of the precise `user_type` reference BT-2932 wired into the class codegen paths.

## Key changes

- Threaded `pre_loaded_aliases` into `handle_inline_protocol_definition`'s `CodegenOptions` builder (`.with_pre_loaded_aliases(pre_loaded_aliases)`), following the same pattern BT-2932 used at the other three call sites in this file (`handle_inline_class_definition`, `handle_compile`'s class path, `handle_compile_method`).
- Updated both callers (`handle_compile_expression`'s REPL-inline protocol branch and `handle_compile`'s protocol-only file-compile branch) to pass their already-computed `pre_loaded_aliases` through.
- Added regression tests for both callers: a protocol method signature referencing a cross-module alias (`Wrapper`, itself referencing a second pre-loaded alias `Base`) now emits a `{'user_type', 0, 'base', []}` reference and declares the matching named `-type` attributes, instead of silently dropping the alias.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression tests fail without the fix (verified experimentally) and pass with it
- [x] `just test` — Rust, stdlib, BUnit, Erlang runtime tests all green
- [x] `just ci-changed` — build/lint/test/check-corpus/check-surface-drift all green

author: cyber-alif
body:
## Summary

This PR bundles a documentation deliverable and several feature additions to the Doctor's Duty Roster App. Each change is additive and self-contained; the app builds and type-checks cleanly.

## What's included

### 1. User manual (PDF)
A 12-page end-user manual (`NHF-Rooster-App-User-Manual.pdf`) written from a full review of the codebase, aimed at the people who run the roster (Master and roster makers) rather than developers. Covers login/roles, doctors, wards, shift requirements, demands, holidays, roster generation & export, summary, duty-bank fairness, notes, settings/backup, the scheduling algorithm, troubleshooting, and a glossary.

### 2. Roster exports — Excel, Word, and CSV
The Generate & Export page previously exported PDF only. It now offers **PDF / Excel / Word / CSV**:
- **Excel (.xlsx)** — one worksheet per shift as a day × station matrix, plus a Summary sheet (assigned vs. target, nights, cath, OPD) and a Warnings sheet when generation produced any. Uses the already-present `xlsx` dependency.
- **Word (.docx)** — a letterhead document mirroring the on-screen roster: per shift → per day → a station/doctor table with holiday markers. Adds the `docx` dependency.
- **CSV (.csv)** — per-shift matrix plus a per-doctor summary block, UTF-8 with BOM for clean Excel opening.

Export logic lives in a new `src/lib/rosterExport.ts` (pure, data-driven, lazily imported); the export buttons share one busy state so only one runs at a time.

### 3. Backup restore (upload)
The Settings → Backup & Restore section could download a JSON backup but never restore one. Adds a **Restore Backup** upload:
- New `useRestoreBackup()` hook performs a replace-all restore. It **validates the file before touching anything**, then wipes and re-inserts doctors, wards, stations, demands, and holidays.
- **Original IDs are preserved** so `demand → doctor` references stay intact; demands that reference a missing doctor are dropped to avoid FK errors. Stations are flattened from the `{morning,evening,night}` backup shape back into rows.
- The UI parses and validates the file, shows a confirmation with per-type record counts, restores the hospital letterhead + selected month, and reports the result. A standing warning notes that restoring replaces shared data.

### 4. Prototype feature parity
Brings the React app in line with the original single-file HTML prototype:
- **Bangladesh holidays loader** — new `bdHolidays.ts` with fixed national days plus movable religious holidays per year, and a "Load BD Holidays" button on the Holidays page that fills in the selected month (skipping days already marked, warning when a year's movable dates aren't known).
- **Interactive roster editing** — a ward × day grid per shift on the Generate page with tap-to-reassign slots. Edits update the store roster immutably and flow through to the preview, summary, and all exports.
- **Richer summary** — adds category, target/night/cath diffs, OPD range, and Friday-night columns to match the prototype.

## New dependencies
- `docx` — Word (.docx) generation. (`xlsx` was already present.)

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; production `npm run build` succeeds.
- Export libraries exercised against representative data: the `.xlsx` re-reads with correct sheets/rows and the `.docx` is a valid OOXML file (content types, tables, headings, holiday markers all present).
- Logic harnesses pass for the restore transforms (station flattening, orphan-demand FK filtering, ID preservation, download→restore key contract), the interactive-edit slot updates (immutability + replace/add/clear), grid-column dedup/ordering, and BD-holiday month/year filtering including the unknown-year warning path.

## Not included (flagged for discussion)
The prototype's "reset all to defaults" and "change master password" were intentionally left out: in the prototype they operate on local `localStorage`, but in this app data lives in shared Supabase and the master password is a fixed constant by design. Adding them would be a destructive/auth-model change rather than a straight port, so they're deferred pending a decision.

- Adds a `/banner report <user_id> <evidence>` flow so admins/mods can nominate a suspected scammer for the shared ban list, gated by human review rather than going straight onto the live list.
- A single global review channel (`REVIEW_CHANNEL_ID`) receives every report from every opted-in server; anyone holding `REVIEW_ROLE_ID` there can Approve/Reject via persistent buttons, which survive bot restarts.
- Also fixes all 10 issues found by a dedicated adversarial review of this new code, including two critical ones: a race that could silently ban a target while the UI showed "rejected", and a failure path that could permanently orphan a stuck report and block re-reporting that user forever.
- Adds `tests/` (unittest-based, didn't exist before) and 80 tests covering the new logic, and `/banner report-cancel` as an operator recovery command for stuck reports.

author: stasson
body:
Closes #336. First story of the v0.11 fidelity track (epic #344).

## What

A run's measured width credited one letter-spacing step to its own last
glyph. Figma excludes that trailing step from the advance it uses for box
extents and alignment, so every line with non-zero letter spacing measured
one tracking step too wide — shifting right-aligned and centered text, and
wrapping one step early.

The correction is applied to the reported width only:

- `position_line` returns `pen_x - letter_spacing` — glyph `x`/`y` are
  untouched, because each glyph is pushed before its own trailing step is
  folded into the pen.
- `break_lines`'s wrap-fit check compares against the same corrected width,
  so the fit check and the reported width stay in agreement: both apply the
  identical single subtraction after an identical per-glyph fold, so a line
  accepted by the fit check still measures exactly what `position_line` will
  report. (This does not close #223, the pre-existing logical-order vs
  visual-order summation gap on bidi lines — see the review comment.)

Applied per line, not only to the paragraph's last line: each line gets its
own alignment shift and can be the widest line a HUG box sizes to.

## Contract change — read this

This corrects the #310 contract. `letter_spacing` now widens a line by
`n - 1` steps for `n` glyphs, not `n`. The pinning test
`letter_spacing_widens_the_measured_line` is renamed and updated to
`..._by_n_minus_one_steps`, with the reason recorded in its doc comment.
The previous behavior matched CSS2; Figma — and therefore the import
oracle — is the reference here.

## Measured (import oracle, no band retuned)

| frame | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `import-text-axes` | 1.829% | **1.029%** |
| `liga-text` | 2.270% | 2.270% (unchanged — its fixture's letter spacing is 0, so this fix is a mathematical no-op for it) |
| all other import frames | unchanged | unchanged |

E7 render oracle: all 7 frames byte-identical (every E7 fixture uses the
default zero letter spacing). The frozen E7 surface is untouched —
`git diff --name-status main` shows 3 files, all under
`crates/dashscene-typeset/`.

## Verification

- `just build` green (includes `cargo test --workspace`, clippy `-D warnings`,
  fmt, dprint, markdownlint, audit).
- `just test` green, `just lint` green.
- TDD: failing tests written and confirmed red before the fix.
- New tests cover the empty run (no underflow), the single-glyph run
  (0 steps), zero letter spacing (unchanged), glyph positions unchanged,
  the corrected wrap-fit check, and a wrapped multi-line run where each
  line drops its own step.

## Review findings

Full pass in https://github.com/driftsys/dashscene-staging/pull/372#issuecomment-5017288297 — 5 parallel reviewers, no correctness bugs.

- [x] `Line.width` field doc went stale against this change — fixed inline in `5b60948`.
- [x] #223 (differing summation orders) not folded in — deliberately deferred, stays open as debt; rationale in the review comment.
- [x] Overstated float-invariant claim in this description — corrected above.
- [x] "story" vs "debt" wording for #336 — scored below threshold, follows existing convention in this crate.

`just verify` exit 0 on the branch tip.

author: edanuff
body:
The storage-port-exclusive subset of #48's audit fixes, split out after hardware verification showed #48's CDC request-path rewrite caused video artifacts (see #48, now draft, and its FAIL comment). These two fixes never touch the video path — `mem_port_cdc.sv` and the dualrate SDC are untouched, verified by diff scope:

```
hdl/disk/drive_ii.sv       | 20 +++++++++++++++++++-
hdl/memory/mem_port_arb.sv | 30 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-
```

## Fixes

1. **`mem_port_arb.sv` — per-client read latch.** In the fb build, Disk II / HDD / MCU share one arbitrated SDRAM port whose read data (`q`) was wired to all clients simultaneously; any client's read completing replaced the word while `drive_ii` was still consuming its own fetch (up to ~32 CPU cycles later). Each client now latches `q` on its own read completion (combinational pass-through on the completion cycle, since the controller registers `port_q` with `ready`). Also documents the latent burst-misroute at the busy-clear (all clients currently `burst=0`).

2. **`drive_ii.sv` — fetch-completion gate.** The nibble head consumed its fetched track word without checking the SDRAM read had completed; under fb-era lowest-priority contention a delayed fetch silently served the stale previous word. Consumption is now qualified on completion; when pending, the head serves the existing self-sync byte (same as non-resident). The `phi0_posedge` advance edge is untouched.

Classic variant is structurally unaffected (dedicated ports, private per-port `q`) — built as regression.

## Provenance
- Base: upstream/main 02404be0; changes verbatim from the audited f51b0ae1 minus the CDC/SDC hunks
- Timing (clean-rebuilt, zero unrouted nets; 0 setup/0 hold, TNS=0, Fmax ≥ constraint): fb — spi 137.1/4, clk_sdram 115.7/108, clk_logic 67.2/54, clk_pixel 41.5/27; classic — spi 176.2/4, clk_logic 74.6/54, clk_pixel 39.7/27
- Artifacts: fb .fs `8e58bc1b…f5576` · classic .fs `f594948d…925fa`

Hardware artifact-watch re-verification on the known-good rig is queued (the workload that caught #48's regression). The CDC request-path fix remains parked in #48 for redesign with backpressure and a video-prefetch latency budget.

author: jaafer272007-design
body:
Builds the last four vocabularies of the configurability arc from `CONFIG_VOCABULARIES_DESIGN.md` — dispositions, isolation types (upgraded from the boolean), shifts (newly editable), and named frequencies — each a Configuration tenant on the proven catalogue pattern, plus the Configuration area redesigned as one coherent family (design §6).

## The three correctness-critical touchpoints (verified against the real code first)

**1. How #96/#120 key off "Died" → the guard is now unbreakable in both directions.**
Found: `AdtLogic.Dispositions` was a hardcoded array; discharge snapshots the code onto the encounter; the #120 deceased re-admission 409 (`AdtApi`) and the match-card status compared the *stored* string to the literal `"died"` — so history was already snapshot-safe, and the real exposures were **forward** (retiring `died` would make death unrecordable and silently kill the mortality numerator) and **coverage** (a hospital-added death disposition would never arm the guard). **Decision — both halves of the design's either/or**, each closing a distinct hole:
- `DispositionRow.IsDeath` — **immutable at creation** (the edit contract has no such field; rows never delete, so `stored code → row → IsDeath` resolves totally and stably). The server guard, patient status, and mortality statistics all key on it — never the label. *Proven: a custom `brain_death` disposition arms the same re-admission 409.*
- The seeded `died` row is **reserved-unretireable** (409 naming the rule — a rule in code, like the q‹n›h pattern), so a death outcome is always recordable.
- Retiring a recorded disposition never rewrites the closed encounter (asserted).

**2. How #114 uses shift → a managed vocabulary with snapshot semantics.**
Found: `PatientAssignment.Shift` validated against a hardcoded `("day" or "night")`; the model's own comment said "No Shift entity exists". Now seeded `day`/`night` (labels verbatim from the dialog, so existing rows stay valid as data); unknown → 400 naming the active vocabulary, retired → 409; **retiring never touches existing assignments** — proven: an assignment on a run-created `evening` shift survived that shift's retirement and kept rendering through the label resolver.

**3. How order validation uses named frequencies vs the regex → the named set is managed, `q<n>h` stays code.**
Found: the `NamedFrequencies` table (GET-only, seeded 9) ∪ the `^q(\d{1,2})h$` 1–48 bound **in code**. The table gained Active + audit + add/retire/reactivate (no edit — the value *is* what orders store; values matching `q<n>h` are refused as built-in). The regex stays code (the infusion-unit closed-union precedent). Four-code split: shape validation unchanged (a retired value is not malformed — stored orders keep resolving); **retired named → 409 at order create/modify**; new per-drug lists require active ∪ regex (400); the plain frequencies GET serves ACTIVE values (wire shape unchanged); retire is **allowed-but-surfaced** (`referencedBy` names the drugs listing the value, shown in the confirm).

## Isolation — boolean → real IPC types
Found: a seeded boolean on the bedside snapshot with **no write path anywhere** (Statistics honestly said "not tracked"). Now: a managed vocabulary (contact / droplet / airborne / protective + the neutral `unspecified`) and **encounter-scoped precautions supporting multiple types** (the recommendation — contact AND droplet is clinically real). Bedside setter (`POST /adt/encounters/{id}/isolation`, replacement set, `[]` clears) on `observations.record` — any doctor or nurse, exactly the `codestatus.set`/`codestatus.manage` split — audited with the prior set + active role. The roster's `isolation` bool is now **derived** from the open encounter (wire parity — every pill/filter/count unchanged) plus an additive `isolationTypes` tail. **Migration preserved, never guessed:** `isolation:true` → `["unspecified"]` on the open encounter, System-audited, clinician refines; false → nothing; idempotent. Statistics' isolation tile is now real.

## RBAC (per-domain atoms, stated)
`dispositions.manage` / `isolation.manage` / `shifts.manage` → **SeniorDoctor** (the `codestatus.manage` precedent); `frequencies.manage` → **Pharmacist** (formulary governance — the Consultant is 403 there, proven). **None on the office Administrator or System Administrator** (403 both directions, headless + rendered). `/config` route + sidebar any-of gates widened to the four new atoms.

## The Configuration area redesigned (§6)
From four stacked hand-rolled sections to one coherent family: a **grouped section rail** (Hospital / Clinical vocabularies / Catalogues & registry) with active/total chips, RBAC-filtered per session, **one tenant on screen at a time**, per-tenant context blurbs, and **one shared `VocabManager`** now rendering code status + all four new vocabularies (the pattern can no longer drift). Identity/imaging/beds keep their specialized forms inside the same frame (flag: full unification deliberately not forced — their semantics differ). Tokens only; 44px targets; focus-visible ring; `aria-current` on the active section. Consumers rewired: Discharges disposition picker, assignment shift picker, order-form frequency filter, the MC bedside Isolation chip + popover, attribute-keyed mortality/deceased checks, print/AiChat label resolution with raw-code fallback.

## Verification
- **92/92 headless** on dev SQLite **and 92/92 on a fresh-Postgres appliance** (full RBAC matrix ×6 profiles, reserved-died, isDeath immutability, discharge/shift/isolation/frequency state matrices, backfill, roster derivation). The **Postgres run caught a real bug** SQLite tolerated: the frequency-entries projection nested a per-row query inside the open outer reader → Npgsql 500; fixed by materializing first.
- **Live-upgrade replica:** the pre-vocabulary appliance image seeded a Postgres; this build booted on the same database — pending chain incl. `AddConfigVocabularies` applied; the migration's **hand-set defaults proved themselves** (the scaffolded `Active=false` default would have retired the entire frequency vocabulary on upgrade); roster byte-parity on all 14 patients; backfill exactly P-1003 + P-1007 → `unspecified`; double-boot idempotent.
- **28/28 rendered** (Playwright on the staging appliance, screenshots): the three RBAC rails (Consultant / Pharmacist-only-frequencies / office-admin-no-clinical), the died Reserved marker, create→retire→reactivate flows through the UI, `daily — listed by 6 drugs`, the MC chip rendering the **backfilled** unspecified and a nurse refining it to Contact, the discharge picker offering a run-created disposition immediately, the real Statistics tile.
- **Production seed mode:** healthz production, **0 patients**, 6/5/2 vocabularies + 9 active frequencies + `died.isDeath` (the T2 `FORMULARY_SEED` tripwire fired first — correct refusal).

## Suites amended in-PR
- formulary: the frequencies-GET **exactness** assertion ("no management endpoint mutates it" — that premise dies with this PR) → 9-seeded-**subset in seed order**.
- assignments: the invalid-shift probe `evening` → `no_such_shift_e2e` (a hospital may legitimately add Evening; the probe must stay invalid forever).

## Flags
1. The per-patient isolation setter rides `observations.record` (bedside documentation); a dedicated atom is a row edit if narrower gating is wanted.
2. Admission-time isolation capture deliberately not added (precautions typically follow swab/clinical grounds post-admission) — a fast-follow if wanted.
3. Mission Control's unit census still renders a literal "/ 16" denominator (predates the bed registry, outside the `?? 16` family killed in #137) — recorded as a small follow-up.
4. Mock stores mirror the seeds for the no-API demo; mock `referencedBy` stays `[]` (display-only, computed live by the server).

`02_PROJECT_STATUS.md` record + marker ride this PR. Rendered verification before merge: complete (above). Post-merge: the standing server-changing routine

body:
Generated by the `sync-sdks` workflow, then reviewed. Only findings the audit **verified against backend source** were applied.

## What this adds

`AsobiMatches.ListLiveAsync` for `GET /api/v1/matches/live`, plus `LiveMatch` models. The backend gained live match discovery in widgrensit/asobi#197; `GET /api/v1/matches` reads the match *record* table (finished matches, an audit trail, nothing joinable), so without this there is no way to browse a joinable match.

Matches are **unlisted by default** — a game opts in with `listed => true` on the mode — so an empty result is expected until then.

## Three stale models corrected

Each verified against the backend rather than inferred:

- `Player.banned_at` → `metadata`. `asobi_player_controller:sanitize/1` is a positive whitelist emitting exactly `[id, username, display_name, avatar_url, metadata, inserted_at, updated_at]`. `banned_at` was never sent, so the field was permanently null; `metadata` was sent and unmodelled.
- `LeaderboardEntry.metadata` dropped. `format_entries/2` builds `leaderboard_id, player_id, score, sub_score, rank, updated_at` and nothing else.
- `MatchRecord` aligned with `public_record/1`.

## Branch name

Pushed as `feat/sync-live-matches`, not `feat/sync-api`. The remote `feat/sync-api` still holds five commits from **closed, never-merged** PR #15. That work was superseded and landed separately (the typed Vote model via #20, confirmed present on main), but it is not mine to discard, so I left it alone rather than force-pushing.

**`feat/sync-api` is dead and wants deleting** — auto-delete only fires on merge, so closed-PR branches linger.

## Verification

Full Runtime assembly compiled clean against a minimal UnityEngine shim: `0 Warning(s) 0 Error(s)`. No Unity Editor available locally, and the Unity test runner is skipped in CI without `UNITY_LICENSE`, so runtime behaviour here is **verified by compile and review, not execution** — same caveat as #26.

## Summary

- add the first Go workspace module at `services/auth` using Go 1.26.5, Chi and GORM
- add strict configuration, PostgreSQL connectivity, health/readiness endpoints and graceful shutdown

No production database is touched. Migrations only run against the isolated CI database in this PR. Runtime AutoMigrate is forbidden.

This PR introduces a new, currently unconsumed service foundation. Reverting the PR removes the module and CI job. The runtime image does not execute migrations at startup and no CD is included.

author: sanyzrn
body: ## Summary On phone portrait widths, the MagicDust “DBS” / “GRAPHIC” formation was shrinking purely with `viewport.width / 15`, down to ~0.23× — readable but visually small. This adds a narrow-viewport scale floor so the formation reads larger on mobile without changing tablet/desktop behavior. ## Change In `magic-dust-shader.tsx`: ```ts const isNarrowViewport = state.viewport.width < 5; const minScale = isNarrowViewport ? 0.32 : 0.0; const rawScale = state.viewport.width / maxComponentWidth; const scale = Math.max(minScale, Math.min(1.0, rawScale)); ``` ## Tuning notes - Camera is `z=9`, `fov=45` → phone portrait world width is ~3.4 units; pure proportional scale was ~0.23. - Measured formation widths: DBS ~5.2wu, GRAPHIC ~10.4wu, torus ~14wu. - Started from the suggested 0.85 floor; that (and 0.55/0.42) clips GRAPHIC at phone width. - **0.32** ≈ GRAPHIC fit at 360–430px (~1.4× the old proportional scale). Tablet (`vw≈5.6`) and desktop keep proportional scale unchanged. - Torus is wider than GRAPHIC, so a text-sized floor can soft-overflow the ring slightly; raising the floor further clips letter edges.

author: willhea
body:
## Problem

`fetch_bills search` matched query tokens as case-insensitive substrings of the raw BILLSTATUS title. Those titles are typeset, not ASCII, so an ASCII query silently missed them — and the miss read exactly like "no such bill".

Measured over the live corpus (43,267 indexed titles), 1,292 carry non-ASCII:

| class | occurrences |
|---|---|
| curly apostrophe U+2019 | 1,024 |
| en dash U+2013 | 217 |
| accented letters (é á ó í ú É î ã ñ ö õ Ō ō ū) | 78 |
| left single quote U+2018 | 14 |
| soft hyphen U+00AD | 12 |
| em dash U+2014 | 8 |
| curly doubles | 8 |

## Fix

A fold applied to **both** the query and the indexed title in `search_titles`, so it corrects either side's typography rather than assuming which side is "clean". Order is punctuation table → NFD → drop combining marks → letter table.

Stored and displayed titles are untouched; only the comparison key is folded.

Three deliberate calls, all grounded in corpus measurement rather than guesswork:

- **Soft hyphen is dropped, not mapped to `-`.** It has no glyph, so a title containing one looks byte-identical to the ASCII query failing to match it — the most silent form of this bug. Mapping it to a visible character would just relocate the miss.
- **NFD (canonical), not NFKD (compatibility).** NFKD rewrites the modifier letter ʷ to `w`, inventing a match against a phonetic spelling no user typed, and additionally reshapes ligatures, fractions and superscripts. This choice is now pinned by a test, not just asserted in a comment.
- **An explicit letter map runs last.** Letters whose diacritic is fused into the code point (Ł, Ø, Đ, Æ, ß) decompose to nothing under NFD, so without it `lodz` would half-fold "Łódź" to "lódź" and still miss.

Phonetic/modifier letters (ʔ, ə, ɬ, ʷ) and symbols (®) are left intact: they are letters in their own right, not accented Latin ones, so no ASCII form is predictable enough to map without inventing matches. Three corpus titles remain non-ASCII after folding; each stays reachable through its other tokens, since the match is AND-of-tokens.

## Evidence

Live-corpus queries that previously returned nothing:

| query | now reaches |
|---|---|
| `david's law` | David’s Law (117-hr-133, 118-hr-64) — the issue's stated case |
| `berta caceres` | Berta Cáceres Human Rights in Honduras Act |
| `vanessa guillen` | Vanessa Guillén (2 bills) |
| `mentor-protege` | Mentor-Protégé (2 bills) |
| `entree act` | ENTRÉE Act |
| `bildagoteel` | Chí’chil Biłdagoteel Historic District Act |

Non-regression, measured rather than assumed: **41,977 of 43,267 titles keep a bit-identical comparison key**, so behavior is unchanged outside the folded classes, and the fold is idempotent. A sweep using every title and every title-token as a query found **zero** cases where something previously findable now misses.

Folding merges 99 keys where distinct raw titles share a fold, all benign — mostly pre-existing case collisions (`FAIR ACT`/`FAIR Act`) plus the intended `COVID-19`/`COVID–19` pairs. `search_titles` returns one row per bill_id and never dedups by key, so output is unaffected.

Performance: the fold is ~3% of a `search` invocation; the index rebuild from ZIPs (~9.5s) dominates. Precomputing the folded key in `build_title_index` is a reasonable optimization for a future persistent-index world, not needed now.

## Review fixes (commit 3)

A cross-model review found three things the first two commits missed:

1. **Fold ordering was wrong.** The letter map ran before the mark-strip, so `Ǿ` (Ø + acute) folded to `Ø` rather than `O` and the fold was **not idempotent** there. The earlier corpus-wide idempotence check passed only because no such character exists in the corpus — a check that could only see characters the data happens to contain.
2. **The NFD choice was ungated.** Swapping NFD→NFKD left every test in the module green. Now pinned by a test with a positive control, verified red under the mutation.
3. **A content-free query matched everything.** Since the fold drops invisible characters, such a query reduced to an empty token list, and AND-of-tokens over an empty list is vacuously true — returning all 43,267 bills. Now returns no matches. This widened a pre-existing gap for empty/whitespace queries, so the guard closes both.

The third commit also corrects an overstatement in the second: NFKD leaves ʔ, ə and ɬ alone; only ʷ is rewritten. NFD is still correct, but the margin is narrower than originally claimed.

## Tests

Five new tests in `tests/test_fetch_govinfo.py`, all confirmed red before green: punctuation fold (both directions), diacritic fold with preserved phonetic letters, fold ordering + idempotence, canonical-not-compatibility, and the content-free query guard.

Full suite: 1335 passed, 93 skipped, 15 xfailed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

Closes #244
Refs: #10

body:
## JSX email bodies (React Email)

Gmail's composing actions (`message.send`, `message.reply`, `thread.reply`, `draft.create`) now take a `jsx` field: a React Email JSX expression rendered server-side into client-safe, table-based HTML with an auto-generated plain-text alternative (multipart/alternative for free). RTL is declarative — `<Html dir="rtl" lang="he">`.

**Breaking:** the `html` composing input is removed. Hand-written email HTML is the root cause of blank-body, broken-RTL, and cross-client rendering failures; everything it did, `jsx` does correctly. The strict schemas reject `html` loudly, so callers self-correct from the error. Raw-HTML embeds remain possible via the documented `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` escape hatch inside jsx. Reading (`message.get` etc.) still returns `html` of received mail.

## Mechanics

- `_shared/emailJsx.ts` — sucrase-transpiles the expression, evaluates with capitalized `@react-email/components` exports in scope, renders html + text. ~200ms cold (lazy import, once per process), ~2ms warm.
- **Optional peers**, following the playwright precedent: `react`, `react-dom`, `@react-email/components`, `@react-email/render`, `sucrase`. Hosts without them get an install hint at first `jsx` use; failed loads aren't cached, so install-and-retry works without a restart.
- Errors teach: parse failures with position, unknown components list the available catalog, non-element results rejected, empty bodies rejected.
- Reply renders jsx before any Gmail API round-trip — malformed jsx costs zero API calls.
- Action + field descriptions surface the jsx preference at `actions.find` and `actions.describe` time, with a worked Hebrew RTL example.

## Verification

- 15 new tests: schema contracts across all four actions (jsx accepted, `html` rejected, whitespace-only rejected, reply-flag exclusivity preserved), RTL render, text fallback, escape-hatch shape, full error taxonomy
- Full suite: 311 pass, 0 fail; build + Biome clean

author: scouten
body:
Closes #766.

## What

Models Asciidoctor's time-dependent document attributes, which were previously all `Unset`:

- `docdate`, `doctime`, `docdatetime`, `docyear`
- `localdate`, `localtime`, `localdatetime`, `localyear`

This ports Asciidoctor's `Document#fill_datetime_attributes`:

- `local*` are derived from "now"; `doc*` are derived from the source file's modification time (defaulting to "now" when none is known).
- An explicit `docdate` / `doctime` (or `local*`) supplied via the API, header, or body is **preserved**, and the derived `*year` / `*datetime` are computed from it (Asciidoctor's `||=` semantics). `docyear` is taken from a `docdate` only when it has a `YYYY-` prefix, matching Asciidoctor's `(date.index '-') == 4` check.
- The computed `doctime` / `localtime` prints its zone as `UTC` for a zero UTC offset, otherwise a numeric `±HHMM` suffix (mirroring Ruby's `%Z`/`%z`).

## Lazy computation (no parse-time regression)

These attributes are resolved **on demand**, not materialized on every parse. A reference instant is captured once — lazily, the first time a time-dependent attribute is read — and the individual values are computed on the fly in the attribute readers of both `Parser` and the `Document` snapshot (`ResolvedAttributes`). A parse that never references one does **no** clock, environment, or allocation work for them. (An earlier eager version regressed the core parse benchmarks ~13–23% on CodSpeed; the lazy version reports **"will not alter performance"**.)

## Injectable clock (reproducible output)

- **`Parser::with_reference_time(ReferenceTime)`** — pins "now" (drives `local*`, and `doc*` when no input mtime is given). API counterpart of `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.
- **`Parser::with_input_mtime(ReferenceTime)`** — pins the source modification time that drives `doc*` (Asciidoctor's `input_mtime`).
- **`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`** — honored as the reproducible-build fallback when no reference time is pinned (per the [reproducible builds spec](https://reproducible-builds.org/specs/source-date-epoch/)); a malformed value is ignored rather than aborting the parse (this crate has no error channel here, unlike Ruby which raises).

New public type **`ReferenceTime`** (`ReferenceTime::from_unix_timestamp` / `from_local`) carries a local wall-clock instant plus its UTC offset and formats dates/times **without adding a datetime dependency** — civil-date conversion uses Howard Hinnant's algorithm.

### Resolution order

- `now` = `with_reference_time` → `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` → real wall clock.
- doc reference = `with_input_mtime` → `now`.

This treats an explicit API injection as authoritative over the ambient environment (a small, intentional divergence from Ruby, where `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` outranks `input_mtime`). It keeps the ported tests deterministic without mutating process-global env state, and still honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` for the common reproducible-build case where the user pins nothing via the API.

> **Note:** the crate carries no timezone database, so an *un-pinned* clock reads real "now" as **UTC** rather than local time. Timezone-correct, reproducible output comes from pinning the clock or setting `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`. Documented on the API.

## Tests

- The `Date time attributes` context in `document_test.rs` moves from `non_normative!` to executed `verifies!` coverage (all six ported tests), plus tests that pin `local*` with `with_reference_time`, resolve the attributes through the parser via body references (`{docdate}` / `ifdef::docdate[]`), and cover the explicit / value-less / unset `doctime` sibling cases.
- Unit tests for `ReferenceTime` and the `DatetimeContext` resolver (epoch/before-epoch/leap-day conversion, offset formatting, explicit-override precedence, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` parsing rules, `docyear` prefix rule).
- The revision-line spec example whose revision date references `{docdate}` now resolves that reference (the correct spec behavior — the caption says "date derived from docdate"); the test pins `docdate` so the resolved value is deterministic.

All lib tests pass; `cargo clippy`, nightly `cargo fmt --check`, and full patch coverage are clean.

## One thing to confirm

The precedence divergence noted above (an explicit API injection outranks ambient `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, the reverse of Ruby's `input_mtime` vs `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`). Everything else follows Asciidoctor.

author: chandlerrankin98-hue
body:
## Overview

Timeline events now auto-populate the same way connections and characters do. Saving an episode kicks off a background scan that (a) writes per-character events for the new episode and (b) backfills events for older episodes whose (character, episode) pairs were never scanned. Only writes events for **characters you've already tracked** — the endpoint's response is guardrailed against invented NPCs.

## What changed

- **`api/episode-info.js`** — new `want: "events"` mode. When called with `characterNames: [...]`, returns `events: [{characterName, description}]` scoped to those characters only. Server-side filter drops any name not in the caller's list.
- **`src/utils/episodeInfo.js`** — mirrors the new field.
- **`src/utils/scannedEventPairs.js`** — per-campaign localStorage cache of scanned `(charId, episodeId)` pairs. Same pattern as scanned connection pairs.
- **`src/utils/scanEvents.js`** — grouped-by-episode scanner: for each episode, one API call covering all its unscanned tracked characters. New episodes prioritized, then older episodes as backfill. Per-save cap = 25 episodes.
- **`src/App.jsx`** — `runPostSaveScan` now runs `scanConnectionsForNewEpisodes` and `scanEventsForNewEpisodes` in parallel; header toast shows combined counts (`✓ Added N connections + M events`).

## Testing

Verified end-to-end in headless browser (no console errors):
- Add a character, save E1 → 1 events API call for `{Imogen} × E1`, event appears on the Timeline tab.
- Save E2 → 1 events API call for `{Imogen} × E2` only; E1 is NOT rescanned.
- Both events show on the Timeline; no duplicates.
- Existing manual events count as "already handled" and are never re-asked.

## Deploy

No new endpoints, no schema migration. Uses the same `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`.
