body: Part of #5252 `recognize_callee_universe` already computes local-binding, imported-identity, and receiver-shape testimony for every unresolved callee before deciding pass/fail — then discarded that testimony once it had the boolean answer. A removed vendor API, a locally-bound test lambda, a builtin, and a chained-receiver method were indistinguishable on the emitted unclassified locus row: the `reason` field is a fixed template identical for every failure class. ## What this adds - `CalleeResolutionKind` + `classify_callee_resolution` in `recognition/callee_universe.py`, reusing the exact structural provenance the recognizer itself already reads (`_local_source_function_identity`, `_result_call_identity`, `_bound_source_callable_identity`, `call_receiver`) — no new scan, no vendor-name matching, no invented category. - `FactoryGapInfo.resolution_kind` (additive, default `""`). - `universe_coverage_gaps` (`audit_only/universe_coverage.py`) computes it for every gap it emits. - `lift_rpc.py`'s row projection threads it into the factory-walk red row's `extra` dict. - `idd/factory_walk_unclassified_locus.py` projects it onto the locus schema (new optional field, not required for `locus_is_addressable`). ## Classes (what the recognizer genuinely supports) - `imported_unresolved` — resolves to an imported/assigned definition (vendor or otherwise) but no recognizer family covers it. **This is the genuine drain frontier.** - `local_binding` — resolves to a local FunctionDef/Lambda/for-unpacked binding (including module-level test-file helpers, not just function-local ones), not a vendor method. - `builtin` — the call leaf is a Python builtin (checked via `builtins` introspection), not a vendor method, even when no production recognizer table claims it. - `chained_receiver` — receiver is an Attribute/Call expression (`a.b.c.method()`), not a bindable Name. - `unresolved_other` — named explicitly rather than silently folded into another class. - `recognized` — guard value; never emitted on a gap row (gaps only exist when `recognize_callee_universe` already returned `None`), proven by a dedicated test so the classifier never mislabels an accepted call. ## Twins `tests/test_callee_resolution_kind_5252.py`, using the audit's confirmed fixtures: - `pd.DataFrame.lookup` (removed API) → `imported_unresolved` - a module-level test-file lambda → `local_binding` - `hash(x)` → `builtin` - `a.b.c.method()` → `chained_receiver` - a recognized call (`re.compile('x').search(...)`) → `recognized`, never one of the unresolved classes - `FactoryGapInfo.to_json()` carries `resolution_kind`; defaults to `""` when a producer computes none - locus projection carries `resolution_kind` from the row's `extra` dict, and `locus_is_addressable` is unaffected by its presence/absence **Fails-before verified**: reverting the change causes `ImportError: cannot import name 'CalleeResolutionKind'` on test collection. ## Counts unchanged Ran the affected suites (`test_universe_coverage_gap.py`, `test_builtin_callee_universe_sugar.py`, `test_source_path_locus_index.py`) with the change stashed out and restored: identical pre-existing failures both times (36 in the first group, 2 in the second), pass counts differ only by the 9 new tests in this PR. No row is added, removed, or reclassified — the field is purely additive telemetry on gaps the code already emitted. Not merging — coordinator merges after a soundness read. > [!NOTE] > ### Thread callee-recognition outcome into `resolution_kind` for callee-universe gap auditing > - Adds a `CalleeResolutionKind` enum and `classify_callee_resolution` function in [`callee_universe.py`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/5925/files#diff-72e9f915afa350390348a1c277d0c2047b26a0182bb4780c57baf73f30fdcaa8) to classify call sites as recognized, imported-unresolved, local binding, builtin, chained receiver, or other. > - Adds a `resolution_kind` field to [`FactoryGapInfo`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/5925/files#diff-9514f90ab65b3bf3751ed83c7852a96672b4255b935996ca2b3d2bbbcbaa5645), populated via `classify_callee_resolution` in [`universe_coverage.py`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/5925/files#diff-7ebc06dd7d5535234c84a3fde5ff86ed07305340e7a60cd9378f765aed76b7b5) and serialized in `to_json`. > - Propagates `resolution_kind` through [`lift_rpc.py`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/5925/files#diff-ae9ef9552d092f7b88255bb5b999856f8ae03f439f4afbaa391586534eefd335) into `FactoryWalkRedRowDto.extra` and through [`factory_walk_unclassified_locus.py`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/5925/files#diff-db8ef8c5a5b27b72879a4464f03f447e6e4ea527b49ad1242ed6bfff844b0e76) into unclassified locus dicts. > - Adds parametrized unit tests in [`test_callee_resolution_kind_5252.py`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/5925/files#diff-67ffb4d39334697a69a583b35d4cd09cfa50824ce637f3589052f6670a56358b) covering classification and end-to-end propagation. > > > > Macroscope summarized 64c2095. > >

body:
Wires the secret-leak remediation flow to a shipped entry the setup wizard invokes, so a user who has exposed secret keys in old transcripts can resolve them without leaving onboarding.

**What's included**
- A production entry the wizard runs when the user chooses "Review leaked keys": it presents the batched remediation decision (a masked finding table plus four options — redact, redact + rotation checklist, set a standing "secret" posture, or leave) and routes each option to its effect.
- A hardened redaction adapter that derives its own transcript artifact scope (never a caller-supplied project root), recovers the raw key values by re-scanning the in-scope artifacts at redaction time (masked findings stay raw-free), and writes each file atomically with no leftover temp file on either the success or failure path.
- The rotation-checklist deliverable (ordered most-exposed-first, masked tokens only) and a resolved summary reporting the real redacted-key and transcript counts and where the checklist was written.
- A guard in the calibration adjust step that warns before lowering a pack below its stored level — including a pack hardened out of band that surfaced nothing this run — and fails open if the store can't be read.

All local: no network calls, reads and writes only the local store and in-scope transcript artifacts. Full plugin and schema test suites green.

author: cjimti
body:
Closes #631

## What this adds

The platform now emails users when something needs their attention: a teammate shares an asset, collection, or prompt with them, or comments on something they own. Recipients previously discovered shared items only by going looking; this PR builds the notification substrate the ticket calls for, and it is the prerequisite #627 (@mention tagging) names.

Everything is admin- and user-configurable at runtime through the portal, delivery is durable (database-backed queue with retries, survives pod restarts), and the enqueue path never blocks or fails the originating share or comment request.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Triggers
        Share[Share created]
        Comment[Thread comment / feedback]
    end
    subgraph Queue
        Prefs[(user preferences)]
        Rows[(notifications queue)]
    end
    subgraph Delivery
        Worker[Send worker]
        SMTP[SMTP server]
    end
    Share --> Prefs
    Comment --> Prefs
    Prefs -->|off| Drop[Dropped]
    Prefs -->|immediate or daily| Rows
    Rows --> Worker --> SMTP
```

## Admin SMTP settings

- New `platform_settings` table (migration 000080): typed, admin-editable settings sections, designed to hold future global settings beyond SMTP.
- Portal page at **Admin > Settings** and REST at `GET/PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/smtp` plus `POST /api/v1/admin/settings/smtp/test`.
- The SMTP password is encrypted at rest with the existing `FieldEncryptor` (`ENCRYPTION_KEY`) and is write-only: no API response ever includes it (`password_set` reports whether one is stored), and an empty password on update keeps the stored one.
- The send-test action delivers a real email through the stored settings; a disabled or unconfigured setup gets a 409 instead of sending around the master switch.
- Like other admin configuration, writes require database config mode (405 in file mode). TLS modes: STARTTLS (default), implicit TLS, or none for closed-network relays.

## User notification preferences

- New `user_notification_prefs` table (000081). Defaults are immediate delivery with all categories on (no row needed), per the platform's default-on convention.
- Portal page at **Settings** (user section): delivery mode Off / Immediate / Daily digest, plus per-category toggles for shares and comments/feedback.
- REST at `GET/PUT /api/v1/portal/notification-prefs`, self-scoped server-side: only the authenticated caller's own preferences are ever read or written.

## Queue and delivery

- New `notifications` queue table (000082). Enqueue consults the recipient's preferences: off drops, immediate schedules now, daily stamps the next digest window. Wired into all three share creation handlers and both thread-event write sites; an enqueue failure is logged and never fails the request.
- The send worker follows the established indexjobs pattern: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY wakeup with a 30-second poll fallback, 2-minute delivery leases so a crashed worker's rows are reclaimed, and up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff (30s doubling to a 32-minute cap). It is started and stopped by the HTTP composition root around the serve loop.
- Daily digest: one email per recipient per window covering that window's events, at a configurable global UTC hour (default 13:00).
- Retention bounds the table: sent/failed rows purge after 30 days and undelivered rows older than 7 days are dropped as stale, so enabling SMTP months into a deployment never delivers an ancient backlog. When SMTP is unconfigured, queued rows wait without burning retry attempts.
- A per-actor rate limit (burst 30, 6 per minute sustained, per replica) bounds how much outbound email one authenticated account can generate; excess events drop with a log line.

## Branded emails

Responsive, table-based HTML with a plaintext alternative part, sent via `github.com/wneessen/go-mail` v0.8.1 (pinned). Templates cover shares (asset/collection/prompt), comments/feedback, the daily digest, and the SMTP test. Emails carry the deployment's brand name linked to the portal, the implementor footer when configured, deep links to the item (`portal.public_base_url`; asset/collection shares use the token viewer, which works for the recipient without signing in, prompts link to the in-app prompt page), and a link to the recipient's notification preferences. All user-controlled content is HTML-escaped by the template engine, and go-mail's header encoding prevents header injection via subjects or addresses.

## Architecture

- `pkg/notification` holds the substrate: settings/preferences/queue stores, the preference-aware enqueuer, the send worker, the LISTEN adapter, the renderer and templates, the SMTP sender, and the self-scoped preferences HTTP API.
- `internal/platform/notifydelivery` composes it into one startable handle and implements the portal-facing trigger bridge.
- `pkg/portal` gains no new imports: triggers fire through a small `portal.Notifier` interface implemented by the delivery seam, and the preferences routes register onto the portal mux via a registrar hook (the same pattern as the DataHub portal routes). The Platform facade is unchanged; wiring lives in the HTTP composition root.
- New config section, enabled by default when a database is available:

```yaml
notifications:
  enabled: true         # set false to disable
  digest_hour_utc: 13   # UTC hour daily digests are sent
```

## Scope notes

- Digest window is a single global UTC hour (the ticket's open question, resolved as suggested).
- Shares targeted by user ID alone are not notified: no email address exists anywhere in the system for such a recipient. Email-addressed shares, the share dialog's normal path, always notify.
- The default confidentiality notice on shares is viewer chrome and is not rendered as a personal message from the sharer; a custom notice passes through to the email.
- The per-actor rate limit is per replica; multi-replica deployments multiply the cap by replica count, which remains bounded.

## Verification

- `make verify` green end to end: formatting, race-detected tests, total and patch coverage gates, lint, gosec, govulncheck, Semgrep, CodeQL, 332 frontend tests plus lint and e2e, documentation gates, migration gate, and the GoReleaser dry-run.
- Real-Postgres integration tests (`make test-realdb`) prove the store SQL against the actual schema: the `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim, expired-lease reclaim, digest batch claiming, retry scheduling, permanent failure, retention purge, encrypted settings round-trip, and the preferences CHECK constraint.
- An end-to-end test drives the real share handler over HTTP through the real bridge, enqueuer, worker, and renderer to a captured SMTP sink, asserting the branded email, its deep link, and the queue row's transition to sent; a companion test proves digest batching. A live localhost SMTP conversation validates the wire path.
- Architectural gates hold: frozen Platform field/method ceilings, package size budgets, the import ratchet (new edges recorded in the allowlist), and the vaporware gates (every new table has non-test DML consumers).

## Documentation

New Email Notifications docs page, plus updates to the configuration reference, admin and user portal guides, README, llms.txt/llms-full.txt, the example config, and CLAUDE.md (package list, migration count, config block).

author: florianpfaff
body:
## Bug

On the PyTorch backend, `backend.linalg.fractional_matrix_power(A, backend.array(0.5))` passed the scalar tensor directly into SciPy. SciPy then attempted NumPy exponentiation with a PyTorch tensor and raised `TypeError`, even though the equivalent Python-float exponent worked.

## Fix

- convert the exponent through the existing no-gradient CPU/NumPy bridge
- require the converted exponent to be scalar
- pass its Python scalar value to SciPy
- add a backend-portable regression using a PyTorch scalar tensor exponent

## Impact

PyTorch callers can use backend-native scalar exponents consistently with other scalar-like linear-algebra arguments. Non-scalar exponents now fail early with a clear error instead of reaching an opaque SciPy failure.

## Validation

- reproduced the pre-fix SciPy/PyTorch `TypeError`
- exercised the patched bridge on a `diag(4, 9)` square-root case
- verified explicit rejection of a one-dimensional exponent tensor
- compiled both changed Python files with `py_compile`
- GitHub Actions will run the repository test and backend matrix on this PR

author: florianpfaff
body:
## Bug

The PyTorch quantile compatibility wrapper accepted both a non-default `method` and the deprecated `interpolation` alias, then silently let `interpolation` override `method`. NumPy rejects this ambiguous call, so identical backend-portable code changed meaning only under PyRecEst's PyTorch backend.

For example, `quantile(..., method="nearest", interpolation="linear")` returned a linear quantile instead of raising.

## Fix

- reject simultaneous `interpolation` and non-default `method` arguments
- retain support for `interpolation` when it is used by itself
- apply the behavior to both `pyrecest.backend.quantile` and the raw PyTorch backend through the existing runtime contract patch
- add a portable regression covering the conflict and the valid deprecated-alias path

## Impact

Ambiguous quantile calls now fail consistently with NumPy instead of silently selecting one interpolation rule.

## Validation

- `python -m py_compile src/pyrecest/backend_support/_pytorch_quantile_empty_batch_contract.py tests/backend_support/test_pytorch_quantile_contract.py`
- exact runtime-patch harness with PyTorch 2.10 verifies both public/raw backends raise for conflicting selectors and still accept `interpolation` alone
- repository diff is limited to 7 implementation lines and 34 regression-test lines

author: michaeltaylor3d
body:
## What
Ship dig-merkle v0.3.0 (MINOR 0.2.0 -> 0.3.0). Headline: `resolve_owner_did` — the chain-walking COMPLEMENT of the pure `did_ref_from_spend`. Walks a store's launcher lineage via an INJECTED `dig_chainsource_interface::ChainSource` to discover the store's OWNER DID, returning a lightweight `DidRef` (launcher-id ref). Plus two hardening items + docs.

## Why (NC-9, money-critical identity attribution)
A wrong owner = mis-attributed ownership. Design is FAIL-CLOSED: the owner must be PROVEN from chain, never guessed. An inconsistent/lying/erroring source returns `Err`, never `Ok(None)`.

## Changes
- `resolve_owner_did<S: ChainSource>(store_launcher_id, &source) -> MerkleResult<Option<DidRef>>` (manual lineage decompose + identity-consistency guards, fail-closed)
- new `MerkleError::Source(String)` variant (chain-source could-not-answer)
- `did_ref_from_spend` rustdoc: NC-9 caller-proof precondition
- `mint.rs` fee `checked_add` overflow guard + regression test
- docs: lib.rs / read.rs / SPEC.md / README.md; version -> 0.3.0

## Blast radius
New public fn + additive error variant; `did_ref_from_spend`/`DidRef` unchanged. mint fee path now returns Err on overflow (was UB/panic). Backwards-compatible -> MINOR.

Refs DIG-Network/dig_ecosystem#1227

author: tautschnig
body:
`operator+=` and `operator-=` pass the right-hand side's digit buffer into the private `add()` method, which resizes `*this` before reading from that buffer. When the right-hand side is `*this` itself (`x += x`, `x -= x`) and the result requires a larger buffer, resize replaces and frees the digit array, and `add()` then reads the operand's digits from freed memory. Address sanitizer flags the read; the computed value may be silently wrong. The bug went unnoticed because no in-tree code self-adds a BigInt, and buffers constructed via the numeric constructors carry enough spare capacity to make small self-additions stay in place.

Per our policy that operand aliasing must never be supported, self-aliased operands now abort loudly instead of silently computing garbage:

1. **Addition/subtraction:** `add()` aborts when the operand's digit buffer aliases `this->digit` (which is exactly the `x += x` / `x -= x` case, since distinct BigInt objects never share buffers). Doubling can be spelled `x + x` or via a copy of the operand.

2. **Multiplication/division:** `mul()` was safe for `x *= x` only by inspection of its current implementation, and self-multiplication is not hypothetical — `pow()` squared its base via `a *= a` on every iteration. `pow()` now squares via a temporary, and `mul()` aborts on self-aliased operands like `add()`. `operator/=` and `operator%=` handled self-aliasing correctly through the value-equality fast path, but abort as well to keep the library-wide contract uniform: a BigInt operand must never alias `*this`. Operands merely equal in value are unaffected.

Unit tests cover doubling, self-subtraction, squaring, division and remainder through a distinct copy of the operand — the supported spelling — using string-scanned values whose buffers have no spare capacity, so the buffer growth in `add()` is genuinely exercised. The abort paths are not unit-testable with Catch2 (no death tests).

author: pkkjassistant-commits
body:
One box over **8,068 entities in ten layers**. Typing "Fresno" returns **64 results in 7 layers** — the city, the county, Fresno Unified, the county office of education, the CSU campus, a charter school, and 58 special districts.

**Page:** [`search.html`](search.html) · **Index:** `search-index.js` · **Builder:** [`pipeline/build_search_index.py`](pipeline/build_search_index.py)

## Payload

| | raw | gzipped |
|---|---:|---:|
| `search-index.js` | 476,799 B | **88,147 B (86 KB)** |
| `search.html` | 24,849 B | ~7 KB |

Loaded **only** by `search.html`. No existing page pays for it.

Two lossless compressions got it there from 907 KB / 145 KB: 7,626 of 8,068 identifiers are just the slugified name and are stored empty (−52 KB gz), and the 2,181 distinct qualifiers are interned (−5 KB gz).

## The trap, and how it's handled

The index **carries no figures at all**. Not "figures we choose not to show" — the entry shape is fixed at five fields (`name, layer, id, notes, qualifier`) with no room for one, and the suite asserts it.

That's the answer to the real problem: a city, the county containing it, its school district and its community-college district spend on overlapping populations, with different responsibilities, on different accounting bases. Four numbers side by side invites exactly the arithmetic the rest of the site refuses. So a result **names an entity, names its layer, names that layer's basis**, and says whether the entity carries comparability notes. To see a number you follow the link into the layer, where the figure appears with its own caveats attached.

Asserted, not just intended:
- not one dollar figure may appear in the results view
- the page may never say "combined", "total spending", "altogether", "sum of", "in total", "grand total"
- every group must name its layer **and** state its accounting basis
- the standing "these layers do not add" statement is on the face

Groups are ordered by how well the query matched **inside** them — that ranks the query's relevance, never the layers against each other.

## Daggers surfaced

An entity carrying comparability notes in its own layer says so rather than presenting a bare name. **801 of 8,068** entities carry at least one. `University of California, San Francisco` shows `† 4 notes`; `San Francisco Unified` shows `† 1 note`. Every flag counted is one the layer already publishes and displays — for cities, the exact rule `cities.html` itself uses (a services-checklist code other than A or B).

## Names match their own pages

Community-college districts are title-cased exactly as `ccc.html` renders them (the portal publishes upper case). CSU and UC campuses use the source names their pages show — my first pass constructed "California State University, San Francisco State University", which is wrong twice over. Where a system's published name differs from its campus names, that system name is searchable as a layer term taken from the layer's own `meta.sourceLabel`, so **"University of California" finds campuses filed as "Berkeley"** without inventing an alias the source doesn't carry.

## Identifier discipline

Storing ids as "empty = slugify(name)" is a *derived identifier* — the exact fragility removed from the K-12 pipeline in #22. So the builder proves the round-trip for **every** entity against the real data files before shipping (7,750 checked, 0 unresolved), and the suite re-proves that every indexed identifier resolves to a real record in its own layer.

## A regression this caused, and the honest fix

Adding Search made **eleven** primary-nav destinations, which wrap to six rows in the phone nav's two-column grid and pushed the front door's statement to 374px — past an existing above-the-fold assertion (`top <= 340`).

Rather than relax that threshold, I fixed the actual problem: the **change record moved out of the primary nav**. It is a provenance surface like About & method, and stays reachable from every footer and from about.html's own section on it. Ten destinations, five rows, assertion passes on its original terms.

## Accessibility

Labelled box, `aria-live` result count, each group an addressable `section` with `aria-labelledby`, results are real `<a>` elements (keyboard-reachable, open-in-new-tab). ArrowDown from the box enters the results, ArrowUp from the first result returns to it. No horizontal overflow at 360, 390 or desktop — all asserted.

Permalinks: `search.html#q=Fresno`, updated as you type and restored on load.

**1176 assertions pass** (+40).

author: jfrench9
body:
## Summary

As the disclosures surface grows, rs-gaap will evolve wholesale (reseeds, new packages) — tenants must not fork it. This PR draws the authoring boundary: **tenants author in their own extension namespace and anchor to library structures; declaring elements under a library-owned prefix is refused.**

- New validation phase `namespace_protection` → issue `library_namespace_reserved`: rejects any envelope element whose qname prefix belongs to a library-seeded namespace (`rs-gaap`, `disclosures`, `styles`, `cm` today). The reserved set is derived from the seeded rows themselves (distinct prefixes of `library-seeder` elements), so future library packages are protected automatically with no config.
- **References stay legal**: arcs and `parent_ref` pointing at library qnames — the extend-and-map pattern (#886/#892) — resolve exactly as before. Only *declarations* are guarded.
- Applies to create and, via the update projection, to `update-taxonomy-block`, across all three writable block types. Existing library-row protections (`library_element_immutable`, `library_origin_smuggled`) guard the real rows; this closes the remaining gap where a tenant could mint a *new* element claiming a library qname, which would shadow the real concept nondeterministically in schema-wide qname lookups and mislabel exports.

## Testing

- 4 new validator tests (rejection, own-namespace acceptance, extend-and-map reference legality, empty-library no-op); 460 tests green across `tests/operations/taxonomy_block` + `tests/operations/information_block`; `just test-code` clean
- Live negative probe: `create-taxonomy-block` with an `rs-gaap:` element → 422 `library_namespace_reserved`
- Full Driftline demo e2e unchanged: notes author (`driftline:`/`coa:`), update-path probe passes (footing rule → 4 children), Arelle valid, SHACL conforms

body:
## 概要

Firestore → D1 / Firebase Storage → R2 のデータ移行スクリプト一式を `server/scripts/migration/` に追加する。

Part of #186（plan「実行手順 > PR 2」）。仕様は `doc/plans/2026-07-20-data-migration-bigbang-switchover.md` の決定事項 2〜5 に準拠。

## 構成

- **export.ts**: firebase-admin で Firestore 全 8 コレクションを NDJSON スナップショットへ保存。アバター画像（デフォルト 3 種 + カスタム）も export 時点でダウンロードし、import がスナップショットのみで完結する
- **import.ts**: スナップショット → 変換（transform.ts）→ SQL 生成（sql.ts）→ `wrangler d1 execute --remote --file`、アバターは `wrangler r2 object put`。冪等性は wipe-and-reload（DELETE 子→親 → INSERT 親→子）。drop/補完の件数と ID を移行レポートに出力
- **verify.ts**: 独立検証器。transform/avatar/sql/import を import せずスナップショットから期待状態を再計算し、D1 実データ・R2 オブジェクトと全件・全フィールド突合。移行レポートとの整合も確認
- 不整合ポリシー: words 正規化衝突・未知の profileImageUrl パターンは fail-fast / FK 孤児は drop + ログ / UserConfigs 欠損はデフォルト補完 + ログ

## 設計判断

- アバター分類は URL 全文字列一致ではなく Firebase Storage ダウンロード URL から取り出した「バケット内オブジェクトパス」で判定（ダウンロードトークンはローテーションし得るため）
- `readingSubGroup` / NFC 正規化はサーバー本体の関数（`server/src/words/reading-sub-group.ts`, `server/src/lib/normalize.ts`）を import して再計算し、書き込み時のサーバー挙動と一致させる

## 検証

- `bun run typecheck` / `bun run lint`: エラーなし
- テスト: bun test 62 件（migration 純関数）+ vitest 93 件、全件パス

Closes #129. Part of the run-aware comparison epic (#127).

Adds `EvalData.paired_run_differences(model_a, model_b)`: for each example that carries repeated `runs` for **both** models, aligns the runs by index (truncated to the shorter) and returns one array of per-run differences (`score_B - score_A`). Examples without runs for both models are omitted.

author: finbarargus
body:
Two independent fixes that were sitting uncommitted in the primary checkout.

## 1. MPI launcher / runtime mismatch

Calibration multistart with MPI aborted:

```
Abort(471483664): Fatal error in internal_Init_thread
check_MPIR_CVAR_PMI_VERSION(167): Runtime environment uses unsupported PMI version PMIx
```

**Root cause.** The launcher and the MPI runtime are chosen by two *uncoupled* mechanisms:

| | resolved via |
|---|---|
| `mpiexec` (launcher) | `PATH` — CUFLynx used `shutil.which("mpiexec")` → system **Open MPI** |
| MPI runtime | `mpi4py`'s `dlopen` of `libmpi` — follows `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` |

When those pick different MPI implementations, every rank aborts at `MPI_Init`. The PMIx message is the Open-MPI launcher's PMIx server talking to an MPICH-linked runtime (`libmpi.so.12` = MPICH, `libmpi.so.40` = Open MPI 4.x).

**Fix.** New `resolve_mpiexec(python)` in `calibration.py` locates the launcher in the *selected interpreter's own* `bin/`, so launcher and `mpi4py` are matched by construction. Falls back to `PATH` when that environment ships no launcher, preserving the old behaviour exactly. Wired into all three job managers — `calibration.py`, `sensitivity.py`, `uq.py` — which each had the identical `shutil.which("mpiexec")` bug.

The user-facing fix path becomes `pip install mpi4py mpich` into whichever interpreter CUFLynx uses: the wheels drop `mpiexec`/`hydra_pmi_proxy` and `libmpi` into `<sys.prefix>/bin`, so no system MPI is involved.

Implementation notes (deliberate, please don't "simplify"):
- bare command names (`"python3"`) are resolved to a real path first, else `.parent` is meaningless
- `shutil.which(name, path=bindir)` confines the search to that one dir *and* still handles Windows extensions + the exec bit

## 2. No OpenCOR, ever

CUFLynx does not bundle OpenCOR, so CA's `CVODE_opencor` must never reach the UI. `UNSUPPORTED_SOLVERS` is now filtered out of `solvers_by_format`, the per-format default, `methods_by_solver` and `solver_info_schema`.

CA lists `CVODE_opencor` as a `cellml_only` solver **and its default**, so the default-substitution branch is load-bearing — `cellml_only` falls through to `CVODE_myokit`. The filter composes with the `SOLVER_INFO_FIELDS` introspection from #55 rather than replacing it. Documented as a standing constraint in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Tests

- 3 new tests for `resolve_mpiexec` — real files on disk, **no mocking**, so they genuinely fail against the old `shutil.which` behaviour
- regression test asserting `CVODE_opencor` appears in no solver list, no schema, and is not the `cellml_only` default

**Backend:** 208 passed, 1 skipped, 25 deselected
**Frontend:** 184 passed (23 files), `npm run build` clean

### Pre-existing failures, not from this PR

`test_casadi_tolerance_fields_restricted_to_adaptive_methods` and `test_casadi_max_step_field_offered_for_bdf_only` fail with `KeyError: 'methods'` **when a `circulatory_autogen` checkout is present**. Verified identical on clean `origin/main` (`f1ae9f3`). #55's `solver_info_fields_by_solver` path drops the curated per-method gating, so the `methods` key is absent — but the tests only surface it when CA is importable, which is why CI (no CA sibling → fallback schema) stays green. Worth a separate issue.

author: chaerem
body:
## WP-126 · Live-koherens (eierbestilling 20.07: «bedre visning for det som pågår live, virker litt random»)

**Rotårsak (verifisert):** tre usammenhengende live-begreper —
- (a) web «Direkte nå» (`live.js renderLive`) viste KUN ESPN-pollede sports (fotballscore/golf/F1); en TdF-etappe/sjakk/CS2/friidrett vises aldri der uansett;
- (b) tidsvindu-«pågår nå» (`followed.js`) er sann kl. 03 for flerdagsevents (impliserer aktiv økt);
- (c) iOS `liveNow` beregnes kun ved reload, tikker aldri, kan vise ferdigspilt event som live.

## Løsning — ÉN delt live-definisjon

`ssLiveState(event, now)` (web, `docs/js/shared-constants.js`) ↔ `AgendaViewModel.liveState` (iOS) — speilet 1:1 med felles sport-default-tabell:

- **`'direkte'`** = nå ∈ `[time, effectiveEnd]`, der `effectiveEnd` = `endTime` når det er en plausibel økt (≤ ~24t), ellers sport-typet default fra start: fotball ~2t15, F1-økt ~2t, sykkeletappe ~5t30, sjakkrunde ~5t, CS2 ~2t30, tennis ~3t30, golf-dag ~10t, ellers ~3t. Autoritativ in-progress-`status` vinner outright.
- **`'pågår'`** = flerdagsturnering (`endTime` > ~24t etter start) UTENFOR plausibelt Oslo-dagsvindu `[08–22)` — rolig tilstand, ALDRI live-dot (fikser 03:00-buggen). Innenfor vinduet → `'direkte'`.
- **`null`** = ikke startet / ferdig.

Heuristikk, dokumentert og bevisst **konservativ**: heller `'pågår'` enn falsk `'direkte'`.

## Per flate

1. **Web «Direkte nå»** (`live.js`): viser ALLE `'direkte'` tavle-events som rolige rader (when·what·where). ESPN-score/leaderboard **beriker** raden der pollingen har data — score er bonus, ikke inngangsbillett. Golf/F1 forblir ESPN-poll-eid (det pålitelige signalet for de to; unngår falsk `'direkte'` fra det grove dagsvinduet). TdF/sjakk/CS2/tennis + upollet fotball vises nå. `hasLiveEvents` gated på delt def ⇒ 60s-tikk også for ikke-ESPN-sport.
2. **iOS** (`AgendaViewModel.liveRows` → `liveState == .direkte`): lett minutt-tikk via `TimelineView(.everyMinute)` + `currentLiveRows(now:)` (Reduce-Motion-vennlig, ikke per-sekund) så linja er sann mellom reloads. Cap på to beholdt (DESIGN §4).
3. **`followed.js relDay`**: bruker delt def — flerdags kl. 03 sier «pågår» (ikke «pågår nå»).

## Grenser (holdt)
`docs/data` urørt · News/Sync/EventDetailSheet urørt · **Widget urørt (WP-127 eier fila, merget i #339)** · predikatene/gylne vektorer bit-like (live-visning er ikke kompilering).

## Tester
- Web: `ssLiveState`-matrise (uten endTime→default, flerdags 03→pågår / 14→direkte, ferdig→null, TdF midt i økta→direkte, in-progress-status vinner) + `directLiveEvents`/`liveEventRow`/`hasLiveEvents` (ikke-ESPN-sport synlig i linja).
- iOS: `liveState`-speilingstest (samme matrise) + `liveRows`-eksklusjon av flerdags 03:00.

## Verifisering
- **699 JS-tester** grønt (`npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1`).
- **Full iOS unit-suite grønn på rebaset tre** (604 test cases, inkl. gylne `FeedVectorTests` bit-like) + **alle 4 schemes bygger** (Sportivista/Widget/UITests/DeviceDev).
- `npm run screenshot` begge temaer: rolig, ingen regresjon (natt ⇒ ingen falsk «Direkte nå»).

body:
Lands the DB-backed, admin-managed, **multi-provider** SSO, and stores each provider's client secret **encrypted at rest**.

## Multi-provider (earlier commits on this branch)
Replaces the flat `Org.sso_*` columns with per-tenant `SsoProvider` rows + a registry-wide `SharedSsoProvider` set, merged tenant-wins. Each enabled row is a "Sign in with …" button at `/login/sso/{slug}`.

## Encrypted client secret (this PR's addition)
`SsoProvider` + `SharedSsoProvider` now carry `client_secret: Cast<EncryptedString>` (XChaCha20-Poly1305, key from `RUSTANGO_SECRET_KEY`) instead of a `secret_ref` env/vault handle. Each tenant stores **its own** secret in its own row — no per-tenant env var, no plaintext in the DB. Decrypted in-memory only for the IdP token exchange (sent over TLS, as OAuth requires). `admin-sso` now depends on `casts`.

## Notes
- Requires `RUSTANGO_SECRET_KEY` on the app (the AEAD key).
- Worked around #1161 (empty-string `default = ""` → invalid DDL).
- Verified locally end-to-end via cms_demo: add provider in the admin UI → secret stored as ciphertext in the DB → login button renders → `/login/sso/{slug}` resolves the decrypted secret.

body:
Implements RM-REQ-020/021/022:

- RM-REQ-020: remediation tasks created by the compliance audit are ordinary tasks, so they already go through gateLoop.ts's existing tiered task-escalation ladder (retry -> escalate model tier -> park) with no separate ladder needed.
- RM-REQ-021: repeated audit failures (a re-audit after a full remediation cycle still finds issues) now escalate the *audit's own* model tier via a new `auditorTiers` ladder in config/models.ts, mirroring executorTiers' shape. Tracked per-PBI via new `auditTierIndex`/`lastAuditHadFindings` fields on PbiRecord.
- RM-REQ-022: persistent failure at the highest audit tier after a full remediation cycle parks the entire PBI (status: blocked) instead of creating further remediation tasks, and gateLoop.ts raises a dedicated async human escalation entry for it.
- Escalation entries distinguish scenarios via failedGate: "compliance-audit-tier-escalated" vs. "compliance-audit-pbi-parked", separate from the existing first-pass-finding path (which already has a trail via its created remediation tasks).

ComplianceAuditResult now carries scenario, auditTierIndex, and pbiParked so callers (and tests) can distinguish clean / first-pass / audit-escalated / pbi-parked outcomes.

body:
Formalizes "a capture" as a run — the pipeline's atomic unit — and adds the command that registers one.

Manifest schema (schema_version: 1): run id, capture date, frame count, UE map, drone model, camera sequence, with reserved fields for future domain-randomization params. Validated on construction; unknown versions and unknown fields rejected.

dronesynth ingest: validate → copy → manifest last. A broken capture is rejected before anything is copied; frames flatten into raw/<run_id>/{normal,mask}/frame_<index>.png. The manifest is written only when every frame is in place, so a run without one is always debris from a failed ingest (a retry clears and redoes it) and a run with one is immutable - re-ingesting an existing id is an error.

dronesynth convert --run-id: consumes registered runs only - no manifest means refusal, and a manifest/disk frame-count mismatch means refusal. Explicit --normal/--mask flags removed.

Verified by registering the real 150-pair capture as run_0001 (map testLevel, drone White_Drone) and re-converting from it: output is byte-identical to the previous direct-path conversion (labels, images, QC), except annotation source filenames reflecting the flattened layout.

**Gap:** `_resume_periodic_entry` in `src/robotsix_chat/subsessions/resume.py` (line 171) does not extract or pass `dedup_key` to `spawn_subsession`. After a server restart, periodic ticket monitors that had a `dedup_key` set would lose their dedup registration because the resume path never re-registers the key.

Compare `_resume_periodic_entry` (lines ~187–198):
```python
def _resume_periodic_entry(...):
    ...
    spawn_subsession(
        env=env,
        kind=SubsessionKind.PERIODIC,
        owner_session_id=owner,
        **_entry_to_common_kwargs(entry),
        max_runs=...,
        sub_id=sub_id,

        checkpoint=...,

```

With `_resume_user_chat_entry` (lines ~220–228) which correctly does:

    dedup_key = _entry_opt_str(entry, "dedup_key")
    spawn_subsession(
        env=env,
        kind=SubsessionKind.USER_CHAT,
        owner_session_id=owner,
        **common,
        sub_id=sub_id,

## Summary

- restore Python test and live-helper imports for the `km003c_lib` module
- correct StartGraph rate serialization and document logical indices versus wire bytes
- isolate transaction-splitter state per capture file while keeping transaction IDs globally unique
- make the Streamlit entry point invoke the dashboard

## Root causes

The StartGraph rate index is a control-header attribute, so logical values `0..3` serialize as wire bytes `0x00/0x02/0x04/0x06`. One raw Python helper bypassed the bitfield serializer and the documentation conflated the two representations.

The transaction splitter globally sorted a combined dataset by `frame_number`, even though frame numbers repeat in every capture. This allowed one logical transaction to contain frames from multiple source files.

author: amirhussain-informat
body:
## Summary

The fused join path (`fused_join_aggregate`) rejected any `Filter` under the
Aggregate's join tree, so **every star-join query with a `WHERE` deferred to
cuDF** — missing the fused kernel's no-materialise probe + accumulate.

This PR removes that restriction by **folding the WHERE into the fused plan**,
with **no C++/CUDA change** — both folding strategies reuse existing
descriptors/kernels.

## How the optimizer lays it out

The optimizer pushes every single-table `WHERE` conjunct to a `Filter -> Scan`
node **under** the join tree (only cross-table / OR predicates stay above as
`Filter -> Join`). `fused_join_aggregate` now collects those `Filter -> Scan`
predicates and folds them:

- **Fact predicates** → the kernel's existing `pass_pred` descriptor
  (`pred_col`/`pred_op`/`pred_lit`), already evaluated on fact columns at row
  `i` in both join kernels. This is the exact machinery the non-join
  `fused_aggregate` path uses (`_flatten_and_pred`).
- **Dim predicates** → filter the dim frame **before** its HT is built, so a
  fact row probing a filtered-out dim key misses → inner drop. Pure
  Python/cuDF via `eval_expr` (`ryudb/exec/ops.py`).

### The `get_codes` cache gotcha

The last (group-key) dim is factorised directly off the **filtered** frame.
`engine.get_codes` caches by `(table, col)` over the **full** scan, so for a
filtered dim it would return stale full-frame codes (wrong length / wrong
row alignment → garbage grouping). Middle-dim payloads (the bridging join
key) are read straight off the filtered `dframe`, so they need no special
handling — only the last-dim group-code path bypasses the cache.

## What still defers (unchanged semantics)

OR predicates, cross-table-compound conjuncts, unknown columns, predicates on
a table not in the chain, and **dim predicates on an outer plan** (the kernel
null-pads at a LEFT stage, so dim-predicate folding is inner-only; fact
predicates apply to all join types). Full Q3 *still* defers — it also needs
multi-key `GROUP BY` + group-key-in-fact (separate PRs).

## Executor

`_aggregate`'s Filter branch now attempts `fused_join_aggregate` for
`Aggregate -> Filter -> Join` (the cross-table / OR shape that stays above the
join) before materialising; the common pushed-down case routes via the existing
non-Filter branch.

## De-risking

- **No C++/CUDA change** — `pass_pred` already runs in both join kernels; the
  dim HT build already reads `dframe`. Primary risk control.
- Dim-predicate folding is **inner-only** (`has_left or full_outer` guard).
- Empty filtered dim → `_empty_result` short-circuit (avoids a 0-capacity HT).
- Stacked `Filter -> Filter -> Scan` chains are folded from the top.

## Tests — `tests/test_join_hash_agg.py` (+10)

Fact / last-dim / fact+last-dim / middle-dim / fact+middle-dim / string-dim
predicates each fire + match DuckDB (parametrised); OR defer; LEFT-join dim
defer; dispatch-fires-with-filter (executor-module-patch gotcha). 1051 tests
green, ruff clean.

## Bench (SF=10)

| query | ryu warm | duckdb | warm x | check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q6_filter_agg | 25.6 | 63.4 | 2.48x | OK |
| four_table_join_agg | 76.4 | 469.0 | 6.13x | OK |
| **Q_join_where_filter** | **49.3** | **170.3** | **3.45x** | OK |
| Q3_shipping_priority | 112.6 | 158.8 | 1.41x | OK |
| Q_high_card_orderkey | 675.1 | 1231.2 | 1.82x | OK |
| Q_high_card_minmax | 1156.4 | 1034.0 | 0.89x | OK |

`Q_join_where_filter` (the `four_table_join_agg` shape + a cross-table WHERE)
now hits the fused path (was cuDF/deferred) at **3.45x** vs DuckDB. No
regression on the existing gates (DENSE join path unchanged).

author: bordenet
body:
## Summary
- A server registered in Claude Code's config but absent from Augment's (or vice versa) is easy to miss -- you configure an MCP server while working in one AI tool, forget the other needs a separate registration step, and only notice when a skill that depends on it behaves differently across the two agents.
- Adds `_doctor_mcp_parity_check()` to `tools/doctor-modules/mcp-checks.sh` (Check 31), called from the existing Check 28 entry point. Compares the full registered-name sets from Augment's `settings.json` and `claude mcp list`, warns (never blocks) on any name present in one but absent from the other.
- Inspired by a comparable check in a sibling private repo; the implementation is written fresh for this repo's own environment, not copied -- the sibling's version is tied to that org's own internal infrastructure with no equivalent here.

## Bug found and fixed along the way
Iterating `"${arr[@]}"` on an **empty** array under `set -u` (which `doctor-checks.sh` sets) is an unbound-variable error on bash <=4.3 -- confirmed to kill the *entire* doctor script against macOS's actual stock `/bin/bash` 3.2, even though the identical expansion is safe on bash 4.4+. This fires whenever exactly one side has zero registered servers (e.g. Claude CLI absent, only Augment configured) -- a common case. The regular bats suite never caught this because `bash -c` resolves to whatever newer bash is first on PATH, not the stock binary. Fixed by guarding each loop on non-empty array first. Added a regression test that pins to `/bin/bash` explicitly and verified it genuinely catches the bug (reverted to the pre-fix loop, confirmed the test fails; restored the fix).

Also caught and fixed: the new check was originally numbered "Check 30", colliding with `guardrails-checks.sh`'s existing Check 30. Renumbered to 31.

## Review
Two rounds of independent adversarial review (dispatched agents, not self-review):
- Round 1: found the bash-3.2 nounset crash and the Check 30 collision.
- Round 2: re-verified both fixes directly against real stock bash 3.2 on this machine, confirmed the diff contains no references to any private/internal organization's infrastructure (a hard requirement given this check was inspired by a private-repo equivalent).

`code-review-battery`: PASS, min-score 9.4.

## Test plan
- [x] `bats tests/mcp-checks-test.bats` -- 13/13 passed (6 new)
- [x] `bash tools/tests/test_doctor_checks.sh` -- 25/25 passed
- [x] Full local suite -- 606/606 bats tests passed
- [x] `shellcheck --shell=bash tools/doctor-modules/mcp-checks.sh` -- clean
- [x] Manually ran `sp-doctor.sh` end-to-end on a real machine and confirmed the new check fires correctly against real Augment/Claude Code configs
- [x] Verified the bash-3.2 crash fix directly against real stock `/bin/bash` 3.2 (not just Homebrew bash)

author: ydhekim
body:
Implements Epic Q (system design §20) — two independent "permanent additive bonus" pacing levers plus the grant capability for them.

## Q1 — Daily battle cap
- Characters can fight at most **5 battles/day** (UTC midnight boundary), extendable via a new `characters.bonus_daily_battles` column (`V12__Add_Account_Progression_Levers.sql`, the only schema change this epic needs).
- `AttackService.remainingDailyBattles(...)` is a **separate pre-check** (`BASE_DAILY_BATTLE_CAP + bonus − battlesToday`, floored at 0), counting every attempt via `BattleHistoryDao.countBattlesSince` (unfiltered by `won`). A failed bonus lookup falls back to bonus 0 rather than spuriously capping a player.
- `AttackRequestHandler` rejects with `AttackRejectedResponse(DAILY_BATTLE_CAP_REACHED)` between the ownership check and combat resolution. `attack()`'s signature and `AttackResponse`'s shape are **untouched**.
- The new `AttackRejectedResponse` packet is registered last in `KryoConfig` (positional/append-only) and sent by the server, but **not** wired into the client — the combat UI (M5) wires all combat packet consumers together, and `AttackResponse` itself still has no client consumer.

## Q2 — Character slots
- `CharacterService.createCharacter` now enforces the account's real `max_slots` (reusing the existing `accounts.max_slots` column, no new field) instead of an independent hardcoded `>= 3`, fixing a pre-existing display/enforcement mismatch (client was already shown `max_slots` but the check ignored it).

## Q3 — Grant paths (capability only)
- `AccountDao.addCharacterSlots` and `CharacterDao.addBonusDailyBattles` — atomic increments mirroring `addGlobalCurrency`. Unused by any caller yet, as scoped (build now, wire later).

## Tests
- New in-memory `FakeBattleHistoryDao`; `FakeCharacterDao` implements both new interface methods.
- All 7 `new AttackService(...)` call sites updated for the new `BattleHistoryDao` dependency.
- New `AttackServiceTest` cases (5 remaining when fresh; 0 after 5 today; yesterday's battles don't count) and a new `AttackRequestHandlerTest` case (5 prior battles → rejection, nothing new recorded).
- `BattleLeavesInventoryAloneTest` (story C2 guard) passes unchanged in its assertions — the new grant methods touch neither `inventory` nor `loadout`.

`gradlew.bat build` is green.

author: erseco
body:
## Summary

Closes #103 (also fixes the root cause of #102 for operators who use a `moodlehtml` volume).

When `/var/www/html` is a named volume, Docker only seeds it from the image on first use. Later image upgrades left the old PHP tree on the volume, so `AUTO_UPDATE_MOODLE` only ran `admin/cli/upgrade.php` against stale code.

### What changed

1. **Dockerfile**
   - Install Moodle into immutable `/usr/src/moodle`
   - Seed `/var/www/html` from that tree
   - Write `.alpine-moodle-release` (Moodle `$version` id)
   - Add `rsync`
   - Defaults: `SYNC_MOODLE_CODE=auto`, `EXTRA_PLUGIN_PATHS=`

2. **`010-sync-moodle-code.sh`** (runs before plugin install / configure)
   - `auto` — sync when the volume is empty or `$version` differs from the image
   - `always` / `never` overrides
   - Preserve `config.php` and `EXTRA_PLUGIN_PATHS`
   - `rsync -a --delete --checksum` so leftover core files are removed
   - Supports pre-5.1 (`version.php`) and 5.1+ (`public/version.php`)

3. **Docs** — persistence, upgrading, env vars, FAQ, README

4. **Tests**
   - `./tests/unit/test-sync-moodle-code.sh` — 7 docker-free cases (auto/always/never, preserve paths, public/ layout, path traversal reject)
   - `run_tests.sh sync` — in-container regression on a live install (wired into `tests/compose-test.sh`)

### Operator UX

```yaml
services:
  moodle:
    image: erseco/alpine-moodle:v5.0.2   # only change the tag
    volumes:
      - moodledata:/var/www/moodledata
      - moodlehtml:/var/www/html
    environment:
      SYNC_MOODLE_CODE: auto              # default
      EXTRA_PLUGIN_PATHS: "mod/attendance theme/space"
```

```bash
docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
# log: Moodle code sync: 2025041401.00 → 2025041402.00
```

Legacy “volume always wins”: `SYNC_MOODLE_CODE=never`.

## Test plan

- [x] `./tests/unit/test-sync-moodle-code.sh` — all 7 assertions pass
- [x] `./tests/compose-test.sh docker-compose.test.sqlite.yml` — HTTP + moosh + **sync** all pass on Moodle `main` (5.1+ `public/` layout)
- [ ] CI unit test step on PR
- [ ] Matrix / push smoke picks up the new `sync` mode via `compose-test.sh`

body:
这几个套件在 gcc-14/16 下无法建置（见 #9141）。gcc-14 起把数个旧式 C 写法从警告升为硬错误，gcc-16 又预设 `-std=gnu23`，这些老原始码因此编译失败。

- **games-roguelike/tsl (r3)**：C23 把 `true`/`false` 变成保留字，原始码自订的 `enum { false, true }` 被拒。沿用 ebuild 既有的 sed，额外注入 `-std=gnu17`（改回 C17 语意，写法合法、无警告）。
- **media-gfx/scangearmp (r1)**：同样的 C23 问题，Canon 标头 `typedef … bool`。以 `append-flags -std=gnu17` 处理。
- **net-print/epson-inkjet-printer_201207w (r1)**：gcc-14+ 把隐式函式宣告、void 函式带回传值升为错误。加 patch 从源头修：为 10 个呼叫 `debug_msg()` 的档补上其 `err.h` 宣告、并把 `debugt_msg()`（void）里多余的 `return 0;` 改成 `return;`。另补 `RPM_COMPRESS_TYPE="none"` 消掉 rpm eclass 的 QA 提示、移除已失效的 HOMEPAGE。

测试：三个都在建置机（gcc-16/glibc-2.43）以 `ebuild clean install` 实测，皆 `Completed installing` 且 elog 无 QA Notice（epson 只余 CUPS `ppd*` deprecated 与 `fread` unused-result 两类良性警告，不触发 QA gate）；`pkgcheck scan --commits --net` 干净。

## v0.2.0 — repository evolution (stabilize + evolve)

Full-repo evolution pass driven by three independent audits (engine/tests, UI/a11y/SEO, data/docs) plus the open P2 items from `docs/review-v0.1.md`. Every change is test-backed; the suite grew **325 → 382 tests** (21 files), with `svelte-check`, ESLint, Prettier and the Cloudflare build all green.

### Evolve (roadmap 0.2 subset)

- **Grid electricity region/year** — engine computes the input energy × cited factor as a `region_year_specific` **mass**, labeled with the factor's own metric (CO2 ≠ CO2e). Data-driven picker (options bar + inline on the emissions row), shareable `?region=&year=`, illustrative examples get CO2/CO2e chips. New sourced factor: **EU-27 2022 (292 gCO2/kWh, EEA)** — recorded in research-notes, now shipped; two EU years make the year-dependence visible.
- **`/api/convert` public API draft** — GET-only, CORS-open, publicly cacheable; framework-independent handler + thin Pages-Function wrapper; structured 400s; documented in `docs/api.md`; 11 handler tests.
- **Result export** — copy JSON, download JSON/CSV (every row keeps exactness + source refs), API deep link.
- **Time result group** — `2 h` gets real time conversions instead of landing under “Energy”.
- **SEO** — prerendered `/sitemap.xml` (116 URLs), OG/Twitter card (`static/og.png` + generator script), `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD breadcrumbs, short unit slugs (`/units/kwh` → 308 → canonical).

### Stabilize (audit findings)

- **Honest ranges (P0)**: ranged heating values used to render raw, *unconverted* low–high bounds identically on MJ/kWh/GJ/BTU rows, bypassing `formatRange`. Now ranges are converted per display unit; spreads >25% (lignite, anthracite) are labeled `estimated` (`~`, 3 sig figs). Rulebook §C.7 updated.
- **Engine**: `region:"global"` no longer mislabeled `region_year_specific`; factor `uncertainty` + `source_table_or_page` surface on results; `maxSigFigs` clamped and threaded to mass/volume rows; unusable `time` falls back to the context prompt; parser accepts `.5 kWh`, tolerates `5. kWh`, rejects >200-char and 10^±30 inputs (`unsupported_value`); lazy did-you-mean suggestions (CPU-amplification guard); dead code removed; data validation enforces positive values and well-formed ranges.
- **UI/a11y**: combobox APG keyboard fixes; radiogroup pattern for LHV/HHV; mobile menu overlays (no reflow); Escape closes popover/menu; WCAG-AA `--text-faint`; distinct critical warnings; “context required” vs “not available” headers; theme-color follows the active theme, no toggle flash; fuel picks materialize into the query text (shareable URLs); no duplicate conversion/`replaceState` on deep links.
- **Compliance**: footer carries the OGL v3.0 attribution required by `docs/sources.md`; version read from `package.json`.
- **Infra**: GitHub Actions CI (lint/check/test/build), Node pinned (`.nvmrc` 22, `engines >=20`).

### Deliberately not done (with reasons)

- **US grid factor** — research-notes flags ~370 gCO2/kWh as provisional/unverified; shipping it would violate no-invented-numbers. Needs EPA Hub Table 6 XLSX re-extraction (tracked in roadmap + sources.md).
- **More fuels / Source Diff Viewer** — DESNZ variant rows are recorded verbatim, but shipping near-duplicate fuel ids without a variant/compare data model risks catalog confusion; blocked on a fuel-variants ADR (roadmap).
- **Import half of import/export, advanced search, natural-gas models** — unscoped/new-data work, listed honestly in the roadmap.

### Verification

- `npm test` 382/382 · `svelte-check` 0 errors/0 warnings · ESLint + Prettier clean · `vite build` (Cloudflare adapter) ✔
- Browser-verified on the dev server: region/year flow end-to-end (`~0.177 kg CO2e` for 1 kWh UK 2025), converted lignite ranges, `/units/kwh` redirect, export toolbar, sitemap in build output, zero console errors.

author: armaxri
body:
## Summary

Adds a SHA-256 integrity check for the bundled `termihub-rdp-helper` sidecar, mirroring the agent-binary checksum verification. Before `SidecarRdp` spawns the resolved helper, it verifies the binary against a known-good digest **embedded at build time**; a tampered, corrupted, or wrong-architecture helper fails the connection with an actionable error instead of being executed.

Closes #1762. Follow-up to #1754 (which bundled the sidecar via Tauri `externalBin` and deferred this optional check).

## Mechanism

- **`core/build.rs` (new)** hashes the staged `externalBin` (`src-tauri/binaries/termihub-rdp-helper-<target>[.exe]`) — the exact bytes Tauri bundles — and emits its SHA-256 as the `TERMIHUB_RDP_HELPER_SHA256` compile-time env var (also honoring an explicit `TERMIHUB_RDP_HELPER_SHA256` override). It never fails the build.
- **`core/src/backends/rdp_sidecar/integrity.rs` (new)** reads that digest via `option_env!` and verifies the resolved binary's SHA-256 before spawn.
- **`SidecarRdp::connect`** calls the verifier before launching the child; a mismatch returns `SpawnFailed` with both digests named.
- **Self-contained across platforms:** `release.yml` / `dev-build.yml` already build+stage one target per matrix leg before `tauri build`, so each platform's app embeds its own helper's digest with no workflow changes.

## Skip paths (mirroring the agent path's tolerance)

- `$TERMIHUB_RDP_HELPER` override set (dev/test) → skipped.
- No digest embedded (per-PR compile/test jobs and plain dev builds never stage the sidecar) → skipped with a warning; integrity cannot be verified but the connection proceeds.

## Tests

- 7 unit tests in `integrity.rs`: known SHA-256 vector, lowercase-hex shape, matching digest accepts (case-insensitive), mismatch rejects with a clear error, missing/empty digest skips, override skips.
- Verified locally end-to-end: staged a helper, confirmed `build.rs` embeds its digest into the compiled artifact, and that removing it re-embeds nothing. `./scripts/check.sh` green (fmt, clippy workspace-wide, eslint, markdownlint).

## Notes

- The build scripts (`build-rdp-sidecar.{sh,cmd}`) additionally write a `.sha256` sidecar next to the staged binary and print the digest, purely for transparency/local verification — the runtime check uses the embedded const, not that file.

author: superhighfives
body:
Points this repo at the reusable workflow in [superhighfives/control-room](https://github.com/superhighfives/control-room), matching nylon-impossible, nowhere-forever and records.

### Why

On [#242](https://github.com/superhighfives/pika/pull/242) the review check went green having posted nothing. The log shows the plugin ran normally in agent mode for ~43s and exited clean — its step-1 eligibility check declined to review, most likely because the head branch is `claude/*` and it treats those as automated. Without `show_full_output` there's no way to confirm which criterion fired.

The plugin also discards any finding below 80 confidence and excludes pre-existing issues, likely-intentional changes, test coverage, and general code quality.

(The `--comment` flag in the old workflow was inert — the plugin command always posts a single summary and never parses it.)

### Swift support

`BASELINE.md` in control-room was written in TypeScript syntax, so on a Swift repo most rules didn't apply. It's now language-agnostic, with [`languages/swift.md`](https://github.com/superhighfives/control-room/blob/main/languages/swift.md) sharpening it into local forms: force-unwrap and `as!` as the "silence the compiler" escape hatch, `try!`, main-actor violations for UI state, and retain cycles in escaping closures.

### macOS runner

Runs on `macos-latest` with `runtime: none`, since the Swift toolchain is already there — `setup_command` only selects Xcode. `verify_commands` runs `build-for-testing`, mirroring [tests.yml](.github/workflows/tests.yml) but without the suite, which that workflow already covers. `timeout_minutes` raised to 30 for the build.

That means the reviewer compiles the project. On #242 that would have surfaced the exit-65 build failure as part of the review rather than only in a separate red check.

### Note

This PR edits `.github/workflows/`, so it can't review itself — the action requires the workflow file to match the default branch. Expect a comment from control-room explaining that rather than silence; it'll be the first live exercise of that fallback.

body:
## Summary
- Each `ArmorLayer` now embeds its own `ArmorLayerDesignState` instead of sharing a ship-wide, index-locked `Armor.layerDesigns` array, allowing heterogeneous layer stacks per plate — the enabler for future plate swapping (a replacement plate may carry a different layer composition than the one ejected).
- `maxHealth` moves off the runtime `ArmorLayer` onto its design (`plateMaxHealth`), exposed via a getter.
- `walkArmorLayers` (damage-manager.ts) now walks each plate in the hit arc **independently and exclusively**: a plate's own resistance depends only on its own layer health (never an average across sibling plates). Each plate takes only its own **relative share of the hit**, proportional to how much of the *hit's own* angular width lands on that specific plate (`Armor.plateHitOverlaps()`) — a hit spread across several plates divides its damage among them; a hit that lands entirely within one plate (a direct hit) gives that plate the full amount. The only remaining cross-plate state is the single reactive-cell-pop budget per hit, matching the existing documented interim Reactive simplification.

Design context: `starwards-design/product/decision-notes-2026-07-20.md` items 1–2 (per-plate design; designs must carry layer type for a future Engineer-station display). Reactive armor full implementation stays out of scope (#1970) — existing `singleUsePlates` behavior preserved.

body: ## Summary Follow-up to #1: cards stop nagging about things the user already handled (replies AND calendar RSVPs), actionable email can be handed off to their EA in one tap, and Gemini quota exhaustion fails over to a second credit pool. ### Already-replied detection - New step 0 in the triage precedence chain: if the user's last reply on a thread is **newer** than the incoming message, it triages as "Handled — you replied. Archive it." instead of `respond`. A follow-up that arrives *after* their reply still triages normally - Signals: the sent-folder scan builds a `threadId → last sent time` map, plus a Redis-backed `replied-threads` store records the thread the instant the user hits Send in Seer - **Reply = handled**: sending a reply from Seer also archives the original message ### Calendar invites as native actions — any invitation - **Answered invites auto-archive**: invite emails match against a **365-day** calendar window (paginated, up to 500 events, both providers) including the user's own `responseStatus`. If they already responded — in Gmail, Google Calendar, or Seer — the card flips to "Handled — RSVP is on your calendar. Archive it." - **Exact resolution in the reader**: the `.ics` part inside the email is parsed for its `iCalUID` and looked up live against the Calendar API — any invitation resolves regardless of date or subject format, with zero cache lag; subject matching is the fallback - **Fresh RSVP state**: calendar events refresh on a 5-minute clock (contacts stay on 6h) so answers given in Gmail/Calendar flip Seer cards on the next load - **One-tap RSVP in Seer**: unanswered invites triage as `act_today` with a Going / Maybe / Can't-go bar in the reader. `/api/calendar/rsvp` patches the attendee response (`sendUpdates=all`), write-through-updates the cached context, and archives the invite email - Organizer-side receipts ("Accepted: Standup @ …") triage as delete - Scope change: Google `calendar.events.readonly` → `calendar.events` (write needed for RSVP; **requires one re-sign-in**) ### EA delegation - Triage prompt (v10): tasks that don't need the user personally get instructions starting with **"Delegate:"** and the exact ask, informed by the user's profile (which names their EA) - **"Delegate to EA" button** in the reader: Gemini drafts a forwarding note with the task, key facts, and what to report back; `SEER_EA_EMAIL` pre-fills the recipient ### Quota-aware Gemini with gateway failover - **Shared KV cooldown on 429s**: per-minute limits honor Google's `retryDelay`, daily limits sleep until the Pacific-midnight reset; status line shows the reason and remaining minutes - **Vercel AI Gateway failover**: while the direct key cools down, triage batches and reply drafts route through the AI Gateway's monthly included credits (verified live against `google/gemini-2.5-flash`) - **40-email batches** (was 25) and `maxRetries: 0` to stretch free-tier request quotas ### Plumbing - `GeminiTriageItem` carries `threadId` + `receivedAt`; all four triage routes pass them - Draft endpoint returns a `mode` (`reply` | `forward`); message endpoint returns a matched `calendarEvent` (id, subject, start, myStatus) for invite emails - Also merges the parallel Seer-branding work (Proxima Nova fonts, guideline palette, circle logo) Deployed to production; `/api/calendar/rsvp` verified serving.

body:
💡 What: Replaced `len(User.objects.filter(email=pec.new_email)) != 0` with `User.objects.filter(email=pec.new_email).exists()`.
🎯 Why: Using `len()` on a QuerySet forces the database to evaluate the entire query and load all matching records into memory, which is a severe performance anti-pattern. `.exists()` uses an efficient database-level `LIMIT 1` check without loading objects.
📊 Impact: Reduces memory usage and database load, especially if multiple matching records existed, but even for single checks it avoids fetching the entire row.
🔬 Measurement: Profile the database queries before and after to observe the difference between `SELECT *` and `SELECT 1` with a `LIMIT 1` clause.
